informal.PackingBounds.FullMain.exact_binary_expo: The base-two logarithm of the unrestricted linear-program bound, divided by dimension, converges to -1/2 log_2(2 pi / e).
informal.PackingBounds.PackingBridge.sphere_packi: There is a vanishing error sequence such that, in every positive dimension, sphere-packing density is at most (sqrt(e / (2 pi)) plus that error) to the dimension.
informal.PackingBounds.sharpFullCohnElkiesManuscr: Packages the complete sharp asymptotic conclusions for the unrestricted program, including quotient-root, natural-logarithmic, and base-two limits, vanishing-error formulas, a universal bound for all admissible functions, and a certified decimal exponent interval.

records.title: Stafford 3.8
records.abstract: Lean formalization of Stafford's Conjecture 3.8 for every characteristic-zero field and every Weyl-algebra rank, proving that each nonzero d admits F, R, and S with 1 = d*R + F*d*S. The development also proves an exact Bernstein-degree fixed-source strengthening and derived localization, adjoint, and evolutionary results.

informal.Stafford38.universalStatement: For every characteristic-zero field, every Weyl algebra rank, and every nonzero d, there are F, R, S with 1 = d*R + F*d*S.
informal.Stafford38.universalFixedSourceStatement: The stated fixed-source strengthening holds with its exact Bernstein-degree bound.

records.title: Verified Stallings folding for finitely generated subgroups of F2
records.abstract: Constructs a finite inverse automaton recognizing the subgroup generated by any finite list of signed words in the rank-two free group. Proves exact subgroup preservation and correctness of canonical reduced-word membership testing. Reusable infrastructure includes inverse-automaton walks, reduction-compatible traversal, finite fold congruences, coset potentials, flower graphs, and basis roses. Folding uses exhaustive finite search over Boolean relations; no complexity bound, core pruning, subgroup basis, intersection, or index algorithm is claimed.

informal.Stallings.folded_recognizer_exists: For every finite list S of signed words on two generators, there exist a finite type of states, a base state, and a partial transition table with inverse-labelled reverse edges, such that traversing the canonical reduced word of any g in FreeGroup (Fin 2) returns to the base exactly when g lies in the subgroup generated by the word values in S. The witness is the computed flower-graph fold.
informal.Stallings.foldWords_loopSubgroup_eq_gene: For every finite input list of signed words in the rank-two free group, the based-loop subgroup of the computed folded flower graph equals the subgroup generated by the input words.
informal.Stallings.foldedMembershipTest_eq_true_i: For any finite generating list S and any rank-two free-group element g, the executable folded-automaton test returns true if and only if g belongs to the subgroup generated by S. There is no efficiency guarantee for constructing the automaton.

records.title: Monotonicity Formula for Stationary Harmonic Maps
records.abstract: Formalizes the monotonicity formula for stationary `W^{1,2}_{loc}` maps with Euclidean target. The proof is target independent: it uses only the displayed weak gradient and a vanishing domain first variation, so no target-manifold structure enters the argument. From a bundled stationary Sobolev witness `StationaryW12LocMap u Omega` it proves, for `0 < s <= r < R0`, that the normalized energy `Theta(Du, a, rho) = rho^(2-n) * integral over B(a, rho) of |Du|^2` is monotone: `weakTheta Du a s <= weakTheta Du a r`, together with the exact increment formula `weakTheta Du a r - weakTheta Du a s = weakMonotonicityRhs Du a s r`. The Sobolev layer is project-defined from Mathlib's `MemLp`, weak-derivative identities, Bochner integration, and Euclidean measure theory, following the De Giorgi-Nash-Moser engineering choice; the internal proof routes through a radial vector-field first variation, a coarea/Radon-Nikodym radius representation, smooth radial cutoffs, and an absolute-continuity boundary step.

informal.LeanStationaryHarmonicMaps.StationaryHar: The public input package: a domain-variation stationary `W^{1,2}_{loc}` Sobolev map bundling a chosen weak gradient (`W12LocMapWitness`) with the vanishing domain first-variation identity. This is the object users construct to invoke the monotonicity theorem.

Witness-style monotonicity: from a stationary `W^{1,2}_{loc}` map package, the normalized weak energy `weakTheta` is monotone in the radius, `weakTheta Du a s <= weakTheta Du a r` for `0 < s <= r < R0`.

Witness-style monotonicity formula: the increment of `weakTheta` equals the nonnegative annular radial-energy term, `weakTheta Du a r - weakTheta Du a s = weakMonotonicityRhs Du a s r` for `0 < s < r < R0`.

Componentwise convenience wrapper: the same monotonicity inequality stated directly from the local `L^2`, measurability, weak-gradient, and first-variation hypotheses, without first constructing the witness package.

records.title: Split, cograph and threshold graph structures
records.abstract: Connects split partitions, cotrees and threshold creation sequences on Mathlib SimpleGraph. Proves the finite forbidden-induced-subgraph characterizations, split iff chordal and co-chordal, and completeness of cotrees and creation sequences. Supplies certificate-preserving operations, twins and nonempty union/join decompositions for cographs, maximum-clique split partitions, and induced/isomorphic transport of existing chordal elimination orders and clique trees. Classical graph theory is formalized; no new mathematical theorem, canonical certificate or recognition-time bound is claimed.

informal.SimpleGraph.isSplit_iff_forbidden_induce: A finite graph is split iff it contains no induced 2K2, C4 or C5.
informal.SimpleGraph.isSplit_iff_isChordal_and_co: A finite graph is split iff both it and its complement are chordal.
informal.SimpleGraph.isCograph_iff_nonempty_cotre: A finite graph is P4-free iff it is isomorphic to the graph of a cotree, whose constructors are empty, singleton, disjoint union and join.
informal.SimpleGraph.isThreshold_iff_isSplit_and_: A graph has a split partition with nested independent-side neighbourhoods iff it is both split and P4-free. No finiteness is required.
informal.SimpleGraph.isThreshold_iff_forbidden_in: A finite graph is threshold iff it contains no induced 2K2, C4 or P4.
informal.SimpleGraph.isThreshold_iff_nonempty_cre: A finite graph is threshold iff it is isomorphic to a graph constructed from the empty graph by successively adding an isolated or universal vertex.
informal.SimpleGraph.IsCograph.exists_twins: A finite cograph with at least two vertices has two distinct vertices with identical adjacency outside their pair, whether adjacent or not.
informal.SimpleGraph.IsCograph.exists_union_root: A finite cograph that is not preconnected admits a cotree representation with a union root and two nonempty children. This is an existence claim, not a claim about every unreduced cotree.
informal.SimpleGraph.IsCograph.exists_join_root: A preconnected finite cograph with at least two vertices admits a cotree representation with a join root and two nonempty children.
informal.SimpleGraph.IsSplit.exists_partition_wit: Every finite split graph admits a split partition whose clique part has maximum cardinality. Such a partition need not be unique.

records.title: The optimal exponent relating sumsets and difference sets
records.abstract: For a finite integer set A with at least two elements, proves that C(A) = log(|A+A|/|A|) / log(|A-A|/|A|) is strictly below 2, while explicit finite sets have exponents tending to 2. Thus 2 is the supremum and is never attained. Also gives an explicit witness within 10^(-999) of 2. This imports the upstream base-39 row-and-column variant, not the paper's base-12 automaton construction or its quantitative cardinality estimates. Supporting infrastructure includes injective digit expansions and the strict Pluennecke-Petridis equality argument for finite integer sets.

informal.SumDifferenceExponent.growthExponent_lt_: For every finite set A of integers with at least two elements, log(|A+A|/|A|) / log(|A-A|/|A|) is strictly less than 2.
informal.SumDifferenceExponent.tendsto_growthExpo: The growth exponents of the explicit finite integer sets approximatingSet l converge to 2 as l tends to infinity; these sets have at least two elements whenever l is positive.
informal.SumDifferenceExponent.isLUB_admissibleEx: The number 2 is the least upper bound of the growth exponents of all finite integer sets with at least two elements.
informal.SumDifferenceExponent.sSup_admissibleExp: The supremum of the growth exponents of all finite integer sets with at least two elements equals 2.
informal.SumDifferenceExponent.supremum_not_attai: No finite integer set with at least two elements has growth exponent equal to 2.
informal.SumDifferenceExponent.quantitative_examp: The explicitly defined finite integer set quantitativeSet has growth exponent strictly between 2 - 10^(-999) and 2.

records.title: Sums of Three Squares
records.abstract: Formalizes a blueprint step in the three-squares theorem using quadratic forms and geometry of numbers.

informal.LeanPool.SumsThreeSquares.blueprint_case: Proves the mod-8-equals-3 blueprint case for the three-squares theorem.

records.title: Sundog certificates
records.abstract: A referee-free, axiom-clean Lean development of coding-theory certificates: syndrome decoding soundness and lossiness bounds for GF(2) parity-check schemes (with a Reed–Solomon evaluation-dual variant), and a fully machine-checked correctness proof of the Karp reduction chain 3SAT ≤ 3DM ≤ X3C ≤ bounded-weight syndrome decoding. Only the logical iff of each reduction is formalized; polynomial-time bounds, NP classes, and Cook–Levin are unformalized external inputs, so NP-hardness of decoding is conditional on those standard facts.

informal.Sundog.SATReductionMain.sat_iff_decodes: The end-to-end reduction correctness: a formula is satisfiable iff its image under the composed 3SAT-to-decoding reduction is a yes-instance of bounded-weight syndrome decoding.
informal.Sundog.MatchingNPHard.threeDM_iff_X3C: The 3-dimensional matching instance has a perfect matching iff the reduced exact-cover-by-3-sets instance has an exact cover, both directions machine-checked.
informal.Sundog.Certificate.accept_sound: Soundness of the cheap syndrome-decoding verifier when it accepts: an exhibited light same-syndrome witness certifies the body is safe within the decoding radius.
informal.Sundog.Certificate.reject_sound: Soundness of the verifier when it rejects: a sound column-weight lower bound on the minimum same-syndrome weight rules out every light witness, so the body is genuinely unsafe.

records.title: Synthetic Euclidean geometry: Euclid's Elements Book I
records.abstract: Formalizes Book I of Euclid's Elements via an axiomatic synthetic-geometry system (incidence, betweenness, congruence, and area), culminating in the Pythagorean theorem and its converse.

informal.SyntheticEuclid4.IncidenceGeometry: The axiomatic class of synthetic Euclidean geometry, bundling points, lines, circles, and the incidence, betweenness, congruence, and area primitives with Euclid's axioms.
informal.SyntheticEuclid4.square_of_len: Constructs a square on a given segment off a given line.
informal.SyntheticEuclid4.pythagoras_construct: Constructs the three squares and parallelograms on the sides of a triangle used in the proof of the Pythagorean theorem.
informal.SyntheticEuclid4.pythagoras: Euclid I.47, the Pythagorean theorem, that the square on the hypotenuse of a right triangle equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.
informal.SyntheticEuclid4.pythagoras_converse: Euclid I.48, the converse of the Pythagorean theorem, that a triangle whose square areas satisfy the Pythagorean relation has a right angle.

records.title: The Three-Gap (Steinhaus) Theorem
records.abstract: Formalizes the three-gap (Steinhaus, three-distance) theorem: for every real `a` and every `N`, the `N`-point orbit `{i·a mod 1 : i < N}` partitions `[0,1)` into gaps taking at most three distinct lengths, and when exactly three occur the largest is the sum of the other two. The proof works in `[0,1)` via `Int.fract` (not `AddCircle`) through the two first-return times `η⁺` and `η⁻`, and is uniform in the rotation number, covering rational and irrational `a` with no case split.

informal.SteinhausThreeGap.three_gap_card_le_thre: For every real `a` and natural `N`, the gaps of the orbit `{i·a mod 1 : i < N}` take at most three distinct lengths.
informal.SteinhausThreeGap.three_gap_lengths_eq: When the gaps take exactly three distinct lengths, those lengths are precisely the two first returns `η⁺`, `η⁻`, and their sum `η⁺ + η⁻`; in particular the largest gap is the sum of the other two.

records.title: Turán's theorem (the "Book" weighting proof)
records.abstract: Formalizes the weighting/optimization proof of Turán's theorem from Proofs from THE BOOK, bounding the number of edges of a p-clique-free simple graph by (1/2)(1 - 1/(p-1)) n².

informal.Turan3.turans: Turán's theorem — a p-clique-free simple graph on n vertices has at most (1/2)(1 - 1/(p-1)) n² edges.
informal.Turan3.finale_bound: For any weight distribution on a p-clique-free graph, the total edge weight is at most ((p-1)(p-2)/2)·(1/(p-1))², the bound used to derive the edge count.
informal.Turan3.Better_forms_clique: Starting from any weight function, the minimal-support weight-non-decreasing improvement has support that forms a clique.
informal.Turan3.Enhance_total_weight_stricinc: Equalizing weights between a maximum- and minimum-weight vertex in the clique support strictly increases the total edge weight.

records.title: Tutte’s path theorem for matroids
records.abstract: Proves the modular-cut path theorem for finite matroids, with reusable rank-partition, hyperplane-separation, relative-complement, indecomposable-cover, and diamond constructions.

informal.TutteFormalization.path_theorem: In a finite connected matroid, any two hyperplanes containing a proper indecomposable flat and lying outside a modular cut are joined by a finite Tutte path all of whose vertices contain that flat and avoid the cut. Consecutive vertices are distinct hyperplanes with indecomposable corank-two intersection; repeated nonconsecutive vertices are permitted.
informal.TutteFormalization.path_theorem_of_indec: In any finite matroid, two hyperplanes containing an indecomposable flat F and lying outside a modular cut are joined by a Tutte path whose vertices contain F and avoid the cut. This strengthens the cited path theorem by requiring only connectedness of the contraction by F; properness of F follows from containment in an endpoint hyperplane.
informal.TutteFormalization.exists_indecomposable: If an indecomposable flat S and a flat U span the ground, every indecomposable flat T contained in both extends inside S to an indecomposable flat R spanning the ground with U, with corank R equal to rank U minus rank T.
informal.TutteFormalization.exists_relative_compl: For nested flats T contained in S, there is a flat U containing T whose intersection with S is T, whose join with S is the ground, and whose corank equals rank S minus rank T.

records.title: Ulm's theorem for countable reduced abelian p-groups
records.abstract: Formalizes Ulm's classification theorem for countable reduced abelian p-groups in arbitrary Lean universes. The development constructs the transfinite Ulm filtration and invariants, proves their invariance under additive equivalence, establishes Kaplansky's one-generator extension lemma, and completes the countable back-and-forth classification. A finite-group regression distinguishes Z/4 x Z/4 from Z/2 x Z/8 at the zeroth Ulm invariant.

informal.UlmsTheorem.ulm_theorem: For any prime p and any two countable reduced abelian p-groups in the same arbitrary Lean universe, the groups are additively isomorphic if and only if all of their classical Ulm invariants, indexed by universe-zero ordinals, agree.
informal.UlmsTheorem.iso_of_ulm_invariants: Equal Ulm invariants at every universe-zero ordinal imply an additive equivalence between countable reduced abelian p-groups, via finite height-preserving partial isomorphisms and a back-and-forth limit.
informal.UlmsTheorem.ulmInvariant_iso_invariant: An additive equivalence preserves every classical Ulm invariant.
informal.UlmsTheorem.UlmDifferentialRegression.no: The groups Z/4 x Z/4 and Z/2 x Z/8 are not additively isomorphic; the proof exercises the classification theorem and independently detects their different zeroth Ulm invariants.

records.title: Unconditional Schauder Bases
records.abstract: Develops an API for Schauder bases and unconditional Schauder bases of complete normed spaces, including ordered partial-sum convergence, rearrangement criteria for unconditionality, and an arbitrary-index variant built on unconditional summability, then proves a finite sign criterion: a family with dense closed span, nonzero vectors, and a uniform finite sign bound is the basis of an unconditional Schauder basis.

informal.UnconditionalCriterion.exists_unconditio: Finite sign criterion for sequences: if `x : ℕ → E` has dense closed linear span, every `x n` is nonzero, and finite sign changes are uniformly bounded by `C`, then `x` is the basis sequence of an unconditional Schauder basis.

Abstract-index form of the finite sign criterion: under the same dense span, nonzero, and uniform finite sign bound hypotheses for an arbitrarily indexed family, there is an abstractly indexed unconditional Schauder basis whose basis family is exactly `x`.

records.title: Virasoro Project
records.abstract: Formalizes the Virasoro algebra, its Witt-algebra central extension, Verma modules, and the basic bosonic Sugawara construction.

informal.VirasoroProject.VirasoroAlgebra: Defines the Virasoro algebra as a one-dimensional central extension of the Witt algebra.
informal.VirasoroProject.sugawaraRepresentation: Constructs the basic bosonic Sugawara representation of the Virasoro algebra from locally truncated Heisenberg actions.

records.title: Viscosity solutions, Aleksandrov differentiability and harmonic Dirichlet problems
records.abstract: Develops second-order semijets, smooth test-function equivalence, Jensen contact sets, convex Aleksandrov differentiability, the quadratic-penalty Ishii lemma and compact-domain comparison for degenerate elliptic equations. Perron assembly retains explicit comparison, barrier and bumping assumptions; these are discharged for classical harmonic Dirichlet existence on bounded open domains satisfying a uniform exterior sphere condition.

informal.AleksandrovDifferentiability.convexAleks: A convex real-valued function on an open subset of any finite-dimensional real inner product space is second-order differentiable at Lebesgue-almost every point.
informal.ViscositySolns.JensenContactSetPositiveM: Under the localized semiconvexity and strict-contact hypotheses, the contact set arising from sufficiently small linear perturbations has positive Lebesgue measure.
informal.ViscositySolns.QuadraticPenaltyIshiiLemm: For an upper semicontinuous function and a lower semicontinuous function on locally compact subsets of real coordinate space, doubled-variable maxima with the quadratic penalty yield closed semijets satisfying the Ishii block-matrix bounds.
informal.ViscositySolns.comparison_of_constantShi: A viscosity subsolution lies below a supersolution on a nonempty locally compact domain with compact closure, assuming boundary comparison, semicontinuity on the closure, properness, operator continuity, the Ishii structural condition and uniform scalar decrease.
informal.ViscositySolns.viscositySubsolution_iff_: On an open domain, semijet and smooth C² test-function formulations of viscosity subsolutions agree for Hessian-continuous, symmetric-part-invariant operators.
informal.ViscositySolns.dirichlet_harmonic_modulu: On a bounded open subset of finite-dimensional Euclidean space with a uniform exterior sphere condition, Lipschitz data on its closure admit a continuous extension that agrees on the boundary and is C² and harmonic in the domain, with a boundary modulus depending only on the domain and Lipschitz constant.

records.title: Vizing's theorem and equitable edge colourings
records.abstract: Proves the maximum-degree-plus-one edge-colouring bound for finite simple graphs by fans and Kempe exchanges. A separate component-swapping argument equitably rebalances any finite proper edge colouring on its original palette. Together they give equitable proper edge colourings on any palette of at least maximum degree plus one colours, with every class bounded by the ceiling of the average class size. Extracted from the published Paper IV formalization; these are classical colouring results, not a claim to new mathematics or to the paper's clique-partition bound.

informal.LeanPool.Vizing.lineGraph_colorable: The line graph of a finite simple graph G is colourable with maximum degree of G plus one colours.
informal.SimpleGraph.lineGraph_chromaticNumber_le: The chromatic number of the line graph of a finite simple graph G is at most maximum degree of G plus one.
informal.LeanPool.Vizing.Equitable.exists_equitab: Every proper edge colouring of a finite simple graph with a finite palette admits a proper recolouring on the same palette in which any two colour classes differ in size by at most one.
informal.LeanPool.Vizing.exists_equitable_edge_co: For every finite simple graph G and natural c at least maximum degree of G plus one, there is an equitable proper edge colouring with c colours; each colour class has at most ceiling(|E(G)|/c) edges.

records.title: Mean-field derivation and well-posedness of the Vlasov equation
records.abstract: Formalizes the mean-field limit, Dobrushin stability, and forward-in-time well-posedness for the Vlasov equation via Wasserstein-1 optimal transport.

informal.Vlasov.vlasovWellPosedness: Forward-in-time existence of a Lagrangian solution to the Vlasov equation on any finite horizon, for interaction forces that are Lipschitz gradients of an even pair potential (class AssW) — with no smallness restriction on the Lipschitz constant.
informal.Vlasov.dobrushin: A Wasserstein-1 form of Dobrushin's 1979 stability estimate (the original uses a truncated metric) - two Lagrangian Vlasov solutions with finite first moments at every time separate at most at an exponential Gronwall rate.
informal.Vlasov.meanFieldLimit: Conditional mean-field limit - given Wasserstein-1 convergence of the initial empirical data and a uniform Dobrushin stability estimate for the empirical curves, the N-particle empirical measures converge to the Vlasov solution uniformly on any finite horizon.
informal.Vlasov.weak_isLagrangianVlasovSolutionOn: On a time window with L * T^2 < 1, a weak solution with the standing regularity (even C^2 pair potential AssW2, finite first moments, narrow continuity, time-continuity of the convolution force at each point, continuity of the convolution-derivative field, and a uniform spatial first-moment bound on the window) is Lagrangian - the pushforward of its initial datum along the characteristic flow.

records.title: The Wallace problem in ZFC
records.abstract: Formalizes in ZFC a Hausdorff countably compact group topology without nontrivial convergent sequences on every torsion-free Abelian group of cardinality continuum. It specializes the construction to the rational direct sum and the additive real group, and derives a commutative Tychonoff countably compact cancellative semigroup that is not a group.

informal.Wallace.torsionFreeAbelianGroup_mainTheo: Every torsion-free Abelian group of cardinality continuum admits a Hausdorff countably compact group topology with no nontrivial convergent sequences.
informal.Wallace.continuumRationalGroup_and_real_: Both the continuum-indexed rational direct sum and the additive group of real numbers admit such Hausdorff countably compact group topologies without nontrivial convergent sequences.
informal.Wallace.commutativeTychonoffWallaceCount: There exists a commutative Tychonoff countably compact topological semigroup with two-sided cancellation which is not a group.

records.title: Whitehead's theorem for CW-complexes
records.abstract: Formalizes Whitehead's theorem — a continuous map between CW-complexes that induces isomorphisms on all homotopy groups is a homotopy equivalence — including the supporting theory of CW-complexes, relative homotopy groups, the homotopy extension property, and compression of maps.

informal.WhiteheadTheorem: Proves that a continuous map between CW-complexes inducing isomorphisms on all homotopy groups is a homotopy equivalence.

records.title: Irrationality of the Riemann zeta function at five
records.abstract: Proves that Mathlib's Riemann zeta function at five is an irrational real number, following Aabir Fauzan's September 2026 preprint. Constructs integer polynomials of degree 37n with positive values at zeta(5) that decay exponentially in n squared. Includes a general integer-polynomial irrationality criterion, Hankel determinant and moment-integral identities, logarithmic-energy estimates, prime-adic integrality bounds, and kernel-checked rational certificates. The formalization uses a different normalizer and a positive decay constant in place of the paper's specific constant 139/5. Reuses the prime number theorem infrastructure already in the MooreBound project.

informal.Zeta5Irrational.irrational_five: There exists an irrational real number x whose complex coercion equals Mathlib's Riemann zeta function evaluated at five.
informal.Zeta5Irrational.main_estimate: There is a positive real c such that, for all sufficiently large n, an integer polynomial Q of degree 37n is a positive rational multiple of the constructed determinant polynomial and satisfies 0 < Q(zeta(5)) < exp(-c*n^2).
informal.Zeta5Irrational.irrational_of_eventually: A real xi is irrational if, eventually, integer polynomials of degree at most d(n) have positive values at xi bounded by epsilon(n), and b^d(n)*epsilon(n) tends to zero for every positive natural b.

records.title: Thakur's hypotheses on power sums of F_q[t]
records.abstract: Formalizes four components of Thakur's hypotheses on power sums over finite polynomial rings, including uniqueness and monotonicity results for the carry-free digit optimization problems and the Laurent-series expansion of finite-field power sums.

informal.ZetaH123.H1.main_theorem: Proves uniqueness of the admissible base-q decomposition maximizing the H1 power-sum weight functional.
informal.ZetaH123.H2.main: Proves the H2 unique-minimizer statement for the recursive digit/carry-free optimization problem defining the values s_d(k).
informal.ZetaH123.H3.main_theorem: Proves the H3 monotonicity statement that s_d(k) is strictly less than s_d(k+1) when p does not divide k.
informal.ZetaH123.Lem41.main: Proves the Lemma 4.1 Laurent-series expansion for S_d(k), with nonzero coefficients indexed by the carry-free tuples.

records.title: Simple zeros of the Riemann zeta function
records.abstract: Formalizes Lamzouri's Hilbert-space proof of lower bounds for simple and distinct zeros of the Riemann zeta function. From explicit Riemann--von Mangoldt and unconditional pair-correlation hypotheses, the development proves that eventually more than 67.25% of nontrivial zeros are simple and on the critical line and more than 83.625% are distinct. It includes the finite-multiset Hilbert-space inequality, zeta-zero multiplicity symmetries, an admissible cutoff construction, and certified trigonometric estimates.

informal.ZetaZeros.simple_proportion_d4: Assuming the stated Riemann--von Mangoldt and unconditional pair-correlation formulas, beyond some height more than 67.25% of nontrivial zeta zeros are simple and lie on the critical line.
informal.ZetaZeros.distinct_proportion_d5: Under the same two explicit analytic hypotheses, beyond some height more than 83.625% of nontrivial zeta zeros are distinct.
informal.ZetaZeros.card_simpleRealPart_lower: Bounds from below the number of multiplicity-one real points in a finite nonempty conjugation-invariant multiset using the squared test-kernel sum of any admissible function.
informal.ZetaZeros.card_lower: Bounds from below the number of distinct points in a finite nonempty conjugation-invariant multiset using the same Hilbert-space kernel method.

records.title: Linear independence of 1, zeta(2), and zeta(3)
records.abstract: Proves that 1, the Riemann zeta function at 2, and its value at 3 are linearly independent over the rationals, using integer polynomial approximation, p-adic coefficient bounds, prime-edge nonvanishing, and logarithmic potential energy estimates for Hankel determinants. Includes reusable irrationality criteria, contour integration, Andreief identities, Newton-basis valuation bounds, and energy inequalities for finite measures. The cited source is the completed Lean proof; independent novelty of the informal argument is not claimed.

informal.Zeta32.one_zeta_two_zeta_three_linearInd: The three complex numbers 1, riemannZeta 2, and riemannZeta 3 are linearly independent over the rational numbers.
informal.Zeta32Acceptance.one_zeta_two_zeta_three: For rational a, b, and c, if a plus b times the real sum of 1/(k+1)^2 plus c times the real sum of 1/(k+1)^3 is zero, then all three coefficients are zero; both sums range over natural numbers k.
informal.Zeta32.zeta3_sub_rat_mul_zeta2_irrationa: For every rational r, the real series for zeta(3) minus r times the real series for zeta(2) is irrational.

records.title: Irrationality of ζ(3)
records.abstract: Formalizes Beukers' proof of Apéry's theorem for ζ(3), including the integral identities, denominator estimates, positivity, upper bounds, and final irrationality contradiction.

informal.LeanPool.Zeta3Irrational.linear_int: Clears denominators in the Apéry integral to produce a linear form in 1 and ζ(3).
informal.LeanPool.Zeta3Irrational.JJ_pos: Proves positivity of the transformed Beukers-Apéry integral.
informal.LeanPool.Zeta3Irrational.JJ_upper: Bounds the Beukers-Apéry integral by a geometric factor times the ζ(3) series.
informal.LeanPool.Zeta3Irrational.fun1_tendsto_ze: Shows that the denominator-cleared Apéry linear forms tend to zero.

records.title: ZFLean
records.abstract: Develops a practical ZFC set-theory framework with von Neumann naturals, integers, rationals, functions, embeddings, isomorphisms, booleans, and sums.

informal.ZFSet.isIso_of_biembedding: Proves a Cantor-Bernstein theorem for ZF sets.
informal.ZFSet.ZFNat.induction: Provides induction for the von Neumann natural numbers.
informal.ZFSet.ZFInt.induction: Provides induction for the quotient construction of ZF integers.

records.title: The Zhang-Yeung non-Shannon information inequality
records.abstract: Formalizes the Zhang-Yeung inequality, the first known non-Shannon-type entropy inequality, together with its dual and averaged forms derived through the copy lemma.

informal.ZhangYeung.zhangYeung: Proves the Zhang-Yeung non-Shannon-type information inequality for four discrete random variables.
informal.ZhangYeung.zhangYeung_dual: Proves the dual form of the Zhang-Yeung inequality.
informal.ZhangYeung.zhangYeung_averaged: Proves the averaged symmetric form of the Zhang-Yeung inequality.

records.title: Modular Schur numbers: S_m(k,ℓ) = n − 1 for k ≥ n − 1, where n = m/gcd(m,ℓ−1)
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization, with Mathlib, of the main results of the paper "Prime-power structure of the stable regime for modular Schur numbers" (docs/paper/modular-schur.pdf in this repository). The modular Schur number S_m(k,ℓ), introduced by Chappelon, Revuelta Marchena and Sanz Domínguez (2013), is the largest N such that 1, …, N can be coloured with k colours so that no colour class contains a solution of x_1 + ⋯ + x_ℓ ≡ y (mod m). For m ≥ 2 and ℓ ≥ 2, put n = m/gcd(m,ℓ−1). The main theorem is the closed form S_m(k,ℓ) = n − 1 for every k ≥ n − 1. D'orville, Sim, Wong and Ho (Integers 25 (2025) #A62) gave it when gcd(m,ℓ−1) = 1 (their Corollary 5). The general case is a short corollary of the singleton criterion and their Corollary 3; to the author's knowledge it is first stated in the paper. The proof turns on one value: ℓ copies of n sum to n modulo m, so the class {n} alone breaks the rule, while each of 1, …, n − 1 is safe in a class of its own. The formalization also proves the one-colour closed form S_m(1,ℓ) = min(ℓ − 1, ⌊m/ℓ⌋) for 2 ≤ ℓ ≤ m, which answers Problem 1.3 of D'orville et al.; the bound S_m(k,ℓ) ≤ m − 1 of Chappelon et al.; and the reduction from integers to residues modulo m. Twelve theorems with Mathlib-only statements are compared by lake comparator (statement identity, permitted axioms, and replay through the Lean, nanoda and con-ron kernels); their only axioms are propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The 33 project modules also contain further results, listed in LEAN_STATUS.md, that are proved and axiom-audited but are not compared, among them the bound m/p, with p the least prime factor of m, on the size of a set of residues whose pairwise differences all lie in a proper subgroup of ℤ/m. An earlier computational part of the project, which uses native_decide, is not in this repository and is not part of these results. The informal proofs, the Lean formalization and the paper were produced with AI systems (Claude, Aristotle and GPT-5) under the direction of the author.

records.title: The compositum of the two Mahler minimizers: exact measure, conjugate census, house, and minimal product recurrence, with the Bedford-Kim plastic family, Lehmer's polynomial, and the E_m Coxeter bridge
records.abstract: Kernel-checked certificates for the multiplicative compositum of the two registered Mahler minimizers — rho, the real root of x^3 = x + 1 (the plastic number: Smyth's nonreciprocal minimum, Siegel's smallest Pisot number) and Q, the real root > 1 of x^4 = x + 1 (the degree-4 entry of the minimal-measure tables) — together with the Bedford-Kim spectral family whose limit rho is, and (new in version 2) the identification of that family with the Coxeter-element spectra of the E_m star trees. Twenty-two compared theorems. The spectral half: (1) for n >= 7 the family chi_n(x) = x^(n+1)(x^3 - x - 1) + (x^3 + x^2 - 1) has a canonical root in [117/100, rho), largest below rho, strictly increasing, tending to rho; (2) every chi_n is strictly positive on [rho, infinity); (3) chi_7 = (x - 1) * L exactly, over any commutative ring, with L Lehmer's degree-10 polynomial; (4) L has a root in [117/100, rho). The compositum half, for the degree-12 minimal polynomial of rho * Q (written out in full in every compared statement): (5) an exclusion witness — a nonreal quartic root z with 1 < |rho * z| < rho * Q; (6) the twelve embedding products ARE the conjugates of rho * Q, both directions; (7) there are exactly twelve of them; (8) rho * Q is an algebraic unit, via an explicit degree-11 cofactor over any commutative ring — the (3, 4, 12) triple in the normal form alpha * beta * gamma = 1; (9) the degree-12 polynomial is not reciprocal (neither its reversal nor the reversal's negation), placing it in the regime of Smyth's theorem; (10) degree multiplicativity — deg minpoly(rho*Q) = deg minpoly(rho) * deg minpoly(Q) = 12; (11) the compositum in sup form Q(rho) join Q(Q) = Q(rho*Q), of degree 12, with the two simple extensions linearly disjoint; (12) the complete unit-circle census — EXACTLY 5 conjugates strictly outside, EXACTLY 7 strictly inside, NONE on the circle, so rho * Q is neither a Pisot nor a Salem number; (13) the house — every conjugate other than rho * Q has modulus strictly below rho * Q; (14) the exact Mahler measure M = rho^2 * Q^2 * psi, where psi is the real root > 1 of psi^4 = psi^3 + 1; (15) the registry bridge — M(X^4 - X - 1) = psi and M(rulerPoly) = (rho * Q)^2 * M(X^4 - X - 1), re-proving in-repo the quantity pinned in registered entry PALOMAR-2026-08-31-000004; (16) the order-12 Hadamard product recurrence — the termwise product of any solutions of the cubic and quartic shift recurrences satisfies the order-12 recurrence whose characteristic polynomial is exactly the degree-12 polynomial, in any Q-algebra; (17) the annihilator ideal of the product power sequence n |-> (rho * Q)^n is EXACTLY the principal ideal of the degree-12 polynomial — the classical order <= 3 * 4 bound is an equality, forced by the polynomial's kernel-held irreducibility. THE COXETER BRIDGE (version 2), for the star trees E_m = T(2,3,m-3) with generalized Cartan matrix A given entrywise and Coxeter element c = s_0 s_1 ... s_{m-1}, each simple reflection the matrix s_i = 1 - e_i e_i^T A of the geometric representation: (18) for every m >= 4, (X - 1) * charpoly(c) = X^(m-2)(X^3 - X - 1) + (X^3 + X^2 - 1) — the classical E_n Coxeter-polynomial identity (recorded in Gross-Hironaka-McMullen 2009, Section 1, and proved there as Cor. 4.3 for n >= 4), whose right-hand side is chi_{m-3}: the spectral half of this entry IS the E_m Coxeter spectrum; (19) with the E_10 Cartan matrix written out, the Coxeter polynomial of E_10 is Lehmer's polynomial; (20) for every m >= 10 the Coxeter polynomial of E_m has a root lambda_m in [117/100, rho) with no real root above it, the lambda_m strictly increasing and tending to rho; (21) for every m >= 10 the complexified Coxeter element has an eigenvalue lambda in (1, rho) and every complex eigenvalue is unimodular, lambda, or 1/lambda; (22) that lambda dominates the modulus of every eigenvalue and is a Salem number, for every m >= 10, with the Salem predicate written out as in the registered entry PALOMAR-2026-09-02-000003. Two disclosures of version 1 are discharged by (21)-(22) for n >= 7: the Salem property of the Bedford-Kim roots is now kernel-held, and the interval (1, 117/100) is now swept (the only eigenvalues off the unit circle are lambda_m and its inverse). The results address four research audiences: the degree problem for products and composita of algebraic numbers (the certified (3,4,12) witness at a canonically distinguished pair, in the field's own unit-product normal form); the Mahler-measure tradition (the measure of the composed product of the two degree-minimal polynomials, in closed form in the second-smallest Pisot number); composed products of polynomials (a certified rational instance where the finite-field coprimality criterion is unavailable and irreducibility is proved by elimination); and, new, Coxeter groups and Salem numbers (McMullen; Gross-Hironaka-McMullen; Hironaka's Lehmer program): the E_m Coxeter spectra, their Salem radii and their limit rho as one kernel-checked family — with the Lean audience served by concrete exercise of the Mahler-measure, linear-disjointness, Matrix.charpoly and spectrum APIs. Like the golden ratio, rho * Q is an algebraic unit of norm -1; the compared cofactor identity is that norm computation, certified. No novelty claim is made for the measure identity (the entry is not aware of it in the literature; the claimed contribution is the kernel certificate), none for the mathematics of (18)-(22), which is classical (the claimed contribution is the kernel-checked bridge from the registered Bedford-Kim family to the E_m Coxeter elements, for every m >= 4 (bridge) and every m >= 10 (spectrum, Salem) at once), no "first formalization" claim is made anywhere, and whether rho is ATTAINED as a dynamical degree is open in the literature — no statement claims it. Hypotheses are inline: rho, Q, psi enter only through their defining equations plus root-selection inequalities, the E_m Cartan matrices only through their entries, and the compared statements use only core Mathlib vocabulary (Filter.Tendsto, nhds, the complex norm, minpoly, Polynomial.rootSet, Set.ncard, Polynomial.mahlerMeasure, IntermediateField adjoin/sup, Module.finrank, Finset.range sums, Matrix.charpoly, Matrix.diagonal, List.finRange/List.prod, matrix literals, Matrix.map, spectrum, IsIntegral, Polynomial.aeval) — zero custom definitions. The name prefix "ruler" in statement names is the source project's term for the product rho * Q; nothing in any statement depends on it.

records.title: Generalized Markoff strong approximation
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the generic branch of eventual strong approximation for generalized Markoff surfaces, specialized to a fixed ordered integral coefficient triple. It proves punctured transitivity for both the full Vieta group and the two-Vieta rotation group, supplies an explicit coefficient-dependent cutoff, and derives surjectivity of coordinatewise reduction onto the full finite-field surface.

records.title: An interval-moment criterion for square-difference-free integer sets
records.abstract: We prove a general interval-moment criterion for square-difference-free integer sets and apply it to obtain an improved unconditional lower bound in Sarkozy's theorem, with exponent 0.7580758318008816. If D(N) is the largest size of a subset of {1, ..., N} containing no two distinct elements whose difference is a square, then for every epsilon > 0 and all sufficiently large N we prove D(N) >= N^(0.7580758318008816 - epsilon). The exact exponent is 473797394875551/625000000000000. The reusable criterion starts from finite digit sets in pairwise coprime square bases, with ordered intervals and width-moment inequalities. A strict surplus in the component exponents yields the asymptotic bound through finite stopping words, rank rounding, the Chinese remainder theorem, and interpolation between geometric scales. Both the general criterion and its numerical application are formalized in Lean. All nine concrete components are proved: six prime chains, a 25-state binary recursion, and two complete composite witnesses, at the primes 5 and 43 (three restricted digits at each) and at 19 and 23 (three at 19, two at 23). Every required ordering, numerical moment, lifting, and asymptotic argument is checked, with no remaining finite-certificate hypotheses. This version replaces the exponent 0.75806746 of version 1 with new finite witnesses and more precise certificates. The repository includes self-contained PDF and LaTeX write-ups of the full result and a simpler companion construction attaining exponent 0.758001 that explains several core ideas, together with exact computational certificate programs. The simpler construction is not separately formalized or a selected submission statement.

records.title: Formalization of a discrete Carleson theorem of Stein-Wainger type
records.abstract: This is a Lean 4 formalization of the main theorem of the papers arXiv:1907.00405 and arXiv:2107.14616 by Ben Krause and Joris Roos. The result concerns l^p boundedness for a  discrete maximal singular oscillatory operator of Stein-Wainger type, also called a discrete Carleson operator.

records.title: An Exponent of 1.043 for the Unit Distance Problem: Lean formalization at exponent 1.04315, conditional on one zeta inequality
records.abstract: Lean formalization accompanying the paper An Exponent of 1.043 for the Unit Distance Problem by Eric Naslund (cited under sources), which proves the exponent 1.043171 unconditionally with a computer-assisted certificate. Conditional theorem on unit distances in the Euclidean plane. Let B = Q(sqrt 241) and let E be the number field of degree 512 generated over Q by sqrt 241 and square roots of the eight elements -1, -71011068 + 4574225 sqrt 241, (-6101 - 393 sqrt 241)/2, (6101 - 393 sqrt 241)/2, 31 - 2 sqrt 241, 31 + 2 sqrt 241, 326 - 21 sqrt 241 and 326 + 21 sqrt 241 of B (a basis of the {2,3,5}-units of B modulo squares). Let E_W be the field of degree 8192 obtained from E by adjoining square roots of four explicit elements beta_1, ..., beta_4 of E, each generating with two of the square roots a dihedral extension of B of degree 8 (the elements are written out in the Challenge). Hypothesis (H_W) is one displayed numerical inequality for the Dedekind zeta function of E_W: log(Re zeta_{E_W}(1 + 1/4411))/8192 + (1/4411)((L - gamma - log(4 pi))/4 - Re((zeta_{E_W}'/zeta_{E_W})(2))/8192) < 50969/1000000, where L = (9/4) log 2 + (1/2) log 3615 and gamma is Euler's constant. The compared theorem proves that (H_W) implies the existence of finite sets U_j in the plane with |U_j| -> infinity such that the number of unordered pairs of points of U_j at distance one, divided by |U_j|^(20863/20000), tends to infinity. The exponent is exactly 20863/20000 = 1.04315. The conclusion is a sequence statement only; no bound at every sufficiently large cardinality is asserted. The infinite pro-2 tower over B with Frobenius caps at both primes above 29 and at one prime above 41 (generators, relation bound, presentation, Golod-Shafarevich infinitude, local data), its fields, which are Galois over B and over a fixed base field but not over Q, their local types and signature, the root-discriminant bound, the field E_W with its degree, its embedding in the base field and its local data, the passage from (H_W) to the analytic ceiling, the numerical margin and the planar construction are proved in Lean over Mathlib; (H_W) itself is not proved. Outside Lean, a rigorous computation (certified values of the 576 L-functions of degrees 4 and 8 in the factorization of zeta_{E_W} and an Euler product with explicit tail) bounds the left side of (H_W) by 0.0509172; that computation is not part of the formal proof. The earlier formalization registered as PALOMAR-2026-10-01-000018 version 1 proved the exponent 10427/10000 from a different inequality, for the field E.

records.title: Optimality, uniqueness and stability of Gerver's sofa from one coercive certificate, formalized in Lean 4
records.abstract:
The moving sofa problem asks for the largest area of a planar shape that can be moved around the right-angled corner of a hallway of unit width. Jineon Baek proved (arXiv:2411.19826) that Gerver's sofa G, of area 2.2195..., is optimal. His proof bounds the area of every large moving sofa by a concave functional Q of a triple (K, B, D) of convex bodies built from a cap K of the sofa, and shows that Q is largest at Gerver's triple, where it equals |G|.

This entry proves one estimate for Q, the coercive certificate, and derives three results from it. On an enlarged domain of triples, on which the cap need not satisfy Baek's injectivity condition, Q(K, B, D) <= |G|, and the cap K lies within Euclidean Hausdorff distance 2 sec(phi) sqrt(|G| - Q(K, B, D)) of the horizontal translate of Gerver's cap with the same leftmost point, where phi = 0.039... is Gerver's angle. The proof writes |G| - Q as a sum of nonnegative terms, and the energy terms among them also bound that distance. The bound is attained: Gerver's triple lies in the enlarged domain, and Q equals |G| there.

From the certificate: optimality, Baek's theorem, proved without his Theorem 1.1.1 and without the balance argument of his Chapters 4 to 6; uniqueness, every moving sofa with the area of G is mapped onto G by a rotation and a translation (a translation suffices); and stability, after a translation a moving sofa of area |G| - epsilon lies within Euclidean Hausdorff distance C sqrt(epsilon) of G, their symmetric difference has area at most C' sqrt(epsilon), its rotation angle misses a right angle by at most C'' epsilon, and the exponent 1/2 cannot be improved. The Challenge also states the correspondence between Baek's definitions and those of Google DeepMind's formal-conjectures, and formal-conjectures' statements, among them the uniqueness, which it lists as open; here they are proved through the certificate.

Versions 1 to 4 of this entry registered the formalization of Baek's paper with a first proof of uniqueness that uses his Theorem 1.1.1; they state the same optimality, uniqueness and formal-conjectures theorems, proved through Baek's argument, and the repository keeps their Challenge and Solution in baek/. This version proves those theorems through the certificate and adds the certificate and the stability. A script in the repository, scripts/AuditCoerciveRoute.lean, run by the continuous integration, checks that its proofs reach neither Baek's Theorem 1.1.1, nor the results of his balance argument, nor the main theorem and the equality analysis of the first proof of uniqueness.

records.title: Lower bounds for the covering numbers C(24,14,4) and C(25,15,5)
records.abstract: A Lean proof that every family of 14-element subsets of a 24-element set covering all 4-element subsets has at least 20 members, so the covering number C(24,14,4) is at least 20, improving the previously tabulated lower bound of 19. Point derivation (the Schönheim bound) then gives C(25,15,5) >= 34, improving the tabulated 32. The proof excludes a hypothetical 19-block covering: a sum-of-squares identity for the minimum-degree incidence vectors forces balanced components, a rigidity theorem for eleven-block (22,12,3) covers controls suitable completions and derivatives, and two counting contradictions finish the argument. The Lean proof follows the accompanying paper, paper/c24-14-4.pdf.

records.title: Dynamic MCS Ordering Maintenance
records.abstract: A fully-dynamic Maximum-Cardinality-Search (MCS) ordering algorithm that, on a single-edge insertion or deletion into a loop-free undirected graph, scans the affected window between the two endpoints for the first step at which the current ordering's choice stops being a legal MCS pick, and only then regreedies the suffix (probe-then-repair). Correctness - every order produced stays a valid MCS ordering of the updated graph, and in fact equals the from-scratch canonical ordering - is machine-checked in Lean 4 / Mathlib, together with locality (the first position whose choice can change lies inside the window between the endpoints; after a break the suffix is regreedyed, so positions past the window may also change), an executable boolean-adjacency implementation proved to refine the abstract update, and per-update cost in a unit-cost query model (counting legality checks and pick steps along the real executable control flow): at most n units for an insertion and n + 1 for a deletion, so the worst case matches static recomputation. A stability theorem is also proved: if the neighbour count of every vertex in one graph exceeds that in the other by at most one along every *proper common MCS prefix* (the sets the constructive proof actually visits -- a hypothesis strictly weaker than the every-subset bound), the two graphs admit a common MCS ordering; in particular inserting or deleting a matching, or flipping a single edge, always preserves a common MCS ordering. This strengthening (exists_common_ordering_prefix) makes the matching result a genuine corollary; the every-subset version exists_common_ordering is retained as a special case.

records.title: Alexandroff Property of Metric Indecomposable Continua
records.abstract: Todorov–Valov Theorem 3.3: for two disjoint closed sets with nonempty interiors in a metric indecomposable continuum, one open cover obstructs every separator map onto every nonempty compact connected Hausdorff target. The classical composant properties remain as foundations.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: Explicit Szemerédi–Trotter bounds over arbitrary fields
records.abstract: We formalize four explicit Szemerédi–Trotter incidence bounds for m distinct points and n distinct affine lines in a field plane. In characteristic zero the bound is 3(mn)^(2/3) + m + n. In positive characteristic p, an arbitrary field admits the additional term 2mn/p. This term is absent when mn ≤ p³. Over the prime field ZMod p the additional term improves to mn/p without a size restriction. The development adapts the author's polynomial-method argument, uses generic coordinates for the improved linear term, and proves a finite-plane counting estimate for the prime-field refinement.

records.title: Linear upper bounds for the first Betti number of four-generated numerical semigroups
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization, against Mathlib, of the theorem that the first Betti number (minimal number of generators of the toric ideal) of a numerical semigroup minimally generated by four elements n0 < n1 < n2 < n3 is at most 2W, where W = (n3 - n0) / gcd(n1 - n0, n2 - n0, n3 - n0); in particular at most twice the width n3 - n0.  This replaces the conjectured quadratic bound (w+1 choose 2) of Herzog–Stamate (2014) and Caviglia–Moscariello–Sammartano (2024) in embedding dimension four; the bound 2w is attained for every width w >= 4 (an informal companion result; sharpness is not formalized).

records.title: The CLARK Tile: An Aperiodic Monotile in Five Dimensions
records.abstract: We give an explicit compact tile, called CLARK (Chair with Local Asymmetric Registration Keys), in five-dimensional Euclidean space. It modifies a chair of 31 unit five-cubes with 256 rational pyramidal keys. Copies may be translated, rotated or reflected. The selected theorem proves tiling existence, no nonzero translation period in any physical tiling, and a finite full Euclidean symmetry group of cardinality at most 3840 for every such tiling. No registration, matching-rule or hierarchy assumption is imposed. A trivial symmetry group is not asserted.

records.title: LeanMMBound: the matrix multiplication exponent is below 2.3710449
records.abstract: The matrix multiplication exponent ω is the least exponent such that n×n matrices can be multiplied in n^(ω+o(1)) operations. This repository proves in Lean 4 / Mathlib that ω < 2.3710449 over every commutative ring, improving the previous bound ω < 2.371177 (Dupont et al. 2026). ω is defined via the exact tensor rank of n×n matrix multiplication. The new ingredient is shared extraction across recursion levels of the asymmetric laser method. The formalization covers the full argument, from the Coppersmith–Winograd degeneration to an exact rational certificate checked in the Lean kernel. The construction and proof were produced largely by AI systems under the authors' direction.

records.title: Order Arcs Between Subcontinua
records.abstract: Properly nested nonempty compact connected subsets A and B of a compact metric space are the endpoints of a continuous embedded interval of nonempty compact connected subsets, strictly increasing under inclusion. The ambient space need not be connected.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: The density hypothesis for σ > 3/4
records.abstract: Lean formalization of Nζ(σ,T) ≪σ,ε T^(2(1−σ)+ε), hence A(σ) ≤ 2, for fixed 3/4 < σ < 1 and ε > 0; zeros with Re(ρ) ≥ σ and 0 < Im(ρ) ≤ T are counted with multiplicity.

records.title: Erdős 374: classical square products of factorials
records.abstract: Formalization of classical factorial-square constructions, exclusion of prime endpoints, existence of minimum representation cardinalities for composite endpoints, and the cutoff D_k = empty for k greater than six. The density question from Erdős problem 374 is defined but not proved. No mathematical novelty or solution of the density problem is claimed.

records.title: Six concyclic points satisfy the Euclidean Ramsey tensor criterion, as does every spherical set of at most m + 4 points of affine dimension m and every algebraic spherical set; given the classification's sufficiency half, these sets are Ramsey (the algebraic ones when spanning)
records.abstract: A Lean 4 development around the tensor criterion of the classification of finite Euclidean Ramsey configurations (openai/math, family 172). With the criterion's definitions restated character for character from that project's challenge file: every set of six distinct points on a circle satisfies the criterion, by an explicit certificate (the product of the two bilinear forms through the first three and the last three points of a homogeneous parametrisation of the circle, scaled and conjugated by the parametrisation); the sharp dimension theorem: every spherical set of at most m + 4 distinct points, m the dimension of its affine span, satisfies the criterion in its own space and coordinate field (either the augmented vectors admit real isolating quadrics and the sphere lifts by the adjugate, or a dependence among them is supported on six concyclic points while every other point adds a dimension, and the six-point certificate is carried into the ambient space, symmetrised, adjusted to the common sphere, extended point by point and descended from R tensor R to F tensor F), so every spherical set of at most six points satisfies it in any dimension with any affine span; every spherical set with algebraic coordinates satisfies it, of any size, by the separability idempotent of F tensor F; the criterion always implies sphericity, so for algebraic coordinates it is exactly sphericity. Given the sufficiency half of the classification as an explicit hypothesis (quantified as the source states its Theorem 1.1), every spherical set of at most six points, every spherical set of at most m + 4 points and every spanning spherical set with algebraic coordinates is Ramsey; given both halves, a spanning set with algebraic coordinates is Ramsey if and only if it is spherical. The source proves the Ramsey property for at most five circle points; six is the first case its method of independent quadratic rows cannot reach. With the seven-point non-Ramsey circle set of A cyclic non-Ramsey heptagon (arXiv:2609.23327), the least size of a non-Ramsey spherical set is seven, given the classification, and, for m at least 2, m + 5 the least size of one with affine span of dimension m, since the heptagon with m - 2 further sphere points fails the criterion and is not Ramsey; the research note in note/ states this, verifies by an exact derivation identity that the heptagon fails the criterion, and proves the sharpness on paper (nothing in Lean says that a set fails the criterion). The classification is not proved here. The restated definitions and a few adapted lemmas derive from Apache-2.0 work of OpenAI (NOTICE, LICENSES/Apache-2.0.txt); the rest is MIT.

records.title: Sharp Wasserstein propagation of chaos from correlated initial data
records.abstract: A Lean 4 proof, checked against Mathlib, of a sharp quantitative propagation of chaos estimate for mean field diffusions dX_i = (a(X_i) + N^{-1} sum_j K(X_i, X_j)) dt + sqrt 2 dW_i with a globally Lipschitz one-body drift a and a bounded, globally Lipschitz pairwise interaction K. If every k-particle marginal of the (possibly correlated and singular) exchangeable initial law lies within squared quadratic Wasserstein distance C_0 (k/N)^2 of the corresponding power of the McKean-Vlasov initial law, then the same holds on every finite time interval [0, T] with an explicit constant C_T that depends neither on N nor on the dimension. No entropy bound, transport inequality or independence of the initial particles is assumed.

records.title: A strongly tempered Meyer space of countably infinite Hamel dimension
records.abstract: There exists a locally finite carrier Λ in the real line whose whole complex strongly tempered Meyer space has Hamel dimension ℵ₀. Both a tempered distribution and its distributional Fourier transform have local atomic formulas on Λ, with coefficient families whose absolute values are summable after division by some polynomial weight (1 + |x|)^N. The same carrier supports the entire space; finite-dimensional exponent layers prove the rank upper bound and independent original parity modes prove the lower bound. The radius schedule is selected classically. This is an existence theorem for one carrier, not an effective construction or a classification of all carriers.

records.title: Improved exponents for 3SUM and APSP from triangles in sparse lopsided graphs
records.abstract: A sorry-free Lean 4 formalization of improved running-time exponents for 3SUM, Exact Triangle, the (min,+)-product and all-pairs shortest paths (APSP), on the word RAM of the published formalization (anthropics/formal-math, 3sum-apsp) of the paper of Alman and Vassilevska Williams, "Truly Subquadratic 3SUM and Truly Subcubic APSP via Triangles in Sparse Lopsided Graphs" (arXiv:2610.06783). That paper gives deterministic algorithms for 3SUM in time O(n^1.9992) and for the (min,+)-product and APSP in time O(n^2.99942), through Exact Triangle in time O(n^(3 - 0.0017)). The project analyzes the same algorithm again and changes it in a few places: an exact count of the leaves of its recursion, a host that charges the solver at the true size of the middle part, and encodings restricted to the leaves that are read. The theorems submitted state, in exactly the sense of upstream's trusted file EndStatement.lean (programs of a word RAM with O(log n)-bit words, numbers of polynomial absolute value, every instance, every size), that 3SUM is solved in O(n^1.99896) steps and Exact Triangle in O(n^2.99791) steps, and, by carrying out the all-edges route that footnote 10 of the paper mentions, that the (min,+)-product and APSP are solved in O(n^2.99791) steps instead of O(n^2.99931) through the standard reductions. None of them has a hypothesis; every proof depends only on the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The library also proves general theorems for all admissible parameters, a closed form for the optimal saving of the method at each ratio of parameters, and that the supremum of that saving over all ratios lies in (0.002095, 0.002096], so that no choice of parameters gives 3SUM an exponent below 1.998952 with this method. The pruned encoder and the two new hosts are written as programs of the machine and their running times are proved on it. All Lean, Python and LaTeX was written by the language model Claude Fable 5.1 (Anthropic) in Claude Code, under the direction of the maintainer, who wrote no Lean by hand; the move to Lean v4.35.0-rc2, with the port of the included part of upstream, was made by Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic) in the same way. An accompanying paper (papers/improved-exponents/) states every result with its Lean name.

records.title: Area stability of planar plank covers and Bezdek's annulus theorem
records.abstract: A complete Lean 4 formalization of Bezdek's annulus theorem and the quantitative area stability of planar plank covers based on the paper "Area stability of plank covers" by Egor Bakaev and Amir Yehudayoff (arXiv:2609.30409). The formalization proves that there exists an explicit positive radius r > 0 such that if finitely many planar planks cover the closed annulus r <= ||x|| <= 1, their total width is at least 2. The core theorem established is the quantitative overlap theorem, which bounds the excess overlap cost on the unit disk from below by a positive constant times the hole area divided by r.

records.title: Matrix multiplication exponent at most 9/4 over arbitrary fields
records.abstract: This development extends OpenAI's Lean proof of the matrix multiplication exponent bound 9/4 from the complex numbers to every field, including finite fields and fields of positive characteristic. It generalizes Fourier separation and interpolation over each field's algebraic closure, descends tensor powers through one fixed finite coefficient algebra, and connects the resulting exact-rank bounds to the original division-free arithmetic-program model. The compared statements include the arithmetic exponent upper bound, nonvacuity and lower-bound checks, an explicit positive-epsilon operation-count theorem, and exact coordinatewise coefficient decompositions. The original numerical bound and complex-field construction are OpenAI's work; this fork contributes the arbitrary-field extension and its formal verification.

records.title: Stability of Matter in Lean: Lieb–Thirring, Ionization, the Thermodynamic Limit and Thomas–Fermi Theory
records.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of the stability of non-relativistic Coulomb matter in three dimensions. For normalized antisymmetric L2 electron states with q >= 1 spin states and static nuclei with charges between zero and Z, it proves a lower energy bound -C(q,Z)(N+M), uniformly in particle counts and nuclear positions. The main estimate is an additive inequality between nonnegative extended energies, valid even for infinite kinetic energy and nuclear collisions. A real quadratic-form theorem proves Coulomb finiteness and the lower bound for states with finite kinetic energy and distinct nuclear positions. The library also proves the kinetic Lieb-Thirring inequality with Rumin's explicit coefficient (9/35)(6 pi^2)^(2/3) q^(-2/3), Baxter's electrostatic inequality with its positive nearest-other-nucleus correction, and equality of the Fourier kinetic form with the classical Dirichlet integral on spin-valued Schwartz functions. The kinetic normalization is -Delta. The proof combines Pauli projections and Rumin's layer cake, a Voronoi boundary-measure proof of Baxter's inequality, nearest-nucleus screening, and Hardy's inequality. Three extensions prove the atomic bound N < 2Z+1 for weak ground states and strict binding, the unique continuous convex canonical zero-temperature energy density of neutral matter with finite-mass bosonic nuclei in Dirichlet balls, and the molecular Thomas-Fermi large-charge limit for arbitrary fixed spin and every fixed TF mass nu>0. Thomas-Fermi theory also has a unique relaxed minimizer, mass saturation at the total nuclear charge, and exact-mass attainment precisely up to neutrality.

records.title: Sharp robustness and stability of the four-row permanent inequality
records.abstract: A formalization of sharp balanced-law robustness and stability refinements of the classical four-row permanent inequalities of Carlen-Lieb-Loss and Bristiel-Caputo. It proves the exact total-variation radius 1/24, optimal variance-deficit coefficient (1-24r)/9, complete nonnegative equality cases, sharp endpoint entropy constants, and adaptive tensorization. The explicit interior exponent is sufficient rather than optimal; at radius zero it is weaker than the classical optimal uniform exponent. Lean checks exhaustive support coverage and exact rational Gram identities.

records.title: Ginibre Poincaré formalization
records.abstract: Lean development of the sharp Poincaré inequality for the complex Ginibre log-gas, its two sum-of-squares deficit identities, equality cases, Gaussian Hermite analysis, and the accompanying analytic and stochastic results.

records.title: The generalized Fermat equation x² + y⁵ = z⁷
records.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of the main results of the paper "The generalized Fermat equation x² + y⁵ = z⁷" by Manvir Jaswal. Following Putz, a solution is a triple of integers (X, Y, Z) with X⁵ + Y² = Z⁷, gcd(X, Y, Z) = 1 and XYZ ≠ 0; put η = X⁵/Z⁷ and A_η = ℚ[t]/(f_η), where f_η(t) = 4t⁵ψ(t) − η(4t − 1) and ψ(t) = 25t³ + 20t² + 14t + 14. Theorem 1.1 says that A_η is never isomorphic to Putz's octic field L₈ = ℚ[x]/(h), where h(x) = x⁸ + 4x⁷ − 28x⁶ − 168x⁵ − 140x⁴ + 560x³ + 840x² − 480x − 940. Theorem 1.2 combines this with Putz's Theorem 4.33, which says that A_η is always isomorphic to L₈, to show that x² + y⁵ = z⁷, and equivalently x² + y⁷ = z⁵ and x⁵ + y⁷ = z², have no solution in nonzero coprime integers. The Lean theorems take two hypotheses: Putz's Theorem 4.33 (for Theorem 1.2 only), and that the class group of the ring of integers of L₂₄ = L₈[t]/(ψ) has no element of order 5, which follows from the paper's proof that L₂₄ has class number 1, a computation that is not formalized. The proof follows the paper: a fifth-power descent over L₂₄, completed by fifth-power residue symbols at the primes 101, 131, 181, 251 and 311, with every computation checked by the Lean kernel.

records.title: Strict Dirichlet Pólya inequality on simply connected planar domains
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the strict Dirichlet Pólya inequality for bounded, open, simply connected planar domains, including the indexed eigenvalue and counting formulations.

records.title: Explicit uniformly bounded bases of homogeneous holomorphic polynomials in every dimension
records.abstract: We construct uniformly bounded orthonormal bases for homogeneous holomorphic polynomials on complex unit spheres. Fix d >= 2 and N >= 0, and put m = d-1 and L = N+d-1. For each multi-index alpha = (alpha_1,...,alpha_d) of nonnegative integers with sum N, define s_b(alpha) = b + alpha_1 + ... + alpha_b, 1 <= b <= m, and the normalized monomial M_alpha(z) = sqrt((N+d-1)! / ((d-1)! alpha_1! ... alpha_d!)) z_1^alpha_1 ... z_d^alpha_d. Let F be the normalized Fourier matrix, with entries F_(t,s) = L^(-1/2) exp(2 pi i t s/L), for 1 <= t,s <= L. For each increasing m-element subset T = {t_1,...,t_m} of {1,...,L}, define P_T(z) = sum_(|alpha|=N) det[F_(t_a,s_b(alpha))] exp(2 pi i sqrt(2) sum_r alpha_r^2) M_alpha(z), where the determinant is over 1 <= a,b <= m. These polynomials form an orthonormal basis with respect to surface measure of total mass one on the complex unit sphere. Their absolute values on the closed unit ball are bounded by a constant depending only on d, independently of N and T. The construction and proof are formalized in Lean.

records.title: A zero-density estimate with exponent 3(1−σ)/(2σ) for the Riemann zeta function
records.abstract: For every real sigma>3/4 and epsilon>0 there exists C>0 such that for all real T>=2, all actual Riemann zeta zeros with Re(rho)>=sigma and |Im(rho)|<=T, counted with analytic multiplicity, number at most C*T^(3*(1-sigma)/(2*sigma)+epsilon). The proof combines separately proved Type I Dirichlet-polynomial large-values and critical-line twelfth-moment bounds. The companion moment is the literal integral on [0,3T] bounded by K*T^(2+epsilon), eventually in T. No analytic premise remains in the final endpoints. Compared with Tao–Trudgian–Yang Table 2 and Kerr Theorem 6, the leading exponent improves for 3/4<sigma<23/29, agrees with the best located leading exponent on [23/29,7/8], and is weaker on (7/8,1). See docs/LITERATURE.md for scope and citations.

records.title: Erdős Problem 809: an independent proof of the seven-cycle threshold
records.abstract: For every fixed integer k >= 3, the minimum number of colors in an edge-coloring of an n-vertex simple graph with at least floor(n^2/4)+1 edges, in which every copy of C_(2k+1) is rainbow, is (1/8 + o(1))n^2. The minimum is attained. The development combines Asad Shahab's seven-cycle proof, using an exact rational five-vertex certificate, with a formalization of the Bucić-Chen-Ma argument for longer odd cycles.

records.title: Strict Neumann Polya inequality on simply connected planar domains
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the strict Neumann Pólya inequality for bounded simply connected Lipschitz domains in the plane. The plane is identified with ℂ; the Neumann eigenvalues μ_0 ≤ μ_1 ≤ ... are defined by the Courant–Fischer min–max formula for the form ∫|∇u|² on H¹(Ω) (weak gradients in L²), indexed from 0 and repeated according to multiplicity, and N_N(E) = #{j ≥ 0 : μ_j < E}. The principal results are: for every bounded simply connected Lipschitz domain Ω and every integer j ≥ 1, |Ω| μ_j(Ω) < 4πj; and, equivalently, N_N(E) > |Ω| E / (4π) for every E > 0. The proof development (about 100,000 lines, namespace PolyaNeumann) also identifies the variational eigenvalues with the spectrum of the constructed self-adjoint Neumann operator, proves a quantitative smooth-domain estimate via boundary transport, Cayley/monodromy rank bounds and a Herglotz-wave reduction, and passes to Lipschitz domains by smooth approximation.

records.title: Finite Chains of Two-Complexes and Acyclic Covers
records.abstract: Whitehead's asphericity problem would have a negative answer if a non-aspherical two-complex began an infinite chain whose inclusions induce zero maps on second homotopy groups. This Lean formalization proves the article's main finite-length characterization: a connected two-complex K begins such chains of every finite length if and only if K has a connected acyclic regular cover. It also formalizes the finite acyclic enhancement.

records.title: Brill--Noether existence and rank for graphs through genus six
records.abstract: This repository proves Baker's Brill--Noether existence conjecture for finite graphs of genus at most six.  The conjecture states that if G is a finite connected loopless multigraph, with genus defined to be g = E-V+1, then for all nonnegative integers d, r, there exists a configuration of d chips on G with Baker--Norine rank at least r provided that the Brill--Noether number rho = g - (r+1)(g-d+r) is nonnegative.  To the author's knowledge, this is a new result, extending a result of Atanasov and Ranganathan from genus five to six.  Two generalizations are also included.  First, in genus at most six, the Brill--Noether rank, in the sense of Lim--Payne--Potashnik, is at least the expected dimension of the Brill--Noether locus, when d is at most g+r. This is a combinatorial analog of the classical lower bound on the dimension of Brill--Noether loci, usually established on algebraic curves using intersection theory.  Second, the Brill--Noether existence conjecture for graphs with one marked vertex, as stated by Pflueger--Solomon, holds in genus up to five.  The proof synthesizes recent work of Christ--Ma and Draisma--Vargas. The work of Christ--Ma predicts the subdivision required to obtain special divisors on graphs, using enumerative geometry. The work of Draisma--Vargas provides a combinatorial construction to realize these special divisors.  The novel contribution in this repository is a descent argument, producing special divisors on the original graph from special divisors on an odd subdivision.  This work has not yet been written up for publication; the present repository is the first announcement of it.

records.title: MaxSNP-completeness and APX-completeness of MAX-3-SAT and 3-OCCURRENCE MAX-3-SAT (the PCP theorem and hardness of approximation) in Lean 4
records.abstract:
A Lean 4 proof of the PCP theorem and of its consequences for approximation, for an explicit single-tape Turing machine model. The compared theorems are: the PCP theorem in gap form, that for a fixed fraction num/den > 0 every NP language reduces in polynomial time to 3-SAT so that members give satisfiable formulas and non-members give formulas of which every assignment leaves at least that fraction of the clauses unsatisfied (Complexity.pcp_gap); the PCP theorem in verifier form, NP = PCP(O(log n), O(1)) (Complexity.pcp_theorem); that the problems of the syntactic class MaxSNP0 are in NPO (Complexity.npo_maxSNP0); that MaxSNP-hard problems have no polynomial-time approximation scheme unless P = NP (Complexity.maxSNPHard_not_hasPTAS), even when a separate algorithm is allowed for each precision (Complexity.maxSNPHard_no_ptas); that MAX-3-SAT and 3-OCCURRENCE MAX-3-SAT are MaxSNP-complete (Complexity.max3SAT_maxSNPComplete, Complexity.max3SAT3_maxSNPComplete); and that both are APX-complete (Complexity.max3SAT_apxComplete, Complexity.max3SAT3_apxComplete). The statement, Challenge.lean, imports only Lean core and defines everything it uses: the machine model, P, NP and polynomial-time functions; probabilistically checkable proofs and gap reductions; optimization problems, approximation algorithms and schemes; NPO; L-reductions, the syntactic class MaxSNP0 of Papadimitriou and Yannakakis (structures of fixed input and solution signatures on a finite universe, and a well-formed quantifier-free formula) and the class MaxSNP of NPO problems L-reducible to it; APX and PTAS-reductions in the sense of Crescenzi and Trevisan; and the two problems.
The gap form of the PCP theorem is proved by Dinur's gap amplification: the 3-CNF gap map, its soundness and its implementation as a polynomial-time multi-stack Turing machine are taken from the Lean formalization of the Unique Games theorem in the OpenAI mathematics repository (194 files, adapted to the Lean module system and to Lean v4.35.0-rc2), and composed with the Cook-Levin reduction of the Palomar entry PALOMAR-2026-10-02-000013 (whose library is included). A simulation theorem carries polynomial time from Mathlib's multi-stack machines to the single-tape model. The verifier form samples clauses of the gap formula with O(log n) random bits. MaxSNP-hard problems have no approximation scheme because MAX-3-SAT L-reduces to them and an approximation scheme for MAX-3-SAT would decide the gap. MAX-3-SAT is put in MaxSNP0 by an explicit quantifier-free formula, and every MaxSNP0 problem L-reduces to it by the Papadimitriou-Yannakakis clause construction (one clause per falsifying pattern of atoms, split into 3-clauses with fresh variables, with an averaging bound for the constant; assignments are mapped back to structures of the solution signature). The MaxSNP0 problems are in NPO by an explicit polynomial-time parser and feasibility check, and a size bound for structures of a fixed signature. 3-OCCURRENCE MAX-3-SAT is reached in two L-reductions: copies of each variable linked along an explicit constant-degree expander (from the same OpenAI development), and then a torus gadget of implications. APX-hardness under PTAS-reductions needs a witness-recovering PCP theorem, which is proved here: an explicit deterministic decoder, shown polynomial-time, turns every assignment of the gap formula that satisfies more than the fraction 1 - num/den of its clauses into an assignment of the original formula and then into an NP certificate. With it every APX problem reduces to MAX-3-SAT by a threshold construction. Membership in APX uses a 2-approximation. The proof uses only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

records.title: Inverse classification for innerly joint short zero-sum subsequences in C3^3
records.abstract: We formalize an exact positional inverse classification in the elementary abelian group C3^3. For a sequence of 24 nonzero elements, every pair of nonempty zero-sum subsequences of length at most three has intersection sum zero if and only if the original sequence, up to a permutation of all 24 positions, consists of three copies of eight distinct elements having no short nonempty zero sum. The two implications, including the positional intersection condition, are proved in Lean. The existing literature review did not locate the exact inverse classification, but historical novelty, priority and significance are not certified.

records.title: MIP* = RE
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of MIP* = RE (Ji, Natarajan, Vidick, Wright and Yuen): the class of languages decidable by a classical polynomial-time verifier interacting with two provers who share entanglement, with completeness 1 and soundness 1/2, is exactly the class of recursively enumerable languages. The development also contains the halting reduction behind it (a computable map from Turing machines to nonlocal games whose synchronous and quantum values are 1 if the machine halts and at most 1/2 otherwise) and its corollaries that the synchronous and the quantum value of a game are uncomputable.
