It builds on three other formalizations: the soundness of the classical low individual degree test (MIPStarRE, by Sirui Lu, Ruixuan Deng and Zhengfeng Ji, registered as PALOMAR-2026-08-18-000001), imported as a pinned Lake dependency, and the parallel repetition theorem for entangled strategies (ten-proofs, OpenAI) and the direct parallel repetition theorem for commuting-operator strategies (commuting-repetition), which are vendored with their provenance recorded. Palomar/Challenge.lean states the four compared theorems on top of Mathlib alone, in a tree-program model of polynomial time that the fidelity section describes; Palomar/Solution.lean proves them from the library.

records.title: Replica symmetry up to the de Almeida–Thouless line in the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of the positive-field Sherrington–Kirkpatrick results in Patrick Lopatto's arXiv:2604.11921v2. The selected registry claims are convergence of the expected finite-volume free energy to the concrete replica-symmetric Gaussian formula for beta > 0, h > 0, and AT parameter at most one, including equality; and an exact description of the positive-field AT boundary as a positive strictly increasing smooth graph on beta > 1, tending to zero at beta = 1 from the right, together with (1,0). The repository also contains the numbered PDE, stochastic-process, moment, and variational results documented in COVERAGE.md and results.json.

records.title: Hörmander's hypoellipticity theorem and the Rothschild–Stein theory
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the regularity theory of Hörmander operators: second-order operators built from smooth vector fields X_1, ..., X_q (and possibly a drift X_0) whose iterated commutators span the tangent space at every point. It proves Hörmander's 1967 theorem that such operators are hypoelliptic: every locally integrable weak solution of X_0 u + sum X_i^2 u + c u = g with smooth data is smooth. It then develops the Rothschild–Stein theory (Acta Math. 1976), following Bramanti and Brandolini's "Hörmander Operators" (2023): lifting and approximation of the fields by the generators of a homogeneous group; the homogeneous fundamental solution and singular-integral estimates on homogeneous groups; and the sharp interior estimates, by which a distributional solution of sum X_i^2 T = f with f in W^{k,p}_X or C^{k,alpha}_X is a function in W^{k+2,p}_X or C^{k+2,alpha}_X, for every k >= 0, and at k = 0 with a drift. The formalization also proves the formal Baker–Campbell–Hausdorff theorem, Chow–Rashevskii connectivity, and the Nagel–Stein–Wainger theorems on control balls (ball-box, volume and doubling, comparison of distances), uniformly over compact sets.

records.title: Uniform permanence of endotactic reaction networks with measurable rates
records.abstract: Uniform permanence is established for finite endotactic reaction networks with arbitrary real complexes and measurable rate coefficients bounded above and away from zero almost everywhere. Each positive stoichiometric compatibility class contains a compact convex forward-invariant absorbing set, with entry times uniform over compact sets of initial conditions and all rate histories within a fixed rate box. Global positive Carathéodory solutions exist and are unique, and an exponential continuous-dependence estimate holds for initial data under a common rate history on a compact positive region. The result resolves the Endotactic Permanence Conjecture stated as Conjecture 1.3 by Johnston, Pantea and Donnell (https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.4662), using an ordinary-endotactic drift estimate together with the finite affine barrier construction from OpenAI’s work on weakly reversible networks.

records.title: Planar Euclidean midpoint rigidity
records.abstract: A complete Lean proof of the dimension-two case of Nielsen–Okamura Conjecture 9.1. On any connected open planar Euclidean domain, complementarity of the actual canonical local affine-parameter midpoints of a smooth pair of dual torsion-free connections forces the symmetric cubic tensor to be constant. The proof constructs and identifies the short geodesic germs and derives the fourth-order obstruction, including the exceptional rank-deficient tensors. A second theorem needs only everywhere Frechet differentiability and vanishing of that obstruction; five fixed direction tests at every point suffice. Dimensions above two are outside the claim.

records.title: Full replica symmetry breaking in the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model
records.abstract: Lean formalization of Patrick Lopatto's zero-field Sherrington–Kirkpatrick results. The selected claims are full interval support, a nonnegative smooth density with a terminal atom for every inverse temperature beta > 1, and quantitative inequalities for that actual atom. The independent Challenge defines the Parisi functional through concrete bounded-gradient weak PDE solutions, with terminal log cosh and coefficient beta squared divided by two. Solution identifies that definition with the constructed Parisi potential. The repository retains the supporting PDE, diffusion, covariance, minimizer, and numbered-result development described in COVERAGE.md and results.json.

records.title: Nearly minimax variance estimation under rough random design
records.abstract: Minimax root-mean-square bounds for estimating a constant conditional variance from independent random-design regression observations. The design density has fixed positive lower and upper bounds but no smoothness; covariate-dependent errors have uniformly bounded conditional fourth moments. For 1 < s < d/4, the proved bracket identifies the polynomial exponent 2(s+1)/(d+4) and the common explicit stretched-exponential factor, with a remaining logarithmic gap. It also proves the exponent corollary, the exact low-smoothness rate, and the parametric regime.

records.title: Kinetic Aleksandrov estimates
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalisation of Aleksandrov maximum principles for kinetic equations d_t u + v.grad_x u - A : D_v^2 u = f in non-divergence form, with measurable, uniformly elliptic diffusion acting only in the velocity. For coefficients A(t,v) the estimate holds for every source exponent p > 2d+1; for autonomous coefficients a(x,v) in one space dimension for every p above a threshold 1 + beta_*(Lambda/lambda) < 4, where no exponent below 4 works uniformly in the ellipticity ratio; and for general measurable coefficients A(t,x,v) for every p >= 1 + 128 d^2 (Lambda/lambda)^2 / 3. In each case the estimate implies interior Hölder continuity of solutions; for coefficients A(t,x,v) this is the kinetic Krylov–Safonov theorem. The library also proves the parabolic Aleksandrov estimate of Krylov, the parabolic Harnack inequality of Krylov and Safonov, the terminal solution operators of the kinetic equation, and classical Dirichlet solvability on ellipsoidal cylinders. Hörmander's hypoellipticity theorem is taken from the formalisation hoermander-rothschild-stein.

records.title: Nearly Minimax Rates for Functional Estimation Under Rough Random Design
records.abstract: A Lean development of upper and local lower minimax bounds for nonlinear functionals of conditional means under bounded, rough random design. The generic theorem covers the root-n regime and the subcritical regime with its density-dependent stretched-exponential correction, logarithmic upper and lower factors, and a one-quarter minimax probability lower bound. The substantive development also contains projection, polynomial-estimator, Poisson reduction, lattice-prior, application, and causal-identification results. The selected Comparator surface is the generic theorem's two parts. The remaining logarithmic gap is unresolved.

records.title: De Giorgi–Nash–Moser theory under coarse ellipticity
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the paper "Coarse ellipticity and De Giorgi–Nash–Moser theory in the optimal range" by S. Armstrong, B. Avelin, T. Kuusi and A. Turpeinen (arXiv:2610.11879). The paper extends the theory of De Giorgi–Nash–Moser to elliptic equations with symmetric coefficients a(x) which are possibly degenerate and unbounded but satisfy a coarse ellipticity condition: spatial moments of coarse-grained matrices, suitably discounted and summed across scales, are finite. Under this condition it proves local upper bounds for weak subsolutions, a weak Harnack inequality for nonnegative supersolutions, and a Harnack inequality for nonnegative solutions. The condition holds if a ∈ W^{-α,p} ∩ L^1, a^{-1} ∈ W^{-β,q} ∩ L^1 and (α+β)/2 + ((d-1)/2)(1/p + 1/q) < 1, for some α, β ≥ 0 and 1 < p, q < ∞. This range is sharp, including its boundary, in every dimension d ≥ 3: for α = β = 0, where it corresponds to the results of Bella and Schäffner, and for the corresponding Besov-type quasi-norms of negative order when α, β > 0. The formalization covers these results, together with the optimality of the powers of the coarse ellipticity ratio in the local bounds and of the range of exponents in the weak Harnack inequality. The statements are for dimension d ≥ 3 and are formulated on the unit cube; the limiting cases p = ∞ or q = ∞ are not formalized. CORRESPONDENCE.md gives the status of every numbered statement of the paper. Built on Mathlib and the CoarseGraining library, using only Lean's standard axioms.

records.title: Exponential separation of analytic self-conformal sets on the real line: Lean formalisation
records.abstract: Lean 4 formalisation of exponential separation for analytic iterated function systems on the real line. Strong exponential separation holds on an open and dense subset in the C2 topology and follows from an explicit criterion involving dual projections. The development characterises conjugacy to self-similar systems and proves dimension consequences conditional on cited results of Rapaport and Bowen, including a drop in the L^q dimensions of the natural measure of a concrete three-map example.

records.title: A 7-vertex tournament whose Sperner capacity exceeds the order of its largest transitive subtournament: T₇, induced by the Paley tournament on 23 vertices on 0, 1, 2, 3, 9, 14, 18, has t = 4 and √18 ≤ C ≤ 5; every tournament on at most six vertices has C = t, so seven is the least order
records.abstract: A Lean 4 development on the capacity of digraphs in the sense of Alon (1998): w(R^n) is the largest set of words of length n such that every ordered pair of distinct words has a coordinate carrying an arc from the first to the second, and C(R) is the supremum of w(R^n)^(1/n), which equals the limit; for a tournament T, t(T) is the order of its largest transitive subtournament and t(T) ≤ C(T). Conjecture 1.1 of Alon's paper, attributed to Körner and Simonyi, asserts C(T) = t(T) for every tournament; Alon disproved it with a random construction and with the Paley tournament on 67 vertices, and asked for the smallest tournament on which the equality fails. Let T7 be the subtournament of the Paley tournament on 23 vertices (x → y iff y − x is a nonzero square mod 23) induced on 0, 1, 2, 3, 9, 14, 18. Proved here: T7 is a tournament with t(T7) = 4; eighteen listed points of T7 × T7 form a transitive clique of its second Sperner power; hence, by the lift lemma (N injective points of the k-th power, each earlier one dominating each later one in some coordinate, give for every m a clique of the km-th power of size at least N^m / ((N − 1)m + 1), by words of fixed index sum), some Sperner power of T7 has a clique larger than 4^n, √18 ≤ C(T7), and t(T7) < C(T7); C(T7) ≤ 5, by an explicit rank-5 factorization over GF(2) of a matrix with nonzero diagonal and zeros on the arcs, through the rank bound (a clique of the n-th power indexes a nonsingular diagonal submatrix of the n-th Kronecker power, which factors through F^(r^n)); the general statements N^(1/k) ≤ C(R), t(R) ≤ C(R), C(R) ≤ r for any such factorization, and C(R) ≤ |V|; and, for the Paley tournament on 23 vertices, t = 5 and √29 ≤ C from a 29-point transitive clique of its second Sperner power; and every tournament on at most six vertices satisfies C(T) = t(T) (for each of the 1, 1, 1, 2, 4, 12, 56 isomorphism classes on 0 to 6 vertices, a representative with a rank-t factorization over GF(2) and a transitive t-chain, and a kernel check, by a bitset over all orientations, that every labelled tournament on at most six vertices is a relabelling of a representative), so a tournament with t < C has at least seven vertices and seven is the least order of a counterexample. The capacity is formalized in its supremum form. On paper, in the research note of the repository, with standard-library certificates: the square value 18 is exact; on seven vertices 455 of the 456 isomorphism classes have a rank-t matrix over GF(2) and the exception is T7, which is therefore the unique smallest counterexample up to isomorphism; every proper subtournament of T7 satisfies the equality; and the Paley tournament on 7 vertices has C = 3. The smallest example previously exhibited has 67 vertices (examples on 27 and 26 vertices follow from Alon's argument over GF(27) with a published value of t). Nothing in Lean is claimed about tournaments on seven or more vertices other than T7 and the Paley tournament on 23 vertices.

records.title: Finite-size mean bias of the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick free energy
records.abstract: Formalization of a fixed-temperature N^(-7/10) bound for the finite-size mean bias of the zero-field Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model with independent standard Gaussian couplings and the unnormalized partition function. For every beta > 1, a positive constant depending on beta bounds the nonnegative pressure gap for every integer N >= 2. The selected results also establish the thermodynamic limit for beta > 0, the corresponding free-energy-density and expected log-partition corrections, a positive exponent saving over 2/3, and a full-sequence little-o improvement. The independently readable interface defines the limiting pressure by a thermodynamic limit; Solution identifies it with the all-probability-profile Parisi variational value.

records.title: Matrix multiplication: omega at most 9/4 over every ring
records.abstract: An integral extension of OpenAI's matrix multiplication exponent bound and its previous all-fields extension. The formalization proves that the exact integer coefficient tensor-rank exponent is at most 9/4, yielding division-free arithmetic programs over every associative unital ring, including noncommutative rings. For every positive epsilon, one constant bounds the operation count at all positive matrix sizes by C*n^(9/4+epsilon). The arithmetic model is preserved apart from Field-to-Ring assumptions. The extension uses a primitive tensor spectrum, coefficient extraction, fixed finite-free descent, and coprime patching of Fourier and interpolation constructions. It does not improve the numerical exponent or assert an endpoint O(n^(9/4)) algorithm, efficient uniform generation, or bit complexity.

records.title: Integrability of Liouville theory: the Kupiainen–Rhodes–Vargas proof of the DOZZ formula
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the theorem of A. Kupiainen, R. Rhodes and V. Vargas (Annals of Mathematics, 2020) that the three-point structure constants of Liouville conformal field theory on the Riemann sphere are given by the DOZZ formula of Dorn–Otto and Zamolodchikov–Zamolodchikov. The structure constants are defined probabilistically: for 0 < gamma < 2, cosmological constant mu > 0 and charges satisfying the extended Seiberg bounds, C_gamma(alpha_1, alpha_2, alpha_3) = 2 mu^(-s) gamma^(-1) Gamma(s) E[rho^(-s)], where rho integrates explicit power weights against the Gaussian multiplicative chaos of the Gaussian free field pinned on the equator. The formalization proves C_gamma = C_gamma^DOZZ, expressed through the Zamolodchikov function Upsilon_{gamma/2}, at every point of the domain where Gamma(s) is finite, and at every point including the poles for the unit-volume constant; and it proves that the probabilistic reflection coefficient, built from Brownian motion conditioned to stay negative and lateral chaos, equals R^DOZZ (Theorem 3.5). The theorems hold for every model of the field and chaos, and models are constructed. All prerequisites are proved: the construction, uniqueness and moment theory of Gaussian multiplicative chaos and the extended Seiberg bounds (David, Kupiainen, Rhodes and Vargas, 2016); the BPZ equations for degenerate four-point functions and the classification of their real single-valued solutions by the Gauss hypergeometric function (Kupiainen, Rhodes and Vargas, 2019); analytic continuation of correlation functions, tail estimates for multiplicative chaos, fusion asymptotics, the shift equations and the quotient argument. Errata found in the three papers, and the places where the Lean statements differ from them, are recorded in docs/ERRATA-AND-DEVIATIONS.md.

records.title: Anomalous scaling limit of a Brownian particle in a log-correlated potential
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the paper "Anomalous scaling limit of a Brownian particle in a log-correlated potential" by Armstrong, Bou-Rabee and Kuusi: the subdiffusive scaling limit of a Brownian particle whose drift is the gradient of a log-correlated random potential (Theorem A, in its introduction form and in its precise quenched form), quantitative homogenization of the Dirichlet problem uniformly in the infrared cutoff (Theorem B), and large-scale Hölder regularity with a Liouville theorem (Theorem C), together with the supporting coarse-graining, elliptic-regularity and Markov-process theory. The theorems hold for every random environment satisfying the paper's standing assumptions (a GMCModel). The development builds on Mathlib and on the public CoarseGraining and MarkovProcess libraries. The three headline theorems are independently checked by the comparator pairs under SubdiffusiveProcessAudit/.

records.title: Zero-density estimates from an improved large-values bound
records.abstract:
Let N(σ,T) count the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function with real part at least σ and imaginary part of absolute value at most T, counted with multiplicity. For every fixed σ ∈ [1/2,1] and every ε > 0, we prove N(σ,T) ≤ Cσ,ε T^(A(σ)(1−σ)+ε) for all T ≥ 2, where

| σ interval | A(σ) |
| --- | --- |
| [1/2,9/13] | 3/(2−σ) |
| (9/13,5/7] | 18/(7σ+3) |
| (5/7,3/4] | 9/4 |
| (3/4,1] | 3/(2σ) |

The maximum of this coefficient bound is 39/17, improving the coefficient 30/13 in the Guth–Maynard bound. We also prove the separate estimate N(σ,T) ≤ Cε T^((39/17)(1−σ)+ε) for every ε > 0, simultaneously for σ ∈ [1/2,1] and T ≥ 2, with a constant independent of σ and T. The improved large-values estimate and its zero-density consequences are formalized in Lean.

records.title: Realizations and dynamics of shared-resource mass-action systems
records.abstract: Ordinary mass-action realizations are characterized for a finite family of two-species modules coupled through a shared resource and buffer. Every positive parameter vector admits a strongly connected realization of the same polynomial field. A complex-balanced realization at a prescribed positive state exists exactly when the state is stationary and two explicit local flux inequalities hold, even when arbitrary finite auxiliary complexes on the same species are allowed. An explicit endpoint sign test determines the untransported heterogeneous parameter locus, and the state criterion extends to directed transfers of both private species. A homogeneous specialization has the sharp sharing threshold v <= n/8, including equality. Global positive solutions and permanence uniform over compact sets of initial conditions are established. For d >= 1, the positive equilibrium is unique and is locally exponentially stable in the homogeneous family. Complex-balanced realizations yield global convergence, including with transport, and local exponential stability is established for the transported complex-balanced family. An exact example at d = 1/10 has three positive equilibria, two locally exponentially stable and one unstable.

records.title: Unimodality of the independence sequence of a finite forest (Erdős Problem 993)
records.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of the theorem that the independence sequence of every finite forest is unimodal: the numbers of independent sets with 0, 1, 2, ... vertices weakly increase up to some index and weakly decrease after it. This is the statement listed as Erdős Problem 993; later sources attribute the question to a 1987 paper of Alavi, Malde, Schwenk and Erdős. The first claimed proof for all finite forests is by T. Zhang and W. Li (self-archived preprints, September 2026). This repository formalizes a second proof, by W. Li, K. Vallier and T. Zhang: it adapts the public arXiv:2610.07943v1 and follows version 2.15 of that manuscript, deposited with restricted access and under revision. The Lean proof is computer-assisted and in two parts (at most 24 vertices; at least 25). About 13,700 finite computations are evaluated by the Lean kernel, without native_decide, on the three standard axioms. AI systems produced and reviewed all of the Lean; no human has read the Lean proofs. No manuscript cited is peer reviewed. No priority and no first formalization is claimed.

records.title: Michael's biquotient-map product and characterization theorems
records.abstract: Formalization of Michael (1968), Theorems 1.2 and 1.3: arbitrary indexed products of biquotient continuous surjections are biquotient, without separation assumptions; for a Hausdorff target, biquotience is equivalent to quotientness of the product with every identity map and to the same property for paracompact test spaces. The cover definition, filter and ultrafilter bridges, and an actual Hausdorff paracompact counterexample topology on the underlying target set are proved. Reverse tests use the target universe; the forward implication is separately universe-polymorphic.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: An explicit computable transcendental counterexample for Erdős Problem #206
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of a deterministic rational nested-interval construction defining a particular transcendental real x in (1/4,1/3). For this x, no strictly increasing infinite sequence of positive integer denominators is optimal among all distinct-denominator strict Egyptian underapproximations at every order from any finite starting order onward. The formalization includes the fully specified terminating construction, all prefix and polynomial enumerations, a total executable rational approximation function, and the error bound |x-q_n| <= 2^(-n-1) for every n >= 0. It also proves attainment of the best finite underapproximation values. The independent Palomar statement quantifies directly over all sequences and all competing positive increasing lists. This is a specific effective example; the measure-zero and prior existence results are not claimed as new.

records.title: Erdos607
records.abstract: Machine-checked upper bound on Erdős problem 607. For n ≥ 2 let F(n) be the number of distinct multiplicity sets A(P) that can arise from a collection P of n points of the plane, where A(P) is the set of block sizes (point counts) of the lines determined by P. The proof shows that the lines of P form a pairwise-balanced design on the n points (every pair of points lies on exactly one line, and each line contains at least two points), so A(P) is exactly the set of block sizes of such a PBD. Hence F(n) is bounded by the number of PBD profile sets on n points, and the Colbourn–Phelps–Rödl (1984) Theorem 2.4 bound exp(c·√n) on that quantity gives F(n) ≤ exp(c·√n) for every n ≥ 2. The bound is stated for n ≥ 2 — the range where the bound is meaningful (a single point determines no line) — so the hypothesis is non-vacuous. The CPR-1984 PBD bound is a published theorem and is taken as the hypothesis hCPR; it is cited, not re-proved here. Together with the Szemerédi–Trotter (1983) lattice-grid lower bound F(n) ≥ exp(c'·√n) (also cited, not re-proved), the order of growth is F(n) = exp(Θ(√n)). This repository contains zero axioms and zero sorry in the proof development (the only sorry is the deliberate statement surface in Challenge.lean).

records.title: Erdős 261: dyadic weighted representations n / 2^n = ∑ a_k / 2^(a_k)
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the solved parts, extremal bounds, and finite verification up to 10000 for Erdős problem 261 on representing n / 2^n as a finite sum ∑_{k=1}^t a_k / 2^(a_k) of distinct positive integers a_k. Proves the Borwein–Loring telescoping family n = 2^(m+1) - m - 2 (resolving Part (i) that infinitely many positive integers n admit such a representation), verifies every integer 1 ≤ n ≤ 10000 via a coalesced dyadic block certificate forest (Theorem 3.5 of Tengely, Ulas, and Zygadło 2020), constructs infinitely many rationals with at least 2^m distinct infinite representations for every m ∈ ℕ, and proves the Tengely–Ulas–Zygadło sharp extremal bound n ≤ 2^(t+1) - t - 2 and its equality uniqueness, first-term localization a_k ∈ [n+1, n+3], 2-adic last-gap divisibility 2^(a_{t+1} - a_t) ∣ a_{t+1}, the punctured-interval infinite family n_k = (2^(4k+2) + 1)/5 - 4k, and arbitrary-length splicing.

records.title: Replica symmetry breaking at arbitrary depth
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of open phases with every prescribed finite replica symmetry breaking depth in mixed even-spin Ising models at zero external field and positive temperature. The first selected result constructs strictly increasing even degrees beginning at four and a nonempty open set of positive effective covariance coefficients, with an optimizing probability measure having exactly k+1 support points. The independent statement uses concrete Gaussian Cole–Hopf recursions and comparison against all finite schemes at every competing depth. The substantive development constructs minimizers over all probability measures and includes the revised quadratic-inclusive universal transition, exact phase geometry and asymptotics, atomic Hessian, entropy, and analytic comparison results.

records.title: Fröberg's conjecture through degree 2d in sufficiently many variables
records.abstract: For every positive generating degree d, there is a variable threshold depending only on d such that, over every infinite field and for every number of general degree-d generators, the quotient polynomial ring has Fröberg's predicted Hilbert function through degree 2d. The threshold is independent of both the field and the number of generators. The prediction uses positive truncation at the first nonpositive coefficient of (1-t^d)^r/(1-t)^n. The development includes a direct construction for d at least three and a separate quadratic argument in arbitrary characteristic.

records.title: Exact robust gaps in finite open chiral chains
records.abstract: Exact worst squared spectral gaps for finite open chiral chains with inhomogeneous strong-bond lower bounds and weak-bond ratio intervals. The scalar optimum is the minimum over the ordered one-switch endpoint configurations, with a two-certificate reduction when cuts are allowed. Strictly positive weak lower bounds give a complete point-or-edge classification of scalar minimizers and an exact aligned-channel equality criterion for arbitrary complex matrix disorder. The sharp channel bound includes the finite chiral Hamiltonian spectral bridge.

records.title: Quantitative permanence and recovery with vanishing reverse rates
records.abstract: Quantitative permanence and recovery bounds are established for mass-action systems with vanishing reverse rates. For a finite weakly reversible network with rates proportional to powers of epsilon, eventual concentration bounds depend on the spread of the rate exponents, with geometric constants chosen before the individual rates. For an explicit three-species network, a prepared region admits global positive solutions with three distinct concentration scales. Every prepared solution reaches and remains in a smaller target by time (31/10)/(p^2 h^7), while an explicit prepared solution cannot enter before 400/(1313 p^2 h^7). Inventory inequalities give additional necessary restoration and depletion times from arbitrary positive initial states. A continuous reverse-exponent family retains arbitrary admitted prefactors and yields matching worst-case prepared recovery orders, together with exact common-clock transport, preparation identities and cumulative reverse-reaction bounds. Abstract constant-capacity and open-range state-dependent inventory comparisons are included without assuming monotone inventories.

records.title: Erdős Problem #824 under a smooth shifted-prime hypothesis
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of the conditional lower bound for the number h(x) of pairs of coprime positive integers a < b < x with equal sums of divisors. Assuming Hypothesis A⁺, which supplies sufficiently many primes p with smooth p+1, h(x) exceeds x^(2-ε) for every ε > 0 and all sufficiently large natural x. The argument adapts Pollack and Pomerance's finite counting method. A⁺ itself, the squarefree strengthening, and the accompanying paper's argument relying on the WD preprint are not formalized here.

records.title: Erdős 252: irrationality of the factorial divisor-sum series
records.abstract: For every natural number k, the series whose nth term is the sum of the kth powers of the positive divisors of n, divided by n factorial, is irrational. This gives the positive-exponent statement of Erdős problem 252 and also includes exponent zero. The proof combines factorial-tail integrality, a finite coprime dilation grid with exact finite-difference cancellation, and incompatible progression means obtained by a fresh-prime refinement. It has no prime-pattern conjecture or unproved number-theoretic hypothesis. The Lean development also proves convergence and the equivalence of its natural-index series with the series starting at one.

records.title: Aging in Spherical Spin Glass Dynamics
records.abstract: Lean formalization of the spherical Gaussian spin-glass dynamics and its positive-semidefinite Cugliandolo--Kurchan limit, including the physical variational response, entropy and Fisher estimates, stationary translated clusters, general-spin selection and aging bounds, and stationary relaxation. Theorem 11.4 covers every integer p >= 3 and beta > 0. The cubic product inequality includes beta = beta_d; strictly positive Fisher-cost conclusions require beta > beta_d. The root Challenge retains the original complete-conclusions theorem with the five principal theorem groups and all-spin forward theorem, sharing CK, stationary-profile, dimension-subsequence, density and Fisher-majorant witnesses. The same file separately retains the original Proposition 5.7 statement for every CK solution, every late sequence and every raw translated cluster.

records.title: Dowker's countable paracompactness, product normality and strict insertion characterization
records.abstract: Formalization of Dowker (1951), Theorem 4: normality plus ordinary countable paracompactness of an arbitrary topological space X is equivalent to normality of X times the closed unit interval, and to strict continuous insertion between arbitrary real upper and lower semicontinuous functions h<g. No T1 or Hausdorff assumption on X, boundedness or uniform gap is added. Companion compact metrizable product theorem (Lemma 3) and countable-cover/decreasing-closed-sequence equivalences (Theorem 2) are included.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: Finitely generated positive cones in F_n × Z
records.abstract: This Lean 4 formalization proves that, for every integer n at least two, the direct product of the free group of rank n with the infinite cyclic group has a positive cone generated by finitely many elements as a semigroup if and only if n is even. It formalizes Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2 of Hang Lu Su's arXiv:2608.31103v1. The even-rank construction passes a positive cone through two finite-index subgroups. The converse derives the parity obstruction from finite circle domains and their endpoint actions. The required base-cone theorem and the supporting algebraic and dynamical arguments are proved within Lean.

records.title: Erdős 1180: representing residues as sums of modular inverses with small denominators
records.abstract: A complete Lean 4 proof of Erdős problem 1180 and its quantitative variants on representing every residue modulo a prime p as a sum of at most C(ε) modular inverses n⁻¹ (mod p) with 1 ≤ n ≤ p^ε and gcd(n, p) = 1. Formalizing Glibichuk's 8-fold bilinear covering theorem via additive energy and Cauchy–Davenport together with an inductive asymmetric two-block prime-reciprocal construction, this development proves the affirmative existence theorem for all ε > 0 and all primes p, the discrete large-prime bound C_asymp(ε) ≤ 8(⌊1/ε⌋ + 1)² = (8 + o(1))ε⁻² (and ≤ 32ε⁻² uniformly on (0, 1]), the asymmetric staircase bounds C_asymp(ε) ≤ 8k(k + 1) whenever (2k + 1)ε > 2 and C_asymp(ε) ≤ 8k whenever (2k - 1)ε > k (giving C_asymp(ε) ≤ 16 for ε > 2/3 and ≤ 24 for ε > 3/5), and Shparlinski's O(ε⁻³) bound. It also proves the large-prime pigeonhole lower bound 1/ε ≤ ⌈1/ε⌉ ≤ C_asymp(ε), the small-prime exponential lower bound 2^(1/ε) ≤ 4 C(ε), the strict separation C_asymp(1/n) < C(1/n) for all n ≥ 15, and the disproof of the unthresholded all-primes optimality statement.

records.title: Sharp last-iterate bounds and extremal trajectories for constant-step gradient descent
records.abstract: Exact final-gradient bounds for convex functions with Lipschitz gradient on real Hilbert spaces, under an initial-distance bound, for every horizon and nonnegative constant step. The factor is the maximum of reciprocal linear progress and the quadratic oscillation power, with genuine smooth convex attaining examples. The formalization includes the joint progress potential, complete sampled equality trajectories in both strict branches and at balance, and a direct transfer from actual constrained proximal minimizers to sharp residual and terminal objective-residual bounds. All ten principal declarations are listed in comparator.json; VERIFICATION.md records checks.

records.title: Classical theorems of Fröhlich and Spencer: the Kosterlitz–Thouless transition, massless phases of abelian gauge theories, and Anderson localization
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of three papers of J. Fröhlich and T. Spencer (Communications in Mathematical Physics, 1981, 1982 and 1983), with the two-dimensional multiscale analysis in the finite-volume form of V. Kharash and R. Peled (2017). For the two-dimensional plane rotator it proves the Kosterlitz–Thouless transition: the two-point function decays exponentially at high temperature, while at low temperature it obeys the power-law lower bound of Theorem C and still tends to zero, so that there is no long-range order. The same multiscale expansion in charge ensembles gives the absence of screening and the power-law decay of fractional charges in two-dimensional Coulomb gases (Theorems A and B), the phase diagram of the Z_n clock models with an intermediate massless phase (Theorem 7.1), disorder bounds for the Villain model (Theorem D) and the roughening transition of the solid-on-solid model (Theorem 7.3), as well as the four finite-square theorems of Kharash and Peled. For the four-dimensional Villain U(1) lattice gauge theory at large beta it proves that the integer-valued dual gauge field has the exponential moments of a free massless field up to a renormalization of the coupling from beta to beta''(beta) with beta''/beta -> 1, in finite volume (2.93) and for every limit state along cubes; that a translation-invariant limit state has a field-strength correlation that is not summable, obtained as the limit of the finite-volume field-strength correlations, which is the paper's massless photon; the perimeter law of the Wilson loop at large beta and its area law at small beta; a perimeter law for the disorder operator of the Z_N gauge theories; and long-range order of the Villain XY model in every dimension D >= 3. For the Anderson tight-binding model on Z^nu at large disorder, or at high energy with Gaussian disorder, it proves exponential decay of the Green function with polynomially high probability, uniformly in the imaginary part of the energy (Theorem 1.2), its almost-sure decay, and the vanishing of the Kubo diffusion coefficient wherever the density of states is positive (Theorem 1.1). The FS82 statements are in finite volume or about limit points along cubes; the thermodynamic limits that the paper takes from Ginibre's inequalities are not formalized. Corrections to the printed texts are listed in the README.

records.title: Formalization of Carleson's theorem via the Lacey-Thiele approach
records.abstract: This is a Lean 4 formalization of Theorem 1.1 from the paper "Bounds for anisotropic Carleson operators" by J. Roos, which generalizes the Lacey-Thiele proof for Carleson's theorem. The classical Carleson theorem on pointwise almost everywhere convergence of Fourier series is derived as a special case.

records.title: Hilbert functions of chopped ideals of general plane points
records.abstract: Formalizes Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 5.1 of Hilbert Functions of Chopped Ideals of General Plane Points over arbitrary characteristic-zero fields: the full Hilbert function of degree-d chopped point ideals, the regular-sequence cases, the least stabilization degree, and the Expected Syzygy Conjecture.

records.title: Optimal universal 1 → 2 qubit cloning at fidelity 5/6, the universal-NOT, and asymmetric cloning
records.abstract: A Lean 4 development of the optimal universal 1 -> 2 cloning of a qubit, with every figure of merit finite: a channel from one qubit to two is a finite Kraus family K_i : C^2 -> C^2 (x) C^2 with sum K_i^* K_i = 1 (the blank qubit is fixed, so this is a 1 -> 2 map; the Choi-Kraus theorem is not proved), the two clone fidelities of a pure input psi are Re <psi| Tr_2 Lambda(psi psi^*) |psi> and Re <psi| Tr_1 Lambda(psi psi^*) |psi>, and F1-bar, F2-bar are their averages over the six Pauli eigenstates (1 +- sigma)/2, Gaussian-rational density matrices (the six states form a 2-design, the octahedron being a spherical 3-design, so these equal the Bloch-sphere averages of Gisin-Massar, as Bowdrey-Oi-Short-Banaszek-Jones 2002, (11), print for qubit maps; that equality is neither used nor claimed). Theorems, kernel-only: for every channel (F1-bar + F2-bar)/2 <= 5/6, so some unit psi has min(F1, F2) <= 5/6 (Gisin-Massar 1997, their largest-eigenvalue bound; Bruss-DiVincenzo-Ekert-Fuchs-Macchiavello-Smolin 1998 within the symmetric isotropic ansatz), proved by a six-term sum of squares in the Kraus entries; the Buzek-Hillery channel (1/6) V1 rho V1^* + (2/3) V2 rho V2^* (V1|0> = 2|00>, V1|1> = |01> + |10>, V2|0> = (|01> + |10>)/2, V2|1> = |11>; Buzek-Hillery 1996, (3.29)) is a channel whose two marginals are rho -> (2/3) rho + (1/6) Tr(rho) 1 (their (4.6); Werner 1998, (3.7)-(3.8)), so F1 = F2 = 5/6 for every unit psi (their root fidelity sqrt(5/6), p. 7); a channel with (F1-bar + F2-bar)/2 = 5/6, or with F1, F2 >= 5/6 on every unit psi, is the Buzek-Hillery channel as a map (the uniqueness under the average-fidelity criterion is proved here from the certificate; Keyl-Werner 1999 prove uniqueness under the worst-case one-clone criterion Delta_one and Werner 1998 under the global criterion; the Kraus family and the dilation are not unique, Roubert-Braun 2008), so 5/6 is the greatest t for which some channel has t <= F1(psi), F2(psi) for every unit psi, in Lean's IsGreatest form; F1-bar, F2-bar >= 1/3 for every channel, attained for the first clone by the universal NOT on it with a maximally mixed second clone (the universal-NOT bound of Buzek-Hillery-Werner 1999 and Gisin-Popescu 1999, in six-state average form); the asymmetric trade-off a b <= a(a + 2b)(1 - F1-bar) + b(2a + b)(1 - F2-bar) for every channel and all weights a, b >= 0, also with worst-case fidelities in place of the averages (the largest-eigenvalue bound of Fiurasek-Filip-Cerf 2005, Section II, in every dimension, with their conic alpha^2 + alpha beta + beta^2 = 1 written homogeneously; Hashagen 2017, (6.4a); the curve of Niu-Griffiths 1998, (6.29); the conic of Cerf, J. Mod. Opt. 2000, (2.31), and x^2 + x'^2 + x x' >= 1/4 of Cerf, PRL 2000, (6); Buzek-Hillery-Bednik 1998, (11); the full achievable region in Hashagen 2017 and Nechita-Pellegrini-Rochette 2021), proved by a sum of squares polynomial in a, b; the family (A0 rho A0^* + A1 rho A1^*)/(2(a^2 + ab + b^2)) with A0|0> = (a + b)|00>, A0|1> = a|10> + b|01>, A1|0> = a|01> + b|10>, A1|1> = (a + b)|11> (the optimal asymmetric cloner of Niu-Griffiths (4.13), Cerf, J. Mod. Opt. 2000, (2.28), Fiurasek-Filip-Cerf (19), Scarani-Iblisdir-Gisin-Acin 2005 (27)) consists of channels with marginals rho -> (1 - b^2/s) rho + (b^2/2s) Tr(rho) 1 and rho -> (1 - a^2/s) rho + (a^2/2s) Tr(rho) 1, s = a^2 + ab + b^2, so F1 = 1 - b^2/2s and F2 = 1 - a^2/2s on every unit psi, with equality in the bound at the weights (a, b), and for a, b > 0 equality holds only for that channel (proved here; Hashagen's uniqueness is within symmetrized channels); a = b is the Buzek-Hillery channel; hence the square-root form sqrt((1 - F1-bar)(1 - F2-bar)) >= F1-bar + F2-bar - 3/2 (Scarani-Iblisdir-Gisin-Acin 2005, (23)), its worst-case form, and equality along the family for a, b >= 0 (the curve of Niu-Griffiths (6.29)). For every channel 3(F1-bar + F2-bar) - 7/2 <= sqrt((3F1-bar - 1)(3F2-bar - 1)), binding also where a clone is below 1/2 (with the floor, the necessity half of Nechita-Pellegrini-Rochette 2021, Theorem 6, at d = 2 for the six-state averages; Hashagen 2017, Theorem 6.4, in entanglement fidelity), proved by a Gram identity in the Kraus entries and Cauchy-Schwarz, with equality along the family when (2a + b)(a + 2b) >= 0 and, with neither clone perfect, only there; a perfect clone on average leaves the other at 1/2 (Hashagen 2017, p. 20, via Nielsen 2002, (3)); the asymmetric bound holds for all real a, b with (2a + b)(a + 2b) >= 0, the family being its only equality case when the product is positive and a, b != 0, and at (3, -1) it is the anticloning bound 3F1-bar - 5F2-bar <= 1, attained only by asymChannel 3 (-1), at (13/14, 5/14); F2-bar = 1/3 forces F1-bar <= 5/6, and (5/6, 1/3) is attained only by asymChannel 2 (-1), on every unit psi, the Buzek-Hillery clone with its anti-clone (Scarani-Iblisdir-Gisin-Acin 2005, (12)-(15)), and likewise with the clones exchanged; if (F1-bar + F2-bar)/2 >= 5/6 - eps, the Kraus operators lie within total squared Frobenius distance 6 eps of span{V1, V2}, and ||Lambda(rho) - Lambda_BH(rho)||_F <= 200 sqrt(eps) ||rho||_F for every input rho. Forty-four compared statements over twenty fully specified definitions; the identities behind every statement are replayed in rational arithmetic in the standard library by scripts/check_cloning.py and scripts/check_extensions.py. As of 2026-10-11 no formalization of the fidelity bound, of the Buzek-Hillery marginals, of the uniqueness, of the floor or of any asymmetric trade-off was located in the Palomar registry, Mathlib, formal-conjectures, openai/math, physlib, Lean-QIT, QICLean, csd-lean4, atlas-lean, trureturing, JWang226/Cloning (asymptotic global-fidelity cloning, a different figure of merit), the Isabelle AFP, the Rocq package index or arXiv; physlib's wishlist names the 5/6 bound as wanted and csd-lean4 holds the qualitative no-cloning and no-broadcasting theorems; nor, on the same date, of the full-range or signed trade-offs, their equality cases or the stability in the Palomar registry, Mathlib, formal-conjectures, physlib, Lean-QIT, QICLean, csd-lean4, atlas-lean, trureturing, JWang226/Cloning, the Isabelle AFP or GitHub code search.

records.title: Expected syzygies and Fröberg’s conjecture through degree 2d
records.abstract: Formalizes Theorem 1.1 of Expected Syzygies and Fröberg’s Conjecture through Degree 2d: assuming the Expected Syzygy Conjecture over a characteristic-zero field, general degree-d forms have the positively truncated Hilbert function predicted by Fröberg’s conjecture in every degree through 2d. The implication holds for every positive number of variables and degree and every number of generators, with one common nonempty open set for all the stated degrees.

records.title: Optimality and uniqueness of Romik's ambidextrous sofa, formalized in Lean 4
records.abstract:
The ambidextrous moving sofa problem asks for the largest area of a connected planar shape that can be moved, from one starting position, around the right-angled corner of a hallway of unit width that turns right, and also around the corner of a hallway that turns left. Dan Romik (Experimental Mathematics, 2018) constructed a shape of area M = 1 + 4Y^2 + arctan Y = 1.64495..., where Y = 0.2980... is the positive root of 4Y^3 + 3Y = 1, and proposed it as a likely solution; in 2025 Georgiev, Gómez-Serrano, Tao and Wagner listed the problem as open.

This entry proves that Romik's ambidextrous sofa is optimal and that it is the only optimal shape. Every compact connected set that continuous rigid motions, starting in the same orientation, move through both hallways has area at most M, with equality if and only if the set is the image of Romik's sofa by a rotation and a translation. It also proves that Romik's sofa and its images by rotations and translations move through both hallways, that its area is M, that its convex hull is the convex body given by its support function, and that M is Romik's closed form (3 + 2 sqrt 2)^(1/3) + (3 - 2 sqrt 2)^(1/3) - 1 + arctan(((sqrt 2 + 1)^(1/3) - (sqrt 2 - 1)^(1/3))/2).

The proof splits the convex hull of a sofa into two caps, one for each hallway, and bounds the area of the sofa by the sum of their scores. The score of each cap is at most M/2, with equality only for Romik's cap, and when the area is M the sofa is recovered from its caps. Two steps use Jineon Baek's theorem that Gerver's sofa is optimal for the ordinary moving sofa problem (arXiv:2411.19826); its Lean formalization comes from lean4-moving-sofa and is included in the repository.

records.title: Perfect surjections and paracompactness
records.abstract: A continuous closed surjection from a Hausdorff space, with compact fibres, preserves and reflects ordinary open-cover paracompactness. The paracompact image is proved Hausdorff without assuming target separation. Supporting selected results give inverse transfer without separation or surjectivity, forward transfer to a regular target, local finiteness of images of arbitrary indexed families, and the regular-space criterion using arbitrary locally finite refinements. No metrizability, countability, local compactness or uniform fibre-size assumption is imposed. The source is based on Munkres section 41 exercise 8 and Sakai Theorem 2.6.3(a),(e); it does not claim new mathematics.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: Grötzsch's theorem, Ore's conjecture for k = 4 (Kostochka–Yancey) and the Grünbaum–Aksenov theorem
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of results on 3-colourings of planar graphs. (1) Kostochka and Yancey's theorem, the case k = 4 of Ore's 1967 conjecture on the minimum number of edges of k-critical graphs: every finite 4-critical graph G satisfies 3|E(G)| ≥ 5|V(G)| - 2, by their potential method. (2) Grötzsch's theorem: every finite triangle-free planar graph is 3-colourable, deduced from (1) as in Kostochka–Yancey, with the topological crossing argument replaced by a K5-minor argument with an apex inside a face. (3) Aksenov's and Jensen–Thomassen's theorem: a triangle-free planar graph plus one edge is 3-colourable (Borodin–Kostochka–Lidický–Yancey, Theorem 2). (4) A triangle-free planar graph plus one vertex of degree at most 4 is 3-colourable (BKLY, Theorem 4). (5) The Grünbaum–Aksenov theorem: every finite planar graph with at most three triangles is 3-colourable, following BKLY's short proof (Theorem 7), with precolouring extension for 4- and 5-cycles (BKLY Theorem 5, for arbitrary cycles) and a combinatorial region (Jordan-type) theorem for rotation systems making the interiors and outer faces of the paper precise. Planarity is defined combinatorially, by rotation systems of genus zero (Euler defect 0); as sanity checks on this definition K4 is shown planar and K5 and K3,3 non-planar.

records.title: Erdős 1105: anti-Ramsey numbers for cycles and paths
records.abstract: A complete Lean 4 proof of both parts of Erdős problem 1105 on the anti-Ramsey number AR(n, H), the maximum number of colors in a surjective edge-coloring of K_n with no rainbow copy of H. Part (i) proves the Erdős–Simonovits–Sós (1975) cycle formula AR(n, C_k) = ((k - 2) / 2 + 1 / (k - 1)) n + O(1) for every fixed k ≥ 3 (Montellano-Ballesteros and Neumann-Lara 2005; Choi 2011), together with the exact triangle value AR(n, C_3) = n - 1 and the explicit two-sided bounds ⌊n / (k - 1)⌋(choose(k - 1, 2) + 1) - 1 ≤ AR(n, C_k) ≤ ((k - 2) / 2 + 1 / (k - 1)) n - 1 for all n ≥ k ≥ 3 via private-color deletion and weak anticyclic block decompositions. Part (ii) proves the Simonovits–Sós (1984) and Yuan (2021) exact path formula AR(n, P_k) = max(choose(k - 2, 2) + 1, choose(ℓ - 1, 2) + (ℓ - 1)(n - ℓ + 1) + ε) for all n ≥ k ≥ 5, where ℓ = ⌊(k - 1) / 2⌋ and ε = 1 for odd k and 2 for even k, via representative-graph exchanges, finite host-window reduction, degree-core elimination, and 2-connected circumference bounds.

records.title: The Hajnal–Szemerédi theorem on equitable colourings
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the Hajnal–Szemerédi theorem (1970), conjectured by Erdős in 1964: every finite graph with maximum degree at most r has an equitable proper colouring with r + 1 colours, i.e. a proper colouring whose colour classes differ in size by at most one. The exact form is also proved: if the number of vertices is s(r + 1), every colour class has exactly s vertices (the colouring form of Erdős Problem #914). The proof follows the short argument of Kierstead and Kostochka (2008): induction on the number of edges; after deleting an edge, a nearly equitable colouring is repaired by moving vertices along paths of an auxiliary digraph on the colour classes (Lemma 2.1); when the large class is inaccessible, a family of terminal classes, solo edges and a discharging count with weights q/|S_z| (Lemmas 2.2–2.3) produce a recolouring that either finishes the colouring or strictly increases the number of accessible classes, using the induction hypothesis on the inaccessible part. The general case is reduced to the divisible one by adding a disjoint complete graph.

records.title: Pure infinitely self-modifying code
records.abstract: Formalizes the corrected construction of pure infinitely self-modifying code from Gregory Morse's 2018 paper. An unbounded integer-address machine simulates finite Turing machines, preserves halting and divergence, writes code at every computational instruction, and admits a run changing unboundedly many fetched code fields from a literal identity-memory initializer whose memory is proved primitive recursive. Terminal interpreter journals occur on reached halted configurations of the numbered interpreter on the encoded finite input. The development includes a four-register MOV foundation, effective finite-machine interpretation, tape and head observations, and conditional bounded x86/x64 instruction, relocation and native-trace refinements. Finite hardware is not claimed to have unbounded memory.

records.title: A lower bound of 21 for 3 × 3 matrix multiplication over every field
records.abstract: Every exact bilinear algorithm for multiplying two 3 × 3 matrices over an arbitrary field uses at least 21 products of input linear forms. The theorem includes finite and infinite fields in every characteristic. The input linear forms and output matrices are unrestricted. This is a lower bound for exact bilinear complexity, not for border rank or general arithmetic circuits. The repository contains the proof development and an interface stated entirely with ordinary Mathlib matrices and linear maps.

records.title: A uniform zero-free region for Dedekind zeta functions
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2 of A quasi-Riemann hypothesis for Dedekind zeta functions: for every number field K, its Dedekind zeta function has no zeros in Re(s) > 31/32. The formal statement asserts the existence of a holomorphic function away from 1 that agrees with Mathlib's Dedekind zeta function for Re(s) > 1 and is nonzero for Re(s) > 31/32 with s different from 1. The corollary gives the same zero-free bound for Hecke L-functions associated with finite-order Hecke characters, including s = 1 for nonprincipal characters. These characters are represented in Lean as ray class characters. This repository contains the substantive Lean development, including its Challenge and Solution.

records.title: Low-discrepancy quasi-uniform digital nets in every dimension
records.abstract:
The main theorem (thm:A, Theorem A "Every dimension", of version 1) of the manuscript "Low-discrepancy quasi-uniform digital nets in every dimension", in one statement. For every dimension s >= 3, every integer base q >= 2 all of whose prime factors are at least s - 1, and every k >= 1, the explicit digital net P^{U*_s}_{k,q} over Z/qZ with N = q^(sk) points (Definition def:Ns for the places infinity, 0, 1, ..., s-2 -- the Faure-Hammersley frame in graph form with the gauges of prop:Ns and prop:Gs -- and the design U*_s of Definition def:Ustar, whose columns are short vectors of the lattices of admissible columns, chosen level by level by Babai rounding) (1) is a (0,sk,s)-net in base q, so every cell of side q^(-k) holds exactly one point, and every point of [0,1]^s lies within Euclidean distance sqrt(s) N^(-1/s) of a net point (covering radius); (2) if q >= 5 a*_s + 4, any two distinct net points have toroidal and Euclidean distance at least (1 - a*_s/q) N^(-1/s), for every k >= 1, and for k >= 2 and q > (s-1) a*_s some two distinct points are closer than (1 - a*_s/q + (s-1)(a*_s+1)^2/q^2) N^(-1/s) (first-order sharpness of a*_s). The constant a*_s = max_c sum_{d != c} max_j |E_{d,j}[c]| of def:Ustar satisfies a*_3 = 2 and, for s >= 4, a*_s <= 2(s-1)^(3/2) (3/2)^(s-2) (s-2)!, and this explicit bound is e^(s log s + O(s)) (|log(bound) - s log s| <= 3s). So a*_s <= e^(s log s + O(s)), an upper bound only. Matching bounds of the same order N^(-1/s) for arbitrary N-point sets (the volume argument behind "optimal order") are classical and not formalized.
Comparator configuration: comparatorHeadline.json (4 compared theorems, all proved, no sorry): Z3NetA.theoremA, and three theorems showing inside the entry that the data the definitions introduce by choice are the paper's -- Z3NetA.ustarCols_spec (the columns E_{d,j} of def:Ustar exist and are unique), Z3NetA.gamma_spec (gamma_j of lem:sat(ii) exists and is unique) and Z3NetA.net_wellDefined (the reduction R_S -> Z/qZ, a solution U' of the residual problem and the coefficients beta of prop:Gs exist, and the net built from any of them is the entry's net). The Challenge (Headline/Challenge.lean) imports only Mathlib and contains verbatim copies of the 43 definitions of the proof side (Z3Net/FDefs.lean, Z3Net/ThmADefs.lean) that the statement reaches. The Solution (Headline/Solution.lean) obtains the theorem from Z3NetA.thmA of the full formalization in the same Lake project (whose single configuration comparator.json covers all compared theorems of the statement library).

records.title: Improved Sidorenko bound for hypergraph Turán densities
records.abstract: For every finite simple r-uniform hypergraph F with r >= 3 and m >= 1 edges, the Turán density is at most 1-c_r/m^((r-1)/r), where c_r=(1/(4r^2))(4/r)^(1/r)(1-1/r)^(2-2/r). The formalization proves the finite embedding argument using two potentials and the Lovász Local Lemma, constructs the extremal numbers, and proves the existence of their binomial-normalized limit by vertex deletion and double counting.

records.title: The full Nagata–Smirnov metrization theorem
records.abstract: A regular Hausdorff space is metrizable if and only if it has an open basis expressed as a countable union of locally finite families. Every layer can have arbitrary cardinality. The development proves the necessity using metric paracompactness, perfect normality from the basis, continuity of arbitrary locally finite bounded coordinates, and a compatible metric via a countable product of metric function spaces. It assumes neither second countability nor separability and includes empty spaces. This formalizes classical mathematics, without claiming new mathematics or first formalization priority.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: The sparsification theorem of Batson, Spielman and Srivastava
records.abstract: Let (Ω, μ) be a measure space and a = (a_k) a family of m square-integrable functions whose Gram matrix ∫ a a* dμ is the identity. Then for every n ≥ m there are points x₁, …, xₙ ∈ Ω and weights w₁, …, wₙ > 0 with (1 − √((m−1)/n))² I ≼ ∑ᵢ wᵢ a(xᵢ) a(xᵢ)* ≼ (1 + √((m−1)/n))² I in the Loewner order. For the counting measure on a finite set Ω this is the theorem for finitely many vectors: if v_k ∈ ℂᵐ, k ∈ Ω, satisfy ∑_k v_k v_k* = I, then for every n ≥ m there are weights s_k ≥ 0, at most n of them nonzero, with (1 − √((m−1)/n))² I ≼ ∑_k s_k v_k v_k* ≼ (1 + √((m−1)/n))² I, so a reweighted subset of at most n of the vectors is a spectral sparsifier of their sum. The original theorem of Batson, Spielman and Srivastava has the constants (1 ∓ √(m/n))²; with m − 1 in place of m, following Chkifa, Dolbeault, Krieg and Ullrich, the statements here are slightly stronger.

records.title: Fixed-dimensional separated Euclidean distances below 0.74 n squared
records.abstract: For every natural n at least 68000, the formalization constructs n injectively indexed points in the fixed Euclidean space R^458999. Distances between distinct points are at least one, distances attached to different unordered non-diagonal pairs differ by at least one, and both every pair distance and the diameter are strictly below (37/50)n^2. The dimension and threshold are explicit sufficient bounds; no optimality or independent priority review is claimed. This code-only port preserves the theorem of the cited public formalization. The full migrated build and final axiom audit have passed; the hosted sandboxed Comparator check has also passed.

records.title: Erdős 836: vertex counts and pairwise edge intersections in 3-chromatic intersecting uniform hypergraphs
records.abstract: A complete Lean 4 resolution of both parts of Erdős problem 836 (posed by Erdős and Shelah; Erdős and Lovász, 1975) on 3-chromatic intersecting r-uniform hypergraphs, together with structural bounds on the Erdős–Shelah codimension-one avoidance question. For Part (i), it formalizes Noga Alon's equitable-partition construction with (2r - 2) + C(2r - 2, r - 1) / 2 active vertices to disprove the O(r²) vertex bound for all r ≥ 2. For Part (ii), it adapts and generalizes Liam Price's minimal-blue bipartite double-counting argument to prove the universal bound r ≤ 2t + 1 when distinct edges meet in at most t vertices, establishing that every 3-chromatic intersecting r-uniform hypergraph has two distinct edges meeting in at least r/3 vertices, that linear intersecting hypergraphs are 2-colourable for r ≥ 4, and that avoiding pairwise intersection r - 1 forces minimum degree ≥ 3, degree ≥ 4 on multi-intersections, and |E(H)|, |V(H)| ≥ 9 at r = 4.

records.title: Heterogeneous Hegselmann–Krause dynamics: counterexamples to two conjectures and a theorem of Mirtabatabaei and Bullo
records.abstract: A Lean 4 development of the counterexamples of Hegarty, Ognissanti and Wedin (arXiv:2610.03229) to two conjectures and a theorem of Mirtabatabaei and Bullo on heterogeneous Hegselmann–Krause dynamics. n agents with real opinions and positive bounds r_1, ..., r_n update synchronously, x(t+1) = A(x(t)) x(t), where row i of A(y) averages uniformly over the neighbourhood N_i(y): the j with |y_i - y_j| <= r_i in the SBC model (synchronized bounded confidence) and <= r_j in the SBI model (synchronized bounded influence). Conjecture 2.2 says the proximity digraph is constant after a finite time; Conjecture 2.3 says every trajectory reaches a fixed state or is eventually pseudo-stable (the agents split into two non-empty classes, fixed at their limits or moving strictly towards them from one side); Theorem 6.4(iv) says a trajectory whose digraph is constant from some time on is eventually pseudo-stable. For the four systems of the source (SBC with seven agents and rate -1/6; SBI with seven agents and rate (1 - sqrt 5)/8; SBC with six agents; a second SBI system with seven agents) the development proves the closed form x(t) = x_inf + c lambda^t v for every t, the neighbourhood of every agent at every t (alternating with the parity of t at the middle agent of the two seven-agent alternating systems, the same at every t in the other two), convergence, and that no trajectory is ever frozen or pseudo-stable after any time towards any vector, since four agents alternate sides of their limits. Hence Conjectures 2.2 and 2.3 fail in each model, and Theorem 6.4(iv) fails in each model, both in its literal reading and in the reading that also admits a fixed state. Two smaller constant-digraph systems found in this development, five SBC agents with rate (1 - sqrt 2)/3 and six SBI agents with rate (13 - sqrt 249)/40, have one real negative mode. A five-agent SBI system of this development has a complex pair of modes: the offsets of its three moving agents follow a rational averaging map from an algebraic initial offset (the real root of a cubic), its digraph is constant, it converges, and every moving agent is strictly on both sides of its limit in every five consecutive times. So Conjecture 2.3 and Theorem 6.4(iv) fail with five agents in either model. A five-agent SBC family shows that these failures persist with positive, unequal bounds whose ratio of largest to smallest is below any 1 + epsilon. Along all four source systems the final value at constant topology (Definition 3.1) of every x(t) is the limit, and in the two constant-digraph source systems the per-step convergence factor (Definition 6.1) of every agent with nonzero offset is identically the negative rate, so it converges to no non-negative number. On the positive side, Lemma 4.2 (the equi-topology neighbourhood preserves the proximity digraph) and Lemma 4.8 (a convergent trajectory whose limit has every equi-topology distance positive eventually has the digraph of its limit, the limit as its final value at constant topology, and an equilibrium limit) are proved for arbitrary bounds; the limits of the two constant-digraph systems satisfy that hypothesis, and those of the two alternating systems violate it. For the source's two spectator systems (nine SBC agents with a spectator and two beacons; eight SBI agents with a spectator) the closed forms, the constant tables and the spectator's side are proved, and along the five-agent SBC and six-agent SBI single-mode systems too the final value at constant topology is the limit and the per-step factor is the rate. Not claimed: Theorem 6.4(iii) in full, Conjecture 2.1 (convergence of every trajectory), or that any minimality result is formalized in Lean.

records.title: Triangle-free graphs with prescribed chromatic number
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of the classical existence of finite triangle-free graphs with arbitrarily large chromatic number. For each integer k at least two, it constructs a finite simple graph whose clique number is exactly two and whose chromatic number is exactly k. The proof iterates the Mycielski construction from the complete graph on two vertices. This is the Tutte–Zykov variant recorded with Erdős problem 627, not a solution of that problem's open asymptotic limit question.

records.title: Write-Execute computation: a Lean formalization of Self-Spectre with errata
records.abstract: Formalizes Gregory Morse's 2019 paper "Self-Spectre, Write-Execute and the Hidden State": the Write-Execute half unconditionally, the Self-Spectre half as conditional theorems over an abstract speculation contract. An ideal word-level machine whose only operations are a store and a jump, with no data reads, simulates finite Turing machines step for step, preserving halting, divergence and the tape; a finite image is exact until its guard faults. The development proves the jump-table lookup, the 8-bit tables, wide ADD, SUB, SHL, SHR, XOR, 32x32 multiplication, 64/32 division, two-step modular reduction, modular exponentiation with its multiplication count, the AES-128 T-table cipher and the Write-Execute AES procedure against FIPS-197. The Self-Spectre half is proved as a conditional result under an abstract speculation contract (a branch predictor and a speculation window as parameters, rollback of the architectural state, persistence of the cache): the Fig. 1 mistraining schedule, the Fig. 2 victim leak with the mix-order reload from a cleared probe array, the speculation-depth boundary (touch trace for any cache, observable reload hits from a cleared probe array) and the hidden Write-Execute computation. Supporting byte-level x86/x64 models of Figs. 5, 6 and 7 and native vectors for the corrected C and MASM sources accompany the selected statement.

records.title: Möbius invariance of the Ramsey property for finite spherical sets
records.abstract: Theorem C: for finitely many distinct points a of the unit sphere of R^d and any L in O(1,d) (L^T S L = S with S = diag(-1, 1, ..., 1)), the configuration a is Euclidean Ramsey if and only if its image under the Möbius map phi_L is Euclidean Ramsey. There is no affine-spanning hypothesis. Ramsey is OpenAI's definition from result 172 (for every r >= 2 there is D such that every r-colouring of R^D contains a monochromatic congruent copy). Corollaries, also proved: every Möbius image of a finite set of distinct unit-sphere points with real algebraic coordinates is Ramsey; and for distinct rationals t_i and arbitrary reals k != 0 and c, the circle points circ(k t_i) and circ(t_i + c) form Ramsey sets, where circ is the stereographic chart of the unit circle. The proof builds on OpenAI's complete Lean proof of the classification of finite Euclidean Ramsey configurations (openai/math fd4aeeb2, result 172), whose 28 files are included with header-only changes for the Lean module system. The Lorentz matrix transports OpenAI's real tensor criterion; OpenAI's descent and sufficiency conclude. All theorems depend on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound only.

records.title: Selection of the electromagnetic source tensor by covariance, conservation and the exchange law
records.abstract: On a fixed flat Lorentz frame with metric diag(1,1,1,-1), sources are symmetric 4x4 tensor-valued functions of the six real components of an antisymmetric field. Twelve kernel-checked statements. Among all symmetric homogeneous quadratic sources (210 free coefficients), the six infinitesimal Lorentz covariance equations together with zero trace select the Maxwell stress (the electromagnetic energy-momentum tensor) up to a unique real scale, and a displayed certificate of 209 linear coefficient equations is equivalent to both laws. Among the same homogeneous quadratic sources, conservation alone - vanishing divergence on every source-free Maxwell/Bianchi first jet - selects the same line, with covariance, trace zero and Hodge invariance derived rather than assumed. The globally C^3 symmetric conserved sources are exactly an explicit seventeen-parameter family (constant, a six-parameter cross term, and the stress), and with covariance zero field value is equivalent to zero trace and to the stress line. Under the sourceful exchange law at current stiffness k (the real factor multiplying the jet current), every everywhere-differentiable symmetric source is a constant plus the Maxwell stress of scale exactly k, and conversely, with no polynomial, degree, C^3, covariance or trace hypothesis; zero field value selects the stress. Explicit counterexamples show that covariance and zero trace are each necessary in the quadratic selection, and that covariance and the zero-field normalization are each necessary in the C^3 selection. Uniqueness of the Maxwell stress tensor is classical (Fock 1964; Kerrighan 1982; Navarro-Sancho 2012; the classification of Maxwell conservation laws by Anco-Pohjanpelto 2001); the contribution is the constructive, kernel-checked development on the explicit register at finite regularity, with finite certificates, the covariance-free routes, and the differentiable-only sourceful statement. Pisot Dimensional Theory motivates the frame; no physical coupling is selected.

records.title: Flatness of one-homogeneous one-phase Bernoulli minimizers in dimensions at most six
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the flatness half of the main theorem of the OpenAI preprint "The critical dimension for one-phase Bernoulli minimizers" (September 24, 2026): for 1 ≤ d ≤ 6, every nonnegative, nonzero, one-homogeneous global minimizer u of the one-phase Bernoulli energy J(v; B) = ∫_B |∇v|² + 1_{v > 0} in ℝᵈ is flat, that is, u(x) = max(⟪x, e⟫, 0) for almost every x, for some unit vector e. The minimizer class is the one of Alt and Caffarelli, written out from Mathlib definitions: on every ball B, u ∈ H¹(B) and J(u; B) ≤ J(v; B) for every v ∈ H¹(B) with v − u ∈ H¹₀(B), with weak gradients and H¹₀(B) (the closure of C_c^∞(B)) defined in the statement itself. The proof follows the preprint's universal-certificate method; the classical regularity theory of one-phase minimizers that the preprint cites is proved, in this repository or its dependencies, and the classification in dimensions d ≤ 4, which the preprint cites, is proved by the same exclusion method with new certificates.

records.title: Sharp universal support criterion for sub-Gaussian laws
records.abstract: For every Borel probability law on the real line that is symmetric about zero and satisfies 0 < a <= |X| <= b almost surely, the support ratio b/a <= sqrt(3) + sqrt(2) guarantees E exp(t X) <= exp(t^2 E X^2 / 2) for every real t. The inequality is strict for nonzero t, and the actual variance is the optimal quadratic proxy. An explicit symmetric law on {-R,-1,1,R} violates the bound near zero for each larger ratio R. In the normalization 3-sqrt(6) <= X^2 <= 3+sqrt(6), the development also establishes the sharp eighth-order MGF gap with its optimal interiority coefficient, identifies the unique law with Gaussian fourth-moment contact, and proves the sharp global Wasserstein bound for the squared law at every feasible fourth-cumulant deficit, including attainment. The proof combines a convex endpoint reduction, control of the entire moment tail, exact rational Bernstein certificates, and an explicit affine transport coupling.

records.title: Smirnov's local-to-global metrization theorem
records.abstract: A space is metrizable if and only if it is Hausdorff, paracompact and locally metrizable. A reusable construction gives a sigma locally finite basis from any point-finite open cover of metrizable patches in a paracompact space, without a separation hypothesis. Local neighborhoods, the cover index and each basis layer may have arbitrary cardinality. The proof assumes no second countability, separability, local compactness or nonemptiness. Classical mathematics; no novelty or priority claim.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: The Häggkvist–Janssen bound on the list chromatic index of complete graphs
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the Häggkvist–Janssen theorem χ′ₗ(Kₙ) ≤ n: for arbitrary lists of at least n colours on the edges of the complete graph on n vertices (from an arbitrary colour type), there is a proper edge colouring, i.e. a colouring of Mathlib's line graph of ⊤, choosing every colour from the list of its edge. Orders 0 and 1 are included. The proof constructs an explicit local-rank certificate, shows by a forced-choice induction that the corresponding coefficient of an extended-star polynomial is nonzero, and applies Mathlib's combinatorial Nullstellensatz; it is an alternative presentation, not a literal translation of the article's argument.

records.title: Vizing's theorem and equitable edge colourings
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Vizing's theorem: every finite simple graph G has a proper edge colouring with Δ(G) + 1 colours, stated with Mathlib's line graph (G.lineGraph is (Δ(G) + 1)-colourable, hence χ'(G) ≤ Δ(G) + 1), proved with fans and Kempe chain exchanges. It also proves the equitable refinement: for every c ≥ Δ(G) + 1 there is a proper edge colouring with colours Fin c in which any two colour classes (including unused colours) differ in size by at most one (McDiarmid 1972), obtained by balancing a Vizing colouring with alternating-component moves that strictly decrease a square energy.

records.title: Wagner's planarity criterion and list colouring of planar and K5-minor-free graphs
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of classical results on planar graphs and graphs without a K5 minor. (1) Wagner's theorem (1937): a finite graph is planar if and only if it has neither K5 nor K3,3 as a minor. (2) Škrekovski's theorem (1998): every finite graph without a K5 minor is 5-choosable, proved along the route of Wood and Linusson, and Thomassen's theorem (1994) that every finite planar graph is 5-choosable, as a corollary. (3) DP-colouring: every finite graph without a K5 minor (Li–Wang, 2022), hence every finite planar graph (Dvořák–Postle, 2018), is DP-5-colourable. (4) Voigt's theorem (1993): an explicit planar graph on 238 vertices with lists of four colours has no proper list colouring, so 5 cannot be lowered to 4; its planarity and non-colourability are checked by kernel reduction. (5) Wagner's equivalence of the Four Colour Theorem with Hadwiger's conjecture for K5 (neither side is proved). Planarity is defined combinatorially, by rotation systems of genus zero (Euler defect 0); as sanity checks K4 is planar and K5, K3,3 are not.

records.title: A finite counterexample for strict consecutive totient patterns
records.abstract: Formalizes the finite counterexample at cutoff 826 from Proposition 1.2 of Przemek Chojecki's Consecutive Totient Patterns. With ranks assigned to positions and an inclusive cutoff, every strict length-three permutation occurs, no increasing length-four block occurs, and a decreasing length-four block does occur. Hence the largest universal length is three and decreasing is not always absent at the first non-universal length. This is a partial negative result for a specified reading of Erdos Problem 415; no novelty, asymptotic result or natural weak-order frequency result is claimed.

records.title: Distinguishing sets and measures from their planar Brownian images
records.abstract: Lean 4 formalisation of all 32 numbered statements of "Distinguishing sets and measures from their planar Brownian images" (Sascha Troscheit, arXiv:2610.16339), which asks whether two deterministic time measures on the unit interval can be distinguished almost surely from a single planar Brownian image. Rescaled correlation integrals of the time measures determine expected correlation profiles of the image measures, and profiles that differ in the limit make the image laws mutually singular, even when the time measures have the same dimension. For natural measures of self-similar sets satisfying the open set condition, renewal theory gives the profile asymptotics, a limit in the non-lattice case and a periodic non-constant limit in the lattice case, which separates lattice from non-lattice measures. Normalised neighbourhood measures of the compact Brownian image converge almost surely to the occupation measure, so the separation transfers to the laws of the compact image sets. In the two-contraction family of fixed dimension, the mean profile is real analytic and non-constant in the parameter, so each parameter is separated from all but finitely many others; for sufficiently small dimension the mean is strictly increasing and every pair of distinct parameters is separated. A homometric pair of self-similar measures with non-isometric attractors and identical profiles shows that the profile does not determine the measure. Renewal theory is proved for the self-similar laws used, and the nine headline results are stated over Mathlib alone and audited with Comparator.

records.title: Dross's theorem on fractional triangle decompositions
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Dross's theorem: every finite graph on n vertices with minimum degree at least 9n/10 has a fractional triangle decomposition, i.e. nonnegative real weights on its triangles such that every edge lies in triangles of total weight exactly one. The threshold 9/10 is the exact one of the paper. The proof follows the max-flow/min-cut approach: the existence of the weights is reduced to a flow problem, a finite max-flow/min-cut theorem (included) is applied, and every cut is bounded below by counting triangles and K4s, with a peeling reduction for heavy triangles.

records.title: The Beck–Fiala integer-making theorem
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the Beck–Fiala integer-making theorem in its rational unit-cube form: if A is a 0/1 matrix in which every column has at most t ≥ 1 ones and x ∈ [0,1]^N has rational coordinates, then x can be rounded to y ∈ {0,1}^N with |∑ᵢ A j i (y i − x i)| < t for every row j; moreover the rounding can keep every coordinate of x that is already 0 or 1. The proof is the floating-coordinates argument: while some coordinates are strictly between 0 and 1, the rows with more than t floating coordinates are fewer than the floating coordinates, so a nonzero direction keeps their sums fixed, and moving along it makes a coordinate integral; induction on the number of floating coordinates.

records.title: H2 obstruction to lifting discrete matrix representations
records.abstract: A Lean proof that a discrete matrix representation lifts across a surjective homomorphism of commutative rings with square-zero kernel exactly when its explicitly constructed second-cohomology obstruction vanishes. The proof constructs the conjugation action and defect cocycle for an abelian group extension, proves the lifting criterion, and applies it to reduction of invertible matrices. The underlying additive kernel is identified with matrices over the coefficient-ring kernel. This is classical obstruction theory motivated by DARPA Challenge 18, not a solution of its homotopy/Langlands research agenda.

records.title: Near-regular hypergraph matchings and the asymptotic triangle-packing gap
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of three results. (1) A finite nibble theorem: r-uniform hypergraphs whose degrees are at most (1+μ)d everywhere and at least (1−μ)d outside an exceptional set of at most η|V| vertices, with codegrees at most μd, have matchings with at least (1−β)|V|/r edges.
