(2) The fractional–integral triangle-packing gap is o(n²) uniformly over finite graphs: every large graph has an edge-disjoint triangle family P such that every fractional triangle packing has weight at most |P| + εn² (the triangle case of Haxell–Rödl). (3) The cover form: a fractional triangle cover of weight at most |P| + εn² exists. The proof combines a nibble with second-moment and Freedman-type concentration, a low-degree core reduction, Mathlib's Szemerédi regularity lemma with a cluster linear program rounded by explicit designs, and LP duality.

records.title: Solvability of divergence-form elliptic equations (Evans §6.2)
records.abstract:
A Lean 4 formalisation of the solvability theory of linear second-order elliptic operators in divergence form on a bounded domain,

  -div(A grad u) + b · grad u + c u = f in Ω,   u = 0 on ∂Ω,

with A uniformly elliptic and every coefficient bounded and measurable. The drift b is unrestricted and the bilinear form is in general non-symmetric. The six compared statements are the results of Evans §6.2: the Gårding inequality, existence and uniqueness of the weak solution with no drift and a nonnegative zeroth-order coefficient, the Fredholm alternative, solvability against the transpose problem, the discrete set of exceptional shifts and boundedness of the inverse. They ask only that Ω be bounded and open, and the compact embedding of H_0^1(Ω) in L²(Ω) is proved. Interior regularity at every order, the maximum principles and the Dirichlet eigenvalue sequence are also proved in the library and appear without a Comparator configuration. Built on Mathlib with only Lean's standard axioms.

records.title: CollatzPosDens
records.abstract: `CollatzPosDens` is a formal proof of the main results of *Explicit positive lower density for the Collatz Conjecture* (hexagon:2610.00249). It proves Theorem 1.3, an explicit positive density of odd starting values reaching a prescribed target $t$ with $3 \nmid t$; Remark 1.4, which replaces the odd part of $t$ by $t$ itself when $\gcd(t, 6) = 1$; and Corollary 1.2, the case $t = 1$. The Lean files were generated by AxiomProver, Axiom Math's in-house theorem proving system.

records.title: The MDS conjecture over finite fields of even order
records.abstract: A Lean 4 proof of the linear MDS conjecture for every finite field of even order. For a finite field K with an even number q of elements and 2 ≤ k ≤ q, the maximum length of a k-dimensional linear maximum distance separable (MDS) code over K is q + 2 when k = 3 or k = q − 1, and q + 1 otherwise; codes are subspaces of K^N and an MDS code is one whose minimum Hamming distance equals N − k + 1. The upper bound is proved through the correspondence between MDS codes and arcs: after puncturing and duality it suffices to exclude arcs of q + 2 vectors in K^r for 4 ≤ r ≤ q/2 + 1. A hypothetical such arc gives one plane arc together with r − 3 lifts that, with three coordinate rows, form r linearly independent vectors; the formalization proves that all lifts of a plane arc lie in one common subspace of dimension at most r − 1. The proof uses an exactly normalized form of Segre's envelope of the tangents, a characteristic-two derivative obstruction, and a dimension bound for a colon ideal of (X^n, Y^n, Z^n) with n = q/2. Extended Reed–Solomon codes and the regular hyperoval show that the bound is attained.

records.title: Localized two-eigenvalue bound for finite noncomplete graphs
records.abstract: For every finite noncomplete simple graph with at least two vertices, the sum of the squares of its two largest ordered adjacency eigenvalues is bounded by the sum over unordered edges of 2(1-1/c(e)), where c(e) is the largest clique containing the edge. The proof establishes the concrete edge-clique scalar certificate and transfers it through the checked BN completely positive spectral lift. Connectedness is unnecessary.

records.title: Perfect images of metrizable spaces
records.abstract: Every continuous closed surjection with compact fibers from an arbitrary metrizable space has a metrizable codomain. A new uniform shrinking-star estimate for compact-fiber metric neighborhoods constructs a sigma locally finite open basis on the image. A proper-map formulation and an actual compatible metric are included. No second countability, separability, compact domain, local compactness, completeness, finite-fiber or nonemptiness assumption is made. Target separation is derived. Classical mathematics; no novelty or priority claim.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: The crystallographic restriction in every dimension: GL(N, ℤ) has an element of order m if and only if ψ(m) ≤ N
records.abstract: A Lean 4 development of the crystallographic restriction in every dimension. For a positive integer m let psi(m) be the sum of phi(p^k) over the prime powers p^k exactly dividing m, except that the prime power 2 contributes 0 (phi is Euler's totient; psi(1) = psi(2) = 0, psi(3) = psi(4) = psi(6) = 2, psi(ab) = psi(a) + psi(b) for coprime a, b; OEIS A080737). Theorem (Vaidyanathaswamy 1928; Hiller 1985; a proof in Kuzmanovich-Pavlichenkov 2002; Theorem 1 of Bamberg-Cairns-Kilminster 2003): for N >= 1, the group GL(N, Z) of invertible integer N x N matrices has an element of order m >= 1 if and only if psi(m) <= N. The development proves both directions: necessity through the minimal polynomial of the matrix over Q, which divides X^m - 1 and is therefore a product of distinct cyclotomic polynomials whose indices have least common multiple m, so that psi(m) is at most its degree; sufficiency by one block of size phi(p^k) for each prime power p^k != 2 of m (multiplication by the root on Z[X]/(Phi_{p^k}) in its power basis), the sign -1 when m is 2 modulo 4, and an identity block. Corollaries: the finite orders of GL(N, Z) are the positive m with psi(m) <= N; the least dimension carrying an element of order m is psi(m), or 1 for m = 2 (OEIS A152455); GL(phi(n), Z) has an element of order n for every n >= 1; the same equivalence holds for GL(N, Q); GL(0, Z) has only the order 1 and the finite orders grow with the dimension; GL(N + 1, Z) has the same finite orders as GL(N, Z) for even N >= 2; the set of finite orders is finite and bounded by 2^(N + 1). The arithmetic of psi: psi(m) = 0 iff m <= 2; psi(p^k) = phi(p^k) for a prime power p^k != 2; additivity on coprime factors; psi <= phi; psi is even; psi as a sum over the exact prime-power divisors; m <= 2^(psi(m) + 1). The tables of finite orders for N = 1, ..., 12 (OEIS A080738) and the largest finite order 2, 6, 12, 30, 60, 120, 210 in dimensions 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12 are proved by the bound and a kernel computation of psi. Beyond dimension 12, the eleven orders 2520 (psi = 20), 2310 (psi = 22) and 2184, 2340, 2640, 2730, 2772, 3080, 3960, 4620, 5040 (psi = 24), which rows 20, 22 and 24 of Table 1 of Bamberg-Cairns-Kilminster omit, are checked with their least dimensions. The same equivalence holds in SL(N, Z) for N >= 2 (an element of odd order has determinant 1; the block for 2^k, k >= 2, has even size and determinant 1; -A keeps the determinant in even dimension), and SL(1, Z) is trivial. Every even number is psi(m) for an odd squarefree m (Proposition 3(2) of Bamberg-Cairns-Kilminster and its proof), so for N, M >= 1 the finite orders of GL(N, Z) are among those of GL(M, Z) iff N / 2 <= M / 2 (integer division); each A in GL(N, Z) of finite order m preserves a symmetric integral form, positive definite on integer and real vectors (the proof takes sum_{k<m} (A^k)^T A^k), so psi(m) <= N is also the condition for an element of order m of GL(N, Z) preserving a positive definite integral form; and GL(N, Z) has an element of order m >= 1 and determinant -1 iff m is even and psi(m) + 1 <= N, so the least such dimension is psi(m) + 1 for even m (also over Q). The hypotheses N >= 1 and m >= 1 are necessary and explicit: GL(0, Z) is trivial while psi(2) = 0, and orderOf is 0 at infinite order. The theorem is the standard description of the finite orders of integer matrices, used in the crystallography of higher-dimensional lattices and quasicrystals and in integral representation theory; Mathlib's docs/1000.yaml (Q3527223) and mathlib4 issue #6091 (item 60) list it unformalized, and as of 2026-10-09 no formalization in every dimension, in either direction, was located in the registry, Mathlib, the Lean repositories searched, the Isabelle AFP or arXiv. Not claimed: priority for the two- and three-dimensional cases (public Lean proofs of the case N = 2 exist), the wallpaper or space groups, the isometry group of a given lattice or form, or integral conjugacy.

records.title: Kuratowski's theorem
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Kuratowski's theorem: a finite graph is planar if and only if it contains no subdivision of K5 and no subdivision of K3,3. Planarity is the combinatorial notion (a rotation system of genus zero). The proof combines Wagner's minor characterization (from the author's planarity library) with three new lemmas: a subdivision of any finite graph H gives H as a minor; a K3,3 minor gives a K3,3 subdivision; a K5 minor gives a K5 or a K3,3 subdivision. The last two rest on joining up to four terminals inside a connected branch set to one centre or to two adjacent centres by internally disjoint paths.

records.title: Kőnig's theorems and Dilworth's theorem
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Kőnig's edge-colouring theorem: the line graph of a finite bipartite graph G is Δ(G)-colourable, and its chromatic number (the chromatic index of G) equals Δ(G). The proof colours edges one at a time with partial proper edge colourings, recolouring by an a/b Kempe-chain swap whose correctness rests on a parity argument in the bipartite graph; the lower bound comes from the edges at a vertex of maximum degree, which are pairwise adjacent in the line graph. Also formalized: the Kőnig–Egerváry theorem (a finite bipartite graph has a matching and a vertex cover of the same size, via Hall's theorem with deficiency, plus weak duality for all finite graphs), Dilworth's theorem (an antichain A and a partition into |A| chains, by Galvin's induction) and Mirsky's dual theorem (a chain C and a partition into |C| antichains, by the height function).

records.title: Menger's theorem and Hamiltonian cycles
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Menger's theorem for finite graphs (set form with a minimum separator and as many vertex-disjoint paths, two-vertex form, edge form for Mathlib's IsEdgeReachable, and the global edge form for Mathlib's IsEdgeConnected) and of classical sufficient conditions for Hamiltonian cycles: the Bondy–Chvátal closure step, Ore's and Dirac's theorems, and the Chvátal–Erdős theorem (k-connected with independence number at most k implies Hamiltonian), whose proof uses Menger's theorem through the fan lemma.

records.title: Classical bounds for graph Ramsey numbers
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the classical bounds for graph Ramsey numbers: R(3, 3) = 6 (every graph on six vertices has a triangle or three independent vertices, and the pentagon has neither), the Erdős–Szekeres upper bound R(s, t) ≤ C(s + t − 2, s − 1), and Erdős's lower bound R(k, k) > 2^(k/2) for k ≥ 3, proved by a union bound over the edge sets of graphs on n vertices.

records.title: Mader's theorem and Hadwiger's conjecture for t ≤ 4
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Mader's theorem (a nonempty finite graph of average degree at least 2^(r−2) has a K_r minor), of Dirac's lemma (a graph without a K4 minor has a vertex of degree at most two, hence at most 2n − 3 edges for n ≥ 2), and of Hadwiger's conjecture for t ≤ 4 (graphs without a K3 minor are 2-colourable, graphs without a K4 minor are 3-colourable). Minors are branch-set models.

records.title: Elliptic curves of exact ranks five, six, and seven: conditional formalization
records.abstract: Lean proves that the finite-complexity affine-linear prime asymptotic implies infinitely many geometric isomorphism classes of rational elliptic curves of each exact Mordell–Weil rank five, six, and seven. The generic analytic theorem is an explicit hypothesis. The specialization checks, two-isogeny descent, exact rank calculations, and passage to infinitely many j-invariants are formalized; the prime asymptotic is not proved in Lean here.

records.title: Brooks' theorem
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Brooks' theorem: for k ≥ 3, a finite graph of maximum degree at most k without a (k+1)-clique is k-colourable (no connectedness assumption), and a finite connected graph that is neither complete nor an odd cycle is colourable with as many colours as its maximum degree. The proof uses greedy colourings in Lovász's style and an induction on the number of edges with a separation-and-gluing step.

records.title: Petersen's theorem
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Petersen's theorem: a finite 3-regular graph in which no edge is a bridge has a perfect matching; moreover, every edge of such a graph lies in some perfect matching. Both statements are derived from Tutte's theorem (in Mathlib) by counting the edges that leave the odd components.

records.title: Formalization of a sharp cone square-function estimate via superorthogonality
records.abstract:
This is a Lean 4 formalization of Theorems 1.1 and 1.4 from the paper "Diameter-free reverse inequalities and superorthogonality" by A. Cushman, C. Demeter and S. Wu.
Theorem 1.1 is a reverse square-function estimate in L^4 under a superorthogonality hypothesis that is weaker than the Type IV superorthogonality of Gressman-Pierce-Roos-Yung.
Theorem 1.4 applies a similar estimate to the three-dimensional light cone, yielding a refinement of the reverse cone square-function estimate of Guth-Wang-Zhang.

records.title: Hilbert–Smith and p-adic exclusion with second countability
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of the Hilbert–Smith statement for a second-countable locally compact Hausdorff topological group acting continuously and faithfully on a connected, Hausdorff, second-countable, finite-dimensional topological manifold. The conclusion gives a smooth real Lie-group structure for the group's existing topology. The development also proves p-adic exclusion for second-countable manifolds and provides universe-polymorphic versions. No second-countability hypothesis is dropped.

records.title: Continuum hypothesis independence: a Flypitch reproduction
records.abstract: An attributed adaptation of the Flypitch formal proof of two-sided syntactic independence of the continuum hypothesis from its explicitly encoded first-order ZFC theory. Cohen and collapse Boolean-valued models, together with soundness, establish that neither the encoded CH sentence nor its negation is derivable. The development uses an expanded language with definable set operations, collection and Zorn's lemma. It does not supply a formal translation to membership-only ZFC or determine the truth of CH for the ambient Lean reals. This is a reproduction of established work, not a new mathematical solution.

records.title: Counterexamples to the restricted-sumset inverse theorem in arXiv:2609.10148v2
records.abstract: Explicit finite counterexamples to Theorem A (Theorem 3.1) and Lemma 3.2 of Li and Liang, arXiv:2609.10148v2. In Z/13Z, sets of sizes seven and four satisfy all size hypotheses and have restricted sumset size nine, but neither is an arithmetic progression. A separate example in Z/11Z contradicts the lower bound of Lemma 3.2 as stated.

records.title: Depth-labeled interpolation and substitution in Sacchetti's modal logics
records.abstract: Classifies depth labelings in the modal logics wGL_n for positive n. Every simultaneous formula-valued substitution indexed by atom and depth label preserves theoremhood exactly when the labels satisfy c(k+n)=c(k) at every positive depth k. The interpolation equivalences identify the corresponding labeled property with its ordinary interpolation property and the same periodicity condition; the ordinary interpolation theorems remain explicit inputs. Further results classify period spectra, boxed-atom implications and composition of depth substitutions, and transfer a supplied ordinary interpolant while preserving syntax-tree node count and modal depth.

records.title: Erdos 99 Partial Solution
records.abstract: A formalization of a partial solution to Erdos Problem 99. It shows that Erdos Problem 99 holds for all sufficiently large n where h(n) is finite. Here, h(n) denotes the number of incongruence, diameter-minimizing sets of minimum separation at least 1.

records.title: Berge's theorem and the Tutte–Berge formula
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Berge's augmenting path theorem (a matching is maximum if and only if there is no augmenting path) and of the Tutte–Berge formula (the maximum size of a matching is the minimum over vertex sets U of (|V| + |U| − odd(G − U)) / 2), with the weak inequality for all matchings and vertex sets; the formula is derived from Mathlib's Tutte theorem by adding universal vertices.

records.title: Connected counterexamples to the exact color-critical two-eigenvalue bound
records.abstract: For F=K5 minus one edge, a color-critical graph of chromatic number four, the graph formed from K(s,s,s) and K4 by one bridge is connected and F-free for every integer s at least three. It has 3s squared plus 7 edges, and the sum of squares of its two largest ordered adjacency eigenvalues exceeds 4m/3 by at least (656s squared-1366s+62)/(3(37s-1) squared)>0. The family has arbitrarily large edge counts, refuting the exact assertion in KKP Conjecture 1.16 and Li–Liu–Zhang Conjecture 5.4.

records.title: Finite Observations and Recognition of the Compact Albert Algebra
records.abstract:
Let J=H_3(O), the real algebra of 3×3 Hermitian matrices over the division octonions, with product a∘b=(ab+ba)/2 and diagonal trace T. A frame p=(p_0,p_1,p_2) consists of trace-one elements satisfying p_i∘p_i=p_i, p_i∘p_j=0 for i≠j, and p_0+p_1+p_2=1. For frames p,q,r, record the 27 pair traces T(p_i∘q_j), T(q_j∘r_k), T(r_k∘p_i), and 27 triple traces T((p_i∘q_j)∘r_k), for i,j,k∈{0,1,2}. How much do these traces determine?

Each trace list in some open neighborhood of the data with pair entries 1/3 and triple entries 1/9, in a fixed twenty-dimensional chart, determines exactly two equivalence classes. Equivalence means one product-and-trace-preserving real linear bijection acting on all nine labeled elements, without relabeling. The sign of the degree-nine scalar Phi distinguishes the classes. With x=p_2−p_0, y=q_2−q_0, z=r_2−r_0, define

B(a,b) = T(a∘b),
U_a(b) = 2a∘(a∘b)−(a∘a)∘b,
Phi(x,y,z) = B((U_x U_y−U_y U_x)z,U_z(x∘y)).

Phi's derivative uses Glennie's degree-eight vector polynomial.

For arbitrary x,y,z∈J, Phi≠0 implies that 1,x,y,z generate J.

Recognition starts from a homogeneous cubic N on finite-dimensional real normed E, with N(e)=1 and g_e=−(1/3)D²(log N)_e positive definite on all E. A supplied linear equivalence ker(DN_e)≃ker T (the trace-zero subspace), matching g_e to B/3 and full vector-valued curvature tensors, yields an Albert algebra equivalence.

Consider 27 fixed parenthesized products of a distinguished element and three chosen elements in a real inner-product space with bilinear multiplication. Exact matching with the Albert table of pairwise inner products, inner products of products with these expressions and full ambient squared product norms determines a unique isometric, product-preserving linear embedding of J onto the subspace they generate under products and linear combinations, preserving the distinguished element and chosen elements.

Further results give error bounds. All project exposition and Lean code are AI-generated under Robert MacGregor's direction. Robert is a non-mathematician and welcomes mathematical collaboration: macgregor@gmail.com. No novelty is asserted.

records.title: Finite quantum designs: mutually unbiased bases, SIC-POVMs, and the Welch and Gerzon bounds
records.abstract: A Lean 4 development of two structures of finite-dimensional quantum information, in the vocabulary of google-deepmind/formal-conjectures (Open Quantum Problems 13 and 23; the fourteen definitions restated character for character under their Apache-2.0 license, see NOTICE). A basis of C^d is a unitary matrix whose columns are the basis vectors; two bases U, V are mutually unbiased when every entry of U^* V has squared norm 1/d; HasMUBs d k says k pairwise unbiased bases exist and IsMaxMUBCount d k that k is the largest such number. Theorems: for d >= 2, HasMUBs d m implies m <= d + 1 (Wootters-Fields 1989; Bandyopadhyay-Boykin-Roychowdhury-Vatan 2002, Theorem 3.5: the identity and the m(d - 1) traceless combinations of the rank-one projectors are pairwise orthogonal in the d^2-dimensional matrix space), and the hypothesis is sharp since in dimension 1 every two bases are unbiased; restriction to subfamilies; the tensor bound HasMUBs m k and HasMUBs n k imply HasMUBs (m n) k (Klappenecker-Rötteler 2004, Lemma 3) and its corollary over the factorization (HasMUBs d k whenever k <= q + 1 for every exact prime-power divisor q of d), hence three mutually unbiased bases in every dimension d >= 2; for a finite field F of odd characteristic and size q, the standard basis and the q bases with entries psi(a x^2 + b x)/sqrt q (psi a nontrivial additive character) are q + 1 mutually unbiased bases (Klappenecker-Rötteler, Theorem 2), through the identity |sum_x psi(c x^2 + e x)|^2 = q for c != 0 proved by Weyl differencing; for q = 2^n the bases with entries i^(x^T S_a x) (-1)^(b . x)/sqrt q, S_a the {0, 1}-lifted Gram matrix of the trace form (x, y) -> Tr(a x y) of the field with 2^n elements (an equivalent form of the Galois-ring bases of Klappenecker-Rötteler, Theorem 3), through the mod-4 identity Q(x + y) = Q(x) + Q(y) + 2 x^T S y and the nondegeneracy of the trace form; so IsMaxMUBCount (p^k) (p^k + 1) for every prime power, HasCompleteMUBs d iff IsMaxMUBCount d (d + 1) for d >= 2, and the values 3, 5, 9 in dimensions 2, 4, 8 also by explicit kernel-checked tables. Weiner's gap (Weiner 2013, Corollary 3.4): any d mutually unbiased bases of C^d extend, by one more basis, to a complete set of d + 1, the given bases keeping their places, for every d (and in the existence form, HasMUBs d d implies HasCompleteMUBs d), by Weiner's proof with its operator-algebra steps written out. The orthogonal projection Phi onto the matrices with a constant diagonal in every one of the d bases has a Kraus form X -> sum_i K_i^* X K_i whose operators K_i have constant diagonals themselves (Weiner's Lemma 3.2, through his Lemma 2.1, sum_k A_k^* X A_k = Tr(X) 1 for an orthonormal basis A_k of the matrix space, recalled there from Werner 2001); at a fixed point X the Kadison-Schwarz defect sum_i K_i^* X^* X K_i - Phi(X)^* Phi(X) is the sum of the squares (X K_i - K_i X)^* (X K_i - K_i X) and has zero trace, so the K_i commute with one another and with their adjoints (in place of the Schwarz inequality and the multiplicative-domain theorem of Choi 1974 that the paper's Lemma 3.1 uses); and the rank-one projectors of a common eigenbasis of the K_i are fixed by Phi, hence have constant diagonals, hence are unbiased to every basis of the family. Corollaries: k >= d bases give a complete set; for d >= 2, d is never the maximal number (in particular mu(6) != 6), and the maximal number is d + 1 or below d. The maximal number mu(d): two bases in every dimension; HasMUBs (p^k) m iff m <= p^k + 1; mu(d) is unique, exists for d >= 2 and lies in [3, d + 1], and does not exist for d = 1; formal-conjectures' mutuallyUnbiasedBases_dim6_bounds, 3 <= mu(6) <= 7, left with sorry there. Reconstruction (Scott 2006, eq. (9)): a complete set of d + 1 bases determines every matrix, X = sum_{s,l} Tr(X P_{s,l}) P_{s,l} - Tr(X) 1 with P_{s,l} the projector onto column l of basis s (after Ivanović 1981 and Wootters-Fields 1989), and so does a SIC family, X = sum_i ((d + 1) Tr(X P_i) - Tr X)/d P_i (its projectors are linearly independent, Renes-Blume-Kohout-Scott-Caves 2004, section II). Second moments (Klappenecker-Rötteler 2005, Theorems 3 and 5; Renes-Blume-Kohout-Scott-Caves 2004, p. 4; Scott 2006, eq. (8)): for all matrices X, Y, sum_{s,l} Tr(X P_{s,l}) Tr(Y P_{s,l}) = Tr(XY) + Tr X Tr Y for a complete set and (d + 1) sum_i Tr(X P_i) Tr(Y P_i) = d (Tr(XY) + Tr X Tr Y) for a SIC family; hence the data Tr(X P_{s,l}), and the SIC-POVM outcomes Tr(X P_i)/d with the factor d(d + 1), give ||X||_HS^2 + |Tr X|^2, the Hilbert-Schmidt distance of two matrices with equal traces, and the purity Tr(rho^2) of a Hermitian rho with Tr rho = 1 (Larsen 1990, not read, as stated by Wu-Yu-Mølmer 2009; Scott 2006, eqs. (32), (36), (55)). A SIC family in C^d is d^2 unit vectors with pairwise squared overlap 1/(d + 1); HasSICPOVM d says one exists. Theorems: N unit vectors of C^d with one squared overlap c != 1 on every pair satisfy N <= d^2 (the absolute bound of Delsarte-Goethals-Seidel 1975, the complex form of Gerzon's bound; the rank-one projectors are linearly independent), and with c = 1 the family may be any length; for d >= 2, d^2 such vectors have c = 1/(d + 1) and resolve the identity, sum_i (1/d) |phi_i><phi_i| = 1, so every SIC family is a POVM (Renes-Blume-Kohout-Scott-Caves 2004), HasSICPOVM d holds iff C^d has d^2 equiangular unit vectors, and a family at the SIC angle has at most d^2 members; Welch's bound (Welch 1974, the bound for k = 1, in the frame-potential form of Benedetto-Fickus 2003): N unit vectors of C^d have sum_{i,j} |<phi_i, phi_j>|^2 >= N^2/d, by the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for the identity and the frame operator in the matrix space; hence N >= 2 unit vectors with one squared overlap c on every pair have c >= (N - d)/(d (N - 1)), pairwise squared overlaps at most alpha with alpha d < 1 give N (1 - alpha d) <= d (1 - alpha) (the relative bound), and at most d^2 unit vectors have every pairwise squared overlap at most 1/(d + 1). Welch's equality case (Mixon-Needham-Shonkwiler-Villar, Proposition 1 and its proof): sum_{i,j} |<phi_i, phi_j>|^2 - N^2/d = ||S - (N/d) 1||_HS^2 for the frame operator S = sum_i |phi_i><phi_i|, so equality holds exactly for a tight frame; at equality in the relative bound every pairwise squared overlap is alpha and S = (N/d) 1 (Strohmer-Heath 2003, Theorem 2.3); d^2 unit vectors with every pairwise squared overlap at most 1/(d + 1) are a SIC family, and HasSICPOVM d holds iff such vectors exist; and pairwise squared overlaps at most 1/(d + 1) + epsilon give ||S/d - 1||_HS^2 <= (d^2 - 1) epsilon for d >= 1, a bound on the resolution of the identity only. SIC-POVMs exist in dimensions 2 (the tetrahedron), 3 (the Hesse configuration), 4 (the sixteen Weyl-Heisenberg translates of Appleby's exact fiducial, Appleby 2005, eq. (149), credited there to Zauner and to Renes et al.; covariance reduces the 240 overlaps to fifteen, proved by exact trigonometric and radical identities in cos(pi/8), sin(pi/8) and sqrt(2 + sqrt 5)) and 8 (Hoggar's 64 lines: the orbit of (-1 + 2i, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1)/sqrt 12 under the three-qubit Pauli group, Jedwab-Wiebe 2015, Example 4, checked by the kernel over all ordered pairs). Sixty compared statements, kernel-only. As of 2026-10-10 no formalization of the general bound, of the prime-power constructions, of the factorization corollary, of the complex absolute bound with its equality case, of Weiner's gap for general d, of Welch's bound, of the two reconstruction formulas for every matrix or of a SIC-POVM in dimension 4 was located in the Palomar registry, Mathlib, formal-conjectures, openai/math, physlib, the other Lean repositories searched, the Isabelle AFP, the Rocq package index or arXiv; none of the second moment of a SIC family with its norm, distance and purity forms, of Welch's deficit with its equality case, of the equality case of the relative bound, of the SIC family from d^2 vectors at or below the SIC angle or of the frame-defect bound was located in the Palomar registry, Mathlib, formal-conjectures, openai/math, physlib or the-omega-institute/trureturing. Read 2026-10-14, after that search: marozols/SIC-existence (public 2026-10-09, Lean v4.34.1, self-assessed, unregistered) states SICs in every dimension and, in RSIC.lean, the N = d^2 equality case, in its own vocabulary, so a dimension-4 SIC and that equality case exist elsewhere in Lean; the statements here are over formal-conjectures' definitions and were proved independently. The neighbours: the dimension-2 MUB case is formal-conjectures' mutuallyUnbiasedBases_dim2; the dimension-6 projector bound and the Kronecker lemma are in the XC0R fork of formal-conjectures (adapted here, see NOTICE); the dimension-2 and 3 SIC overlaps are in zblore/csd-lean4; the-omega-institute/trureturing kernel-checks the same 64 Hoggar vectors and the Hesse SIC in its own vocabulary, proves that the trace pairings with a complete family of rank-one contexts determine every matrix, proves the density-matrix formula under an assumed completeness hypothesis, and proves the second moment of a complete set in operator form with the purity identity for density matrices (complete_context_collision_conservation, 2026-08-28); openai/math holds mu(6) <= 5 and Weiner's gap at d = 6 (six_extend_to_seven), with lemmas for general n (commutator_trace_identity, commute_of_kraus_fixed, exists_joint_projection_basis) that make the same elementary move as the route here, the Schwarz defect of a Kraus map as a sum of squared commutators; the Kadison-Schwarz inequality for Kraus and completely positive maps is in physlib, QuAIR/Lean-QIT and kencyke/quantum-system. Not claimed: anything about dimension 6 beyond 3 <= mu(6) <= 7 and mu(6) != 6 (openai/math holds mu(6) <= 5), SICs in dimensions 5 to 7, that a family near the SIC angle is close to a SIC family, any first formalization.

records.title: The Gallai–Hasse–Roy–Vitaver theorem
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the Gallai–Hasse–Roy–Vitaver theorem: if an orientation of a finite graph has no directed path on more than k vertices, the graph is k-colourable; and conversely every k-colourable graph has such an orientation. Hence the chromatic number is the minimum over orientations of the number of vertices of a longest directed path.

records.title: Euler's theorem on Eulerian circuits and trails, and Petersen's 2-factor theorem
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the classical characterization of Eulerian graphs and of Petersen's 2-factor theorem, for finite simple graphs. (1) Euler–Hierholzer: a finite connected graph has an Eulerian circuit if and only if every vertex has even degree, and the circuit can start at any prescribed vertex. (2) Eulerian trails: a finite connected graph has an Eulerian trail if and only if it has 0 or 2 vertices of odd degree; when the odd vertices are exactly a and b, there is an Eulerian trail from a to b. (3) Eulerian orientations: if every degree is even, the edges can be oriented so that every vertex has equal in- and out-degree. (4) Petersen's 2-factor theorem (1891): every finite 2k-regular graph is the edge-disjoint union of k spanning 2-regular subgraphs. The proof of (4) is built on (1)–(3): the graph is decomposed into edge-disjoint closed trails (using the closed-trail lemma behind the Euler theorems), oriented along them, and the resulting k-regular digraph is split into k permutations by Hall's marriage theorem; each permutation yields a 2-factor. Mathlib already contained the necessity directions of (1) and (2); their sufficiency directions were listed there as open TODO items.

records.title: Graphic sequences: the Erdős–Gallai and Havel–Hakimi theorems
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the two classical characterizations of degree sequences of finite simple graphs: the Erdős–Gallai theorem (a non-increasing sequence is graphic if and only if its sum is even and every initial segment satisfies the Erdős–Gallai inequality) and the Havel–Hakimi theorem (a non-increasing sequence is graphic if and only if its first term is at most the number of remaining terms, the next d₀ terms are positive, and the reduced sequence is graphic).

records.title: Algebraic points on a circle plus at most three arbitrary points are Euclidean Ramsey
records.abstract: Theorem B(b): finitely many distinct points on a circle in the Euclidean plane (centre and radius arbitrary reals), all of whose coordinates are algebraic over Q except for the points with indices in a set T of at most three, form a Euclidean Ramsey configuration. Ramsey is OpenAI's definition from result 172 (for every r >= 2 there is D such that every r-colouring of R^D contains a monochromatic congruent copy). The theorem is stated in OpenAI's vocabulary and again in Mathlib vocabulary (Mathlib's Congruent). With the Möbius invariance of the Ramsey property (mobius-ramsey, Theorem C; the combination is by hand), it shows that every set in the class of Theorem A.10 of the appendix of Pálvölgyi's arXiv:2609.23327 is Ramsey; A.10 shows only that his derivation certificates cannot prove such sets non-Ramsey, and leaves their Ramsey status open. Proof: for at most six points, the six-concyclic-points theorem (prior work of JD-Jones-ASES, here with OpenAI's proved sufficiency); otherwise three algebraic points make the circle algebraic, a translation, rational rotation and scaling normalize it, and an explicit certificate (the separability idempotent of the number field of the algebraic points times a graph form through three points containing the exceptional ones) proves OpenAI's field criterion, after which OpenAI's sufficiency theorem concludes. The proof builds on OpenAI's complete Lean proof of the classification (openai/math fd4aeeb2), whose 28 files are included with header-only changes for the Lean module system. All theorems depend on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound only. Provenance: this repository is a port, to the Lean module system and Lean v4.35.0-rc2, of a Lean proof already public as rope AV5 of spherical-ramsey v1.1.0 (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23396387; a rope there is a self-contained Lean project checked by Comparator), with the same statements and proofs; it packages that one theorem as a standalone, Comparator-checked repository at a current toolchain (docs/PORT-LOG.md).

records.title: The Cauchy–Binet formula, Kirchhoff's matrix-tree theorem and Cayley's formula
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the Cauchy–Binet formula for determinants of products of rectangular matrices over commutative rings (not in Mathlib), of Kirchhoff's matrix-tree theorem (the number of spanning trees of a finite graph is any principal cofactor of Mathlib's Laplacian matrix), and of Cayley's formula (n^(n−2) labelled trees on n ≥ 1 vertices), derived from the matrix-tree theorem for the complete graph.

records.title: The augmented Descartes theorem in every dimension, its converses, and Soddy's two spheres
records.abstract: A Lean 4 development of Section 3 of Lagarias, Mallows and Wilks, Beyond the Descartes circle theorem (Amer. Math. Monthly 109 (2002) 338-361), in the Lorentz form. An oriented sphere in R^n with centre x and signed radius r has the augmented curvature-centre row (|x|^2/r - r, 1/r, x/r); an oriented hyperplane <h, y> = delta with unit normal h has the row (2 delta, 0, h) (LMW Definition 3.2, (3.7)-(3.9)). Tangency is distance-encoded in LMW's oriented sense: two spheres dist^2 = (r + s)^2 (external tangency for two positive radii, internal when one radius is negative), a sphere and a hyperplane <h, x> - delta = -r, two hyperplanes opposite unit normals, LMW's oriented tangency pair by pair, and the converses deliver tangency in this sense; the compatible orientations of an oriented Descartes configuration (disjoint interiors, with the given orientations or all reversed) are proved separately for every solution, after multiplying each row's power polynomial by the total curvature, and for a valid, pairwise tangent family with positive total curvature for its own open interiors. Kernel-checked, for every n >= 1 (LMW's Section 3 assumes n >= 2; their Section 8, (8.4), is the identity on the line): the augmented matrix W of n + 2 pairwise tangent spheres of nonzero curvature, and of n + 2 pairwise tangent spheres and hyperplanes, satisfies W^T Q_n W = [[0, -4, 0], [-4, 0, 0], [0, 0, 2 I_n]] with Q_n = I - (1/n) 11^T (Theorem 3.3); every real solution W is the augmented matrix of exactly one family of valid, pairwise tangent oriented spheres and hyperplanes, and, when its second column has no zero, of exactly one pairwise tangent family of spheres (the converse of Theorem 3.3); the Soddy-Gosset relation (sum 1/r_i)^2 = n sum (1/r_i)^2 with and without hyperplanes (Theorem 1.2, (1.2)) and its form b^T Q_n b = 0 ((3.2)); the curvature-centre identity M^T Q_n M = diag(0, 2 I_n) (Theorem 3.2, (3.5)); at n = 2 the complex Descartes theorem (sum b_i z_i)^2 = 2 sum (b_i z_i)^2 and sum b_i (b_i z_i) = (1/2)(sum b_i)(sum b_i z_i) (Theorem 2.1, (2.2)-(2.3)); det Q_n = -2/n; and the three statements for Mathlib's EuclideanGeometry.Sphere (pairwise IsExtTangent, or one enclosing sphere to which the others are IsIntTangent, with curvature -1/r_e). The matrix identity is proved as LMW's Section 4 argument (Lemmas 4.3-4.4, (4.9)-(4.10)) run directly in Euclidean coordinates: W^T Q_n W is the target exactly when the rows of W have Lorentz norm 1 and pair to -1 under G = [[0, -1/2, 0], [-1/2, 0, 0], [0, 0, I_n]], since W G W^T = 2I - J and (2I - J)(Q_n/2) = I. Also proved: both halves of the converse of the Soddy-Gosset theorem, LMW's Theorem 3.1, about which they write "We do not know an easy proof of this result; a proof appears in [16]" ([16] is Graham-Lagarias-Mallows-Wilks-Yan III, whose arXiv versions 1-2 prove both halves as their Theorem 2.2 from the same base configuration and the transitivity of the Lorentz group, a section the published version omits). Existence: every nonzero b with (sum b_i)^2 = n sum b_i^2 is the curvature vector of a pairwise tangent family of spheres, where b_i is nonzero, and hyperplanes, where b_i = 0, and of a family of spheres when no b_i vanishes, by one Q_n-reflection from the configuration of two parallel hyperplanes and n unit spheres in the proof of GLMWY III's Theorem 6.1, or from its inversion in the unit sphere. Congruence: two valid, pairwise tangent families with the same curvatures, index by index, are carried one to the other by exactly one Euclidean motion x -> x O + t with O^T O = I, reflections and hyperplanes included, with O = (1/2) X^T Q_n X' and t = -(1/4) a^T Q_n X' for augmented matrices [a | b | X] and [a' | b | X'] and the motion's action on points, spheres and hyperplanes; W_1^-1 W_2 preserves the target form and fixes the curvature coordinate, and every such matrix is a motion matrix (GLMWY III's arXiv v1-v2 argue instead by the rigidity of a simplex of centres); its uniqueness and parameters are proved here. A motion preserves validity, curvature and tangency, so two valid, pairwise tangent families are congruent exactly when their curvature vectors agree. For every solution W: the total curvature B is nonzero, the open sets {y : B F_i(y) < 0}, F_i(y) = b_i |y|^2 - 2 <v_i, y> + a_i the power polynomial of row i (negative exactly inside a ball, outside a ball of negative radius, or on the side of a hyperplane its normal points to), are pairwise disjoint, at most two rows are hyperplanes, and no three boundaries pass through a finite point; for a valid, pairwise tangent family the total curvature is nonzero, at most two members are hyperplanes, and when the total curvature is positive the open interiors are pairwise disjoint. The converse of Theorem 3.2 in every dimension under the hypothesis of a nonzero first column (every real M with M^T Q_n M = diag(0, 2 I_n) and a nonzero first column is the curvature-centre matrix of exactly one family of valid, pairwise tangent oriented spheres and hyperplanes), which GLMWY I, Theorem 3.1 and its Remark, prove at n = 2 with that hypothesis and which LMW's printed converse ("any real solution M") and GLMWY III's arXiv v1-v2 Theorem 2.3 omit, together with the matrix at n = 2 with columns 0, e_0 - e_1, e_2 - e_3 (GLMWY I's configuration (3.15) with its first column zeroed; the matrix of four oriented lines with normals +-e_0, +-e_1), which solves the equation and is the curvature-centre matrix of no valid, pairwise tangent family. The existence of a configuration in every dimension (that configuration); for n >= 2 the Apollonian generators S_k = I + (2/(n-1)) e_k 1^T - (2n/(n-1)) e_k e_k^T of GLMWY III, (4.1), preserve Q_n and carry configurations to configurations, with the row formula (S_k W)_k = (2/(n-1)) sum_{i != k} W_i - W_k, and Soddy's two spheres (LMW, footnote 3; GLMWY III, Section 4.1), in the signed sense: the oriented spheres and hyperplanes tangent to n + 1 members of a configuration are exactly the missing member and its Apollonian reflection, two distinct objects whose curvatures sum to (2/(n-1)) times the sum of the others' curvatures. The planar Soddy-Gosset relation for four circles of positive radius, pairwise externally tangent or with one enclosing circle, is already in Lean in facebookresearch/atlas-lean (descartes_circle_theorem, not registered); rjwalters/lean-genius and carlok/LeanFrontier treat the planar relation as a definition (its two roots, the same over the complex numbers, integer reflections and parity; LeanFrontier checks it for one family of Ford circles and their tangent line), with no derivation from tangency; no other formalization of these statements was found by the dated searches.

records.title: Alexandroff–Urysohn cover metrization
records.abstract: A T0 space is metrizable if and only if it admits a sequence of open covers such that every intersecting pair of members at the next level has union contained in one member at the current level, and the point-stars form a neighborhood basis. Without separation the same criterion characterizes pseudometrizability. The proof constructs a countably generated co-membership uniformity with exactly the supplied topology. Covers have unrestricted cardinality; empty spaces are included. Classical mathematics, with no novelty or priority claim.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: Erdős Problem 656: translated restricted pair sums
records.abstract: A reproduction of a complete Lean proof that every set A of natural numbers with positive ordinary upper asymptotic density contains an infinite subset B whose distinct pair sums, after one integer translation, all lie in A. This is the exact ordinary-density statement of Erdős Problem 656, an instance of Kra–Moreira–Richter–Robertson Theorem 1.2(i).

records.title: Waist
records.abstract: Formalization of waist inequalities for different settings: (1) Gromov's waist theorem for the round sphere S^n (the original proof in Memarian arXiv:0911.3972 has gaps; here a spherical adaptation of Klartag's proof is used); (2) An explicit positive lower bound on the unnormalized (n-k)-dimensional Hausdorff measure (Mathlib's muH[n-k], defined via sum of (diam U_i)^{n-k} without the unit-ball normalization factor omega_{n-k} / 2^{n-k}, in the chordal metric on S^n) of a fiber on the round sphere S^n: muH[n-k](f^{-1}(y)) >= 1 / (12 * 4^n * 3^k), yielding the positive lower bound (omega_{n-k} / 2^{n-k}) / (12 * 4^n * 3^k) for conventionally normalized Hausdorff measure (motivated by Gromov's 2003 conjecture of the sharp bound vol(S^{n-k}), which remains open for 1 < k < n; proved via Akopyan modification of Klartag's argument, Waists.sphere_hausdorff_waist); (3) The Gaussian waist inequality on (R^n, gamma_n) (Gromov 2003, Klartag arXiv:1608.04121); (4) The waist of the open unit cube (0,1)^n (Klartag arXiv:1608.04121); (5) The waist of the Euclidean ball B^n(R) with arbitrary center and radius (Akopyan-Karasev, arXiv:1608.06279); (6) The waist of a spherical ball of radius R < pi in S^n (Akopyan-Karasev, arXiv:1702.07513); (7) The waist of a hyperbolic ball of radius R in H^n (Akopyan-Karasev, arXiv:1702.07513); (8) The waist of an ellipsoid with semi-axes a_1 <= ... <= a_n (Akopyan-Karasev, arXiv:1608.06279, Corollary 1); (9) The waist of a box / parallelotope (0, a_1) x ... x (0, a_n) (Akopyan-Karasev, arXiv:1608.06279, Corollary 2). Supporting developments include: classical and tree Borsuk-Ulam theorems derived from combinatorial Tucker-type lemmas; Prékopa-Leindler and Brunn-Minkowski inequalities; spherical cap quasiconcavity; Archimedes' projection; and Frostman center measures.

records.title: Füredi's stability theorem and the Erdős–Simonovits stability theorem
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the stability theory of Turán's theorem. (1) Füredi's sharp stability theorem for cliques: a K_{p+1}-free graph on n vertices with at least t(n, p) − t edges (t(n, p) the number of edges of the Turán graph) has a p-partite subgraph with at least e(G) − t edges, via Füredi's partition inequality e(G) + Σᵢ e(G[Vᵢ]) ≤ e(K(V₁, …, V_p)); also edit distance at most 3t to a complete p-partite graph. (2) The Erdős–Simonovits stability theorem for every forbidden graph L with χ(L) ≤ p + 1: for every ε > 0 there are δ > 0 and n₀ such that every L-free graph on n ≥ n₀ vertices with at least (1 − 1/p) n²/2 − δn² edges differs from a complete p-partite graph in at most εn² edges, derived as in Füredi's paper from the regularity method. For this, the project extends Mathlib's regularity theory, which only treats triangles, with (3) the clique counting lemma in ε-uniform parts, (4) the clique removal lemma (fewer than δn^r copies of K_r can be destroyed by deleting fewer than εn² edges) and (5) the embedding lemma for any fixed graph with a proper colouring into pairwise uniform dense parts. Mathlib has Turán's theorem, Szemerédi's regularity lemma and triangle counting/removal, but none of (1)–(5).

records.title: A converse to the discrete four-vertex theorem
records.abstract: Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the paper "A converse to the discrete four-vertex theorem", answering Tabachnikov's Problem 2. For every n >= 4, every cyclic sequence of positive numbers with two distinct plateau maxima and two distinct plateau minima is the sequence of circumradii of consecutive vertex triples of a simple, strictly convex, coherent polygon (circumcenters inside the vertex angles). Together with Dahlberg's discrete four-vertex theorem, also proved here, this characterizes the nonconstant radius sequences of such polygons. The realization can be chosen C^1 in the data near every nonconstant admissible sequence, but an explicit path of hexagon data admits no continuous choice of realizing polygons. The analogous characterization for circles tangent to three consecutive supporting lines (the converse to Wegner's four-edge theorem) is also proved.

records.title: Erdos 662: corrected global threshold conjecture
records.abstract: Disproves an explicitly corrected global threshold formulation of Erdos problem 662. For each radius, the conjecture bounds the average number of nearby points in every sufficiently large one-separated planar set by the unit triangular lattice's neighbor count. An exact rational oblique lattice and separated finite replicas violate the bound at radius six.

records.title: Sneider's Gδ-diagonal metrization theorem
records.abstract: A compact Hausdorff space is metrizable if and only if its diagonal is a Gδ subset of its square with the product topology. The proof supplies a cofinal countable family of finite intersections of closed diagonal neighborhoods and an actual metric inducing exactly the given topology. The underlying type is arbitrary and may be empty. A general supporting theorem proves countable neighborhood character of every closed Gδ set in a compact normal space. This is classical mathematics; no novelty or priority is claimed.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: Pseudorandom hypergraph matchings (Ehard–Glock–Joos)
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the main results of Ehard, Glock and Joos, "Pseudorandom hypergraph matchings" (Combin. Probab. Comput. 2020): Pippenger's theorem on almost perfect matchings in almost regular hypergraphs with small codegrees (Theorem 1.1); the existence of a matching M in any r-uniform hypergraph with Δ(H) ≤ Δ, codegrees ≤ Δ^{1−δ} and at most exp(Δ^{ε²}) edges such that ω(M) = (1 ± Δ^{−ε}) ω(E(H))/Δ simultaneously for up to exp(Δ^{ε²}) weight functions (Theorem 1.2, with ε = δ/(50r²)); the generalization to weight functions on ℓ-tuples of edges, under the same exponential cap on the number of edges and of weight functions (Theorem 1.3, the main theorem, with ε = δ/(50L²r²)); the concentration inequality for pattern weights under a uniformly random colouring (Theorem 3.1); and the existence of partial Steiner systems whose subgraph counts behave as in the random model (Theorem 4.1). The formal proof is self-contained over Mathlib: Freedman's and Bernstein's inequalities are proved inside the project, and the Molloy–Reed colouring theorem used as a black box in the paper is replaced by a self-contained nibble.

records.title: A sharp asymptotic spectral bound for forbidden subgraphs
records.abstract: For every fixed finite graph F of chromatic number r+1 at least three and every positive epsilon, there is an edge threshold M such that every finite simple F-free graph G with m at least M satisfies F2(A_G) <= 2(1-1/r)m - (2(1-1/r)-1)Delta(G) + epsilon m. F2 is the sum of the squares of the two largest positive adjacency eigenvalues with missing terms padded by zero. The graphs may be disconnected. A companion theorem establishes agreement with the two largest ordered eigenvalue squares in the same eventual range. Enough edges force an F-free graph to be noncomplete; BN nonedge interlacing gives a nonnegative second ordered eigenvalue, so its positive-two energy equals the first two ordered eigenvalue squares. The proof checks ordinary clique removal through regularity and clique counting, derives weighted deletion, reuses the proved BN rank-two Gram inequality, and supplies the spectral lift, hub separation and uniform assembly.

records.title: Low-dimensional exact counterexamples to the Recht–Ré inequality
records.abstract: Five real symmetric PSD 3×3 integer matrices and five complex Hermitian PSD 2×2 Gaussian-integer matrices each have sum 100I and exact norm-of-averaged-product ratio 10329/10000 at n=k=5. The Lean statements use Mathlib positive semidefiniteness over the real and complex fields and the Euclidean operator norm. The rational formalization of De Sa's dimension-five norm-19/16 example is included as a supporting benchmark. The real symmetric dimension-two case is not resolved.

records.title: Sharp quartic Lyapunov boundaries and sextic separation for a planar cubic family
records.abstract: For a specified planar homogeneous cubic family, positive definite real homogeneous quartic Lyapunov certificates exist with strict derivative exactly when the absolute parameter is below an explicit algebraic boundary, and with weak derivative exactly through that boundary. Its value is about 2.1281535330886186. At the positive endpoint the entire cone of quartics with nonpositive derivative is one explicit nonnegative ray, without any positivity assumption. The negative Lie derivative of the endpoint quartic is a cubic square with three distinct real zero lines. Exact integer certificates separate degrees two and four at parameter two, and degrees four and six at nine fourths. The formal statements use actual partial derivatives and allow unrestricted real coefficients.

records.title: The Nash-Williams–Tutte tree packing theorem and Nash-Williams' arboricity theorem
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of three classical results on edge-disjoint trees and forests in finite simple graphs, none of which is in Mathlib. (1) The Nash-Williams–Tutte tree packing theorem: a graph has k edge-disjoint spanning trees if and only if every partition of its vertices into m parts has at least k(m − 1) edges between different parts. (2) Nash-Williams' arboricity theorem: the edges can be covered by k forests if and only if every nonempty vertex set S spans at most k(|S| − 1) edges. (3) The corollary that every 2k-edge-connected graph has k edge-disjoint spanning trees. Mathlib has no matroid union theorem and no graphic matroid; the proofs are direct edge-exchange arguments.

records.title: Erdős' theorem on graphs of large girth and large chromatic number
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Erdős' 1959 theorem: for every g and k there is a finite graph with girth greater than g and chromatic number greater than k. The formalization proves the structural form given by Erdős' probabilistic argument: for every g and every ε > 0, for all sufficiently large n there is a graph on n vertices with no cycle of length at most g in which every independent set has fewer than εn vertices; hence, for all large n, a graph on n vertices with girth greater than g that is not k-colourable. Mathlib has girth and chromatic number but not this theorem; Mycielski's construction (registered separately by another author) gives triangle-free graphs only.

records.title: Rényi and Tsallis entropy monotonicity for Bernoulli sums
records.abstract: Lean formalization of coordinatewise Rényi and Tsallis entropy monotonicity for finite independent Bernoulli sums on the closed half cube, for every real order in [0,2], as stated in Hillion-Johnson Conjecture 4.4. The complete core proves both entropy comparisons and the finite inverse-score association inequality. Concrete coefficient-law and entropy definitions are checked separately. VERIFICATION.md defines exact-source Linux acceptance and distinguishes historical association-only checkpoints.

records.title: Compact Hausdorff countable-network metrization
records.abstract: For an arbitrary compact Hausdorff space, metrizability and second countability are each equivalent to the existence of a countable network of arbitrary subsets. A genuine Urysohn-function construction from pairs of network elements supplies continuous separation, and a compatible metric induces exactly the original topology. Supporting results give bounded-real-coordinate closed embeddings, preservation under continuous surjections, arbitrary-subspace heredity and compact-subspace metrization. Empty spaces and arbitrary universes are allowed. This is classical mathematics; no novelty or priority is claimed.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: The connected size-Ramsey number of a four-edge matching versus a quadrilateral
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization project for the connected size-Ramsey equality rhat_c(4K2, C4) = 17. The intended proof uses a universal C4 vertex-transversal bound 4 tau_4(G) <= |E(G)|, a classification of the connected equality cases through sixteen edges (C4, the 4-wheel, K_{3,3} minus an edge, the octahedron), an avoiding-colouring construction from a three-vertex transversal, and an explicit twelve-vertex, seventeen-edge host. Proofs are complete as of commit c8d54e2 (2026-10-17); the proof certificate is Solution.lean and its dependency closure. Formal adversary pass 1 and reviewer pass 1 are ACCEPT_WITH_FIXES (fixes applied); the CI comparator passed at 38bd345 (2026-10-17) with five records. A sixth record, the transversal half of Corollary C (SizeRamsey.connected_transversal_le_three), was registered on 2026-10-17 (commit cc2aec2); the CI comparator passed with six records at 46bf2d0 (2026-10-17, run 39034260971).

records.title: Growth series of the triangle Coxeter groups (p, q, infinity), with the PGL(2,Z) instance: Padovan sphere sizes and growth rate the plastic number
records.abstract: Kernel-checked proof, for every Coxeter system on three generators a, b, c with m(a,c) = p, m(b,c) = q, m(a,b) = infinity and p, q >= 2, of the growth-series identity in the ring of integer power series: (sum_n a(n) X^n) * (1 - (X + ... + X^(p-1))(X + ... + X^(q-1))) = (1 + X)(1 + ... + X^(p-1))(1 + ... + X^(q-1)), where a(n) is the number of group elements of Coxeter length n; together with its instances (2,3,inf), (2,4,inf), (3,3,inf) and, for (2,3,inf) = PGL(2,Z), the sphere sizes 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 12, 16, ..., the Padovan identity a(n) = Pad(n+5) for n >= 2, the two-sided bounds 2 rho^n <= a(n) <= 4 rho^n (n >= 2), and the growth rate a(n)^(1/n) -> rho, the plastic number, the unique real root > 1 of x^3 = x + 1; and, for the whole family, monotonicity and symmetry in (p, q), the growth rate of every hyperbolic member, and the minimality of the plastic number. Twenty compared theorems: (1) the general identity for all p, q >= 2; (2) non-vacuity, a Coxeter matrix of that type exists for all p, q >= 2; (3)-(5) the three instances; (6) the (2,3,inf) sphere sizes a(0..4) = 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 and the recursion a(n+5) = a(n+3) + a(n+2) for all n; (7) that the recursion fails one step earlier, a(4) != a(2) + a(1); (8) a(n) = Pad(n+5) for n >= 2, for any sequence with the Padovan initial values and recursion; (9) existence and uniqueness of the plastic number; (10) the bounds; (11) the n-th-root limit; (12) monotonicity: a(n) of a (p,q,inf) system is at most a(n) of a (p',q',inf) system for p <= p', q <= q'; (13) symmetry in p and q; (14) 2 rho^n <= a(n), n >= 2, for every hyperbolic member; (15) for (p,q) != (2,2) exactly one tau > 1 solves (tau^-1 + ... + tau^-(p-1))(tau^-1 + ... + tau^-(q-1)) = 1; (16) a(n)^(1/n) -> tau; (17) tau strictly increasing in (p,q); (18) rho <= tau with equality exactly at (2,3), (3,2), so the plastic number is the minimal growth rate of the family; (19) tau < 2; (20) tau -> 2 as p, q -> infinity (for every sigma < 2 there is N with tau > sigma whenever p, q >= N). The family statements (12)-(20) give the growth rate of every hyperbolic (p, q, inf) group as the unique root tau > 1 of an explicit equation, strictly increasing in the labels, with the plastic number as the family minimum attained only at (2,3,inf) and (3,2,inf); they restrict to this family, and kernel-check there, Terragni's monotonicity (2016, Thm. A), Floyd's planar minimality (1992, p. 482) and the continuity of the growth rate (Floyd 1992; Yukita 2024). The mathematics is classical and no novelty is claimed for it: the growth series of a Coxeter group is rational and determined by its finite parabolic subgroups (Steinberg 1968; Humphreys 1990 Section 5.12); growth of planar hyperbolic Coxeter groups is Floyd 1992 and Cannon-Wagreich 1992, and the (2,3,inf), (2,4,inf) and (3,3,inf) sphere sequences are OEIS A096231, A179070 (shifted) and A054886, with generating functions derived there from Cannon-Wagreich Prop. 3.1 and, for A096231, the Padovan form a(n) = A000931(n+10) recorded; Floyd 1992 (p. 482) proves (2,3,inf) minimal among cusped planar groups and Kellerhals 2013 gives an alternative proof; Bucher-Talambutsa 2016 Prop. 18 proves statement (11) itself by a normal form and, with Mann's bound, the minimality of rho for PGL(2,Z) over all generating sets. The (p, q, inf) family is hyperbolic exactly when (p, q) differs from (2, 2); the affine (2, 2, inf) is included in (1). The contribution claimed is the kernel-checked general identity for all p, q at once, and the family statements (12)-(20) derived from it, from Mathlib's CoxeterSystem alone — Mathlib at this pin has no growth series, no exchange or deletion property and no parabolic-subgroup API — by constructing the amalgam normal forms, lifting their action to the group, proving Coxeter length equals normal-form length, and counting. No "first formalization" claim is made. Application, cited and not a claim of the entry: the (2,3,inf) group is the Weyl group of AE_3 = PGL(2,Z) (Feingold-Frenkel 1983) and, in the Damour-Henneaux-Nicolai billiard description of the Belinski-Khalatnikov-Lifshitz limit (a conjecture for generic singularities, Henneaux-Persson-Spindel 2008 Section 2.9), the reflection group of the billiard of 3+1-dimensional vacuum gravity near a spacelike singularity (Damour-Henneaux-Nicolai 2003 Section 8; Henneaux-Persson-Spindel 2008 Section 3.1), where a(n) counts the chambers reachable from the fundamental chamber after exactly n wall collisions over all initial data, so (10)-(11) give the growth rate of those outcomes (elementary reflection-group geometry, not formal content). Hypotheses are inline: the Coxeter system enters through Mathlib's CoxeterSystem with the three matrix entries as hypotheses, rho through its defining equation and 1 < rho, the Padovan sequence through its initial values and recursion; the compared statements use only core Mathlib vocabulary (CoxeterMatrix, CoxeterSystem, CoxeterSystem.length, Nat.card, PowerSeries.mk, Finset.range/Ico sums, Filter.Tendsto, Filter.atTop, nhds, real powers) — zero custom definitions. The pinned source of each Coxeter-specific imported definition, and of Nat.card and PowerSeries.mk, is quoted verbatim, with permalinks, in MATHLIB_DEFINITIONS.md (the remaining vocabulary is standard Mathlib and is not quoted), and DefinitionAudit.lean kernel-checks the facts the statements rely on (the entry 0 encodes infinity; length is the minimal word length; spheres are finite and Nat.card is their cardinality; every Coxeter matrix has a Coxeter system).

records.title: First Betti numbers of five-generated numerical semigroups
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization project for (F) an explicit two-parameter family of minimally five-generated numerical semigroups <m, m+1, m+k, m+2k-1, m+2k>, m = 2kq+1, whose toric ideal has spanRank exactly 4k+2. Planned scope for (W), a proposed finite-width bound beta1 <= 2w+2 (4 <= w <= 40), not all formalized: the generic fiber-graph infrastructure, both algebraic bridges (only the upper bridge is formalized; the reverse bridge is not), the corrected singleton-counting decomposition beta1 + p = 5 + N, the pair-component antichain lemma and certificate-checker soundness (not yet written). Version 1 targets F; W is stated and excluded from the release comparator. F is sorry-free at 793e759.

records.title: Countable-coordinate factorization for compact products
records.abstract: Every continuous map from an arbitrary product of nonempty compact Hausdorff spaces into a metrizable space factors continuously through a countable subproduct. A uniform-space proof establishes countable coordinate dependence for uniformly continuous maps into separated countably generated uniform spaces. The factor for a fixed coordinate set is unique. Countably many maps share a countable coordinate set. Continuous injections into metrizable targets force only countably many nontrivial factors, giving the exact metrizability criterion for nonempty compact Hausdorff products. Empty index and empty selected-coordinate sets are allowed. These are classical results and no novelty or priority is claimed.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: NumericalSemigroups: Huang's quadratic form, its positivity, and its n-generator kernel windows
records.abstract: Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization around the quadratic form Q(n) = sum_{i,j in G} K(g(j) - g(i)) n_i n_j of Y. Huang (arXiv:2604.13238) on the gap diagram G of the numerical semigroup <a,b>, in two parts. Part A (Huang's results, two generators): the symmetric bilinear form B of Q satisfies B(1_D, 1_E) = dinv(D, E) for subdiagrams D, E (Huang's Theorem 1.2, formalized by AxiomProver and included in `Dinv/AxiomProver.lean`); from it this work proves Q(1_D) = dinv(D) and Q(1_D) > 0 for nonempty D (Theorem 1.1), B >= 0 on the cone of nonnegative decreasing functions, and the bound Q(n) >= n_i^2 / |G| for every coordinate i (Theorem 1.3, so Q(n) >= ||n||_inf^2 / |G|), which settles Huang's positive-definiteness conjecture for Q on that cone; Theorem 1.3 had not been formalized. Part B (the author's manuscript "A Linear Algorithm for Huang's Quadratic Form on Numerical Semigroups and Density Asymptotics", Flamandzki, 2026): for generators p_1,...,p_n the generalised kernel K^(n)(d) is the inclusion-exclusion sum over sub-multisets S of the generators of (-1)^|S| times the indicator of d >= sigma(S), where sigma(S) is the sum of S; it is a step function whose jumps are the parity function pi(s) = K(s) - K(s-1). Part B states and proves: (1) for two generators a < b, Q equals the sliding-window form sum_k n_k (W+_k - W-_k); (2) for any nonempty generator list, Q(n) is a sum over the breakpoints s of K of pi(s) times the tail pair-sum T(s) = sum_{j-i >= s} n_i n_j, with at most sigma + 1 breakpoints, and the number w of active windows (intervals between consecutive breakpoints on which K is nonzero) is at most sigma, and at most 2^n - 2 for n >= 2 distinct positive generators; and (3) for strictly increasing generators p_k >= 2 with log p_n = o(n), the density w(n)/(2^n - 1) is o(P(n)) where P(n) = prod (1 - 1/p_k), equivalently delta(n)/P(n) tends to 1 for delta(n) = P(n) - w(n)/(2^n - 1). The complexity claims of the manuscript (running times of the algorithms) and its computational tables and conjectures are not formalized. The substance of Part B is the exact breakpoint decomposition of Q, the identification of the inclusion-exclusion kernel with its recursive form, and the asymptotic squeeze. Zero sorries; depends only on the three standard Lean axioms. The file `Dinv/AxiomProver.lean` is third-party code under the MIT license (see NOTICE); everything else is Apache-2.0.

records.title: Optimal Local Decompression: Uniform Finite-View Reduction
records.abstract: A uniform finite-view reduction at the paper's counting-optimal k-bit vertex budget for odd maximum degree 2k-1. Given one total finite-view orientation rule with a sufficient one-bit advice guarantee, one decoder family is chosen before graph order, topology, markers, advice and payload. Every connected graph on Fin n with n>16(k+1) and degree at most 2k-1 admits an encoder recovering every edge bit at either endpoint from a 2^k-symbol vertex alphabet. The same total decoder is local across different connected graphs and arbitrary labelings, with no marker validity or encoded-input premise. Its explicit physical radius depends only on k and the oracle's radius, not n. Eight selected endpoints also cover storage capacity, advice-first coding, complete-graph counting, and bounded connected cell geometry. The external orientation algorithm, computability, general identifier assignments for the assembled theorem and mixed-component assembly remain outside the selected formal scope.

records.title: Moore graphs of diameter two: the Hoffman–Singleton theorem
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the Hoffman–Singleton theorem on Moore graphs of diameter two. For a finite k-regular graph of diameter at most two: the Moore bound n ≤ k² + 1; if moreover the girth is at least five, then n = k² + 1 and the graph is strongly regular with parameters (k² + 1, k, 0, 1); and, if k ≥ 2, then k ∈ {2, 3, 7, 57}. Mathlib has strongly regular graphs and the spectral theorem for Hermitian matrices, but not this theorem.

records.title: Countable-density Hewitt–Marczewski–Pondiczery theorem
records.abstract: A product of at most continuum many separable topological spaces is separable. The proof constructs a countable family of finite binary tables that realizes every finite assignment of natural-number labels, then applies dense sequences in the factors. No separation, metrizability, compactness or countable-base assumption on the factors is needed. Empty factors and empty index sets are allowed. A companion theorem proves the sharp criterion for discrete Boolean cubes: Bool^I is separable exactly when the index cardinality is at most continuum. This is the classical countable-density case; no arbitrary-cardinal or algebraic generalization, novelty or priority is claimed.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: Chvátal's and Pósa's degree conditions for Hamiltonian cycles
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of two classical degree-sequence conditions for Hamiltonicity of a finite simple graph on n ≥ 3 vertices with degrees d₁ ≤ ⋯ ≤ dₙ. Chvátal's theorem (1972): if for every i < n/2, dᵢ ≤ i implies d_{n−i} ≥ n − i, then the graph is Hamiltonian (stated without sorting: if at least i vertices have degree at most i, then at least i + 1 vertices have degree at least n − i). Pósa's theorem (1962): if for every k with 1 ≤ k < (n − 1)/2 fewer than k vertices have degree at most k, and, for odd n, at most (n − 1)/2 vertices have degree at most (n − 1)/2, then the graph is Hamiltonian. Mathlib has Hamiltonian cycles but neither theorem.

records.title: The graph removal lemma for every fixed graph
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the graph removal lemma of Erdős, Frankl and Rödl for an arbitrary fixed finite graph H on k vertices: for every ε > 0 there is δ > 0, depending only on H and ε, such that every finite graph on n vertices with fewer than δ nᵏ labelled copies of H can be made H-free by deleting fewer than ε n² edges; equivalently (far form), a graph from which at least ε n² edges must be deleted to destroy all copies of H has at least δ nᵏ labelled copies. Also included is the counting lemma used in the proof: if parts s x (one for each vertex x of H) are robustly dense with density at least d along the edges of H, with 2kη ≤ dᵏ and #(s x) ≥ 4k/dᵏ, then at least (dᵏ/4)ᵏ ∏ #(s x) injective maps send H into G with f x ∈ s x. Mathlib has the regularity lemma and the triangle removal lemma, but not the removal lemma for a general H.

records.title: Additive strengthening of Erdos problem 679: a known refutation
records.abstract: For every real additive constant C and natural cutoff K, every sufficiently large natural n admits K < k < n with omega(n-k) at least log(k)/log(log(k)) + C. Here omega counts distinct prime factors. This independently implemented proof uses a fixed primorial residue window, elementary Chebyshev estimates and Stirling bounds. It refutes the known additive strengthening and does not resolve the main multiplicative question. No mathematical novelty is claimed.

records.title: Tamper-proofing with self-modifying code: a Lean formalization of the threat model
records.abstract: Formalizes Gregory Morse and Tamas Kozsik's paper "Tamper-Proofing with Self-Modifying Code" (arXiv:2604.12407v1). The selected statement (PalomarSMT.mathematical_result, four results T1-T4) is an abstract threat model for checksum units whose opcode state lives in the memory they checksum: a system of units with regions and code, a timeline of write, execute, check, split-view and DMA events, adversary levels L0-L4, a cost contract with lower bounds on emulation, forgery and mediation, and eight structural assumptions A1-A8 (none of the form "the attacker is detected"). An effective alarm needs a unit with a response code (at least one response byte, all of it unmodified) and either a value mismatch or a positive number k of consecutive timing failures; A6 therefore includes k > 0 and A7 includes that every unit has a response byte. The four selected results are: for every well-formed timeline of a system satisfying A1-A8, if a protected byte outside the SMC opcode bytes (which legitimately vary) is executed while the fetch view differs from the original image, an effective alarm occurs somewhere in the timeline, not necessarily before that execution (T1; executing a changed protected opcode byte is outside the goal); in a faithful split-view run every iteration with a non-zero toggle (apart from the last) is mediated, and under A3 and A5 a faithful mediated check that the cost contract admits, with such an iteration, is a timing failure (T2; not every split-view attack is claimed detected); each of the eleven assumptions is necessary, by an explicit winning adversary against a system that satisfies all the others (T3); and every well-formed timeline at level L0 or L1 with the inline timer satisfies A1, A4 and A5, while there are winning adversaries against systems satisfying every other assumption at L1 with an operating-system timer, at L2 and at L4 (T4: the removed assumption is A5 at L1 with an operating-system timer and at L2, A1 at L2, A4 at L4). Proved in the same development but NOT part of this record (they are not in the Comparator configuration): the paper's Harvard/von Neumann observation (C01, C02), a general fact about observation-preserving simulation whose time bound assumes the per-read charge it uses; the three-quadword forgery of the checksum and the proof that two quadwords do not suffice (the selected T3 witness for A8 is a single two-quadword collision pair); the x86-64 model of the kernels, the static kernel against its C emulation, the 296-unit unrolled kernel at an abstract level and at the instruction level, the byte layout against assembler output, a clear-count contract checked against the paper's tables, timers, the noise estimator, the detection predicate and the data ratios, and native test vectors for the corrected sources.

records.title: Tutte's f-factor theorem
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Tutte's f-factor theorem: a finite simple graph G has a spanning subgraph H with deg_H v = f v for every vertex v if and only if, for all disjoint vertex sets S and T, q(S, T) ≤ ∑_{v ∈ S} f v − ∑_{v ∈ T} f v + ∑_{v ∈ T} deg_{G−S} v, where q(S, T) is the number of connected components C of G − (S ∪ T) for which ∑_{v ∈ C} f v + e(C, T) is odd and deg_{G−S} v is the number of neighbours of v outside S. Mathlib has Tutte's 1-factor theorem but not the f-factor theorem.

records.title: Chordal, split, threshold and cograph structure
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of classical structure theorems for finite simple graphs. Chordal graphs: every minimal a–b separator is a clique, a nonempty finite chordal graph has a simplicial vertex, and a connected non-complete one has two non-adjacent simplicial vertices (Dirac 1961); a finite graph is chordal iff it has a perfect elimination order (Fulkerson–Gross 1965), iff it is the intersection graph of subtrees of a finite tree (Gavril 1974); a nonempty finite chordal graph has treewidth ω − 1, and every finite graph has ω ≤ tw + 1. Split graphs: split iff the graph and its complement are chordal, iff no induced 2K₂, C₄ or C₅ (Földes–Hammer 1977). Threshold graphs: threshold iff no induced 2K₂, C₄ or P₄ (Chvátal–Hammer 1977), iff split and a cograph (no induced P₄). Mathlib has none of these graph classes; their definitions are stated in the Challenge.

records.title: Elementary bounds for Erdos problem 684
records.abstract: Let U(n,k) be the full prime-power part of the binomial coefficient n choose k supported on primes at most k. For all sufficiently large n, there exists k at most n with k at most 514(log n)^2 and U(n,k) greater than n squared. For arbitrarily large n greater than one, U(n,k) equals one throughout k at most (log n)/8. This independent Mathlib-only implementation adapts the known residue averaging and prime-power obstruction of APSSV26 with coarse Chebyshev constants. It does not formalize that paper's sharper coefficients or Bae's stronger registered lower bound. The optimal order remains open and no mathematical novelty is claimed.

records.title: Planar Pólya–Szegő Buckling Inequality
records.abstract: Lean formalization proving the planar Polya-Szego conjecture for the first buckling eigenvalue. For open planar sets of positive finite area, it proves the sharp area inequality and characterizes equality by exact equality with an open disk. It retains the original Sobolev-space, variational eigenvalue and Bessel definitions, and includes the disk eigenvalue and buckling–Dirichlet comparison.

records.title: Jaeger's 4-flow theorem
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Jaeger's 4-flow theorem: every finite 4-edge-connected simple graph has a nowhere-zero integer 4-flow, i.e. an antisymmetric function on darts with values in {±1, ±2, ±3} that is conserved at every vertex. Also proved: a graph with two edge-disjoint spanning trees has its edges covered by two even subgraphs (a nowhere-zero ℤ₂ × ℤ₂-flow) and has a nowhere-zero integer 4-flow. Mathlib has no flows. Jaeger's 8-flow theorem for bridgeless graphs is not included.

records.title: Normalizers of Γ_Δ(N), Γ(N) and ±Γ₁(N)
records.abstract: Formal statements and proofs, in Lean 4 with Mathlib, about the normalizers in SL₂(ℝ) of the groups Γ_Δ(N) between Γ₁(N) and Γ₀(N), and the quotients Nor(Γ)/Γ, the modular automorphism groups of the curves X_Δ(N): a generalization of Newman's description of the normalizer to Γ_Δ(N); Nor(Γ(N)) = SL₂(ℤ), so the modular automorphism group of X(N) is SL₂(ℤ/N)/{±1}; and, for N ≠ 4, Nor(±Γ₁(N)) is generated by Γ₀(N) and the Atkin–Lehner elements, so X₁(N) has 2^ω(N) φ(N)/2 modular automorphisms for N ≥ 3 (N = 4 is an exception). 34 theorems, no sorry, only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

records.title: Dirac's theorem: k vertices of a k-connected graph lie on a common cycle
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Dirac's 1960 theorem: in a k-connected finite simple graph with k ≥ 2 (more than k vertices, and connected after deleting any set of fewer than k vertices), any set of at most k vertices lies on a common cycle. In particular, in a 2-connected finite graph any two vertices lie on a common cycle. Cycles are Mathlib's `SimpleGraph.Walk.IsCycle`. Mathlib does not have this theorem.

records.title: The normalizer of Γ₀(N): Newman's theorem, and the order and presentations of B(N)
records.abstract: Formal statements and proofs, in Lean 4 with Mathlib, about B(N) = Nor(Γ₀(N))/Γ₀(N), the normalizer of Γ₀(N) in SL₂(ℝ) modulo Γ₀(N), for every N ≥ 1: Newman's theorem describing the normalizer, in both directions; the order |B(N)| = 2^ω(n) ψ(N)/ψ(n), where h is the largest divisor of 24 with h² ∣ N and n = N/h²; generators and complete presentations of B(N) for every N; a criterion for B(N) to be the internal direct product of its local factors; B(18) ≅ S₄; and the errors in the published presentations: the Akbaş–Singerman relation fails in B(256), and Bars's presentations at levels 32, 64 and 128 define infinite groups, while completed presentations present B(32) and B(64) and Bars's presentation at level 256 presents B(256). 36 theorems, no sorry, only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

records.title: Modular automorphisms of Cartan modular curves of prime level
records.abstract: Formal statements and proofs, in Lean 4 with Mathlib, about the normalizers in SL₂(ℝ) of the groups defining the split and non-split Cartan modular curves and their normalizer curves: for any level N, every element of the normalizer of a group containing Γ(N) is a rational matrix of a restricted form; X_sp(N) ≅ X₀(N²); X_sp(p) (p ≥ 5) and X_ns(p) (p odd) have exactly 2 modular automorphisms; X_sp⁺(p) (p ≥ 7) and X_ns⁺(p) (p ≥ 5) have none, and both bounds on p are sharp. 17 theorems, no sorry, only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

records.title: Fréchet–Urysohn Σ-products of first-countable spaces
records.abstract: The countable-support Sigma-product of arbitrary first-countable topological factors, relative to an explicit basepoint and with the ordinary product-induced topology, is Frechet-Urysohn.
