An adaptive finite-coordinate schedule constructs a sequence from each set converging to any of its closure points. The index set may be arbitrary, including empty, and no separation assumption is used for this theorem. Companions give countable tightness and subspace inheritance, density in the full product, T1 countable-closure support control and sequential closedness, and nonsequentiality of an uncountable discrete Boolean cube. No normality, W-space, arbitrary Frechet-factor, compactness or novel-mathematics result is asserted.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: The local dynamical structure of Δ* sets via a new Furstenberg family algebra
records.abstract:
This development formalizes in Lean 4 the results of the paper "The local dynamical structure of Δ* sets via a new Furstenberg family algebra", which strengthens the connection between the combinatorics of difference sets and the dynamics of group rotations.
Let S be a discrete semigroup. A set A ⊆ S is syndetic if there is a finite F ⊆ S with S = ∪_{f ∈ F} f⁻¹A; a Δ set if there is a sequence s₁, s₂, … in S with s_j ∈ s_i A for all i < j; and a Bohr_0 set if it contains the preimage of an open neighborhood of the identity under a semigroup homomorphism from S to a finite-dimensional torus. Dually, a set is thick, a Δ* set, or a set of Bohr recurrence according as it meets every syndetic, every Δ, or every Bohr_0 subset of S. Bohr_0 sets in the integers are the almost periodic sets of classical interest, and Δ* sets are combinatorially large, being syndetic and rich in additive patterns.
The definition of a Δ set used here is the one given for general semigroups by Hindman, who calls these rQ sets, Q for quotient; in a commutative semigroup his left- and right-handed variants agree. It does not require the witnessing sequence to be injective, and so is slightly more inclusive than the classical difference-set definition. In the positive integers the two agree exactly: if A consists of positive integers and s_j − s_i ∈ A for all i < j then the sequence is strictly increasing, so A contains the difference set (S − S) ∩ ℕ of the infinite set S = {s₁, s₂, …}, and conversely. The two notions separate only in a semigroup containing an element a with sa = s for some s, where the constant sequence makes every set containing such an a a Δ set. In the integers the element 0 is of this kind, so a Δ set in the present sense is either a classical difference set or a set containing 0, and a Δ* set is exactly a classical Δ* set that contains 0.
The main result (Theorem A) is that Δ* sets in an arbitrary commutative semigroup carry local Bohr structure: if A ⊆ S is a Δ* set, then for every thick H ⊆ S there is a thick H′ ⊆ H and a Bohr_0 set B with A ∩ H′ = B ∩ H′. This generalizes results of Bergelson, Furstenberg and Weiss and of Host and Kra from the positive integers to arbitrary commutative semigroups by a purely topological-dynamical route in place of the ergodic- theoretic arguments used in the integer case. Theorem B is the dual formulation, in terms of Δ sets and sets of Bohr recurrence, that the proof actually establishes: if A ⊆ S admits a thick H such that A ∩ H′ is a set of Bohr recurrence for every thick H′ ⊆ H, then A is a Δ set. Theorem C exhibits a second instance of local structure by the same method: in a countable commutative semigroup, every C* set agrees with an IP* set on a thick subset of any prescribed thick set.  Theorem C also formulates the equivalent dual statement, just as Theorem B is in relation to Theorem A.
Theorem D supplies the algebraic framework the arguments rest on. A Furstenberg family on a set S is an upward-closed collection of subsets of S. On the Furstenberg families of a non-empty set, two binary operations, family meet and family join, are described and shown to be associative, commutative and monotone. Together with the family dual, they satisfy De Morgan-type laws. Family join has appeared before in the literature; family meet, as presented here, is believed to be new. The algebra reduces the equivalence of Theorems A and B to a short computation and makes similar reformulations in Ramsey theory routine.
The proofs of Theorems A and B depend on a companion result, formalized here but the subject of another Palomar entry, that the regionally proximal relation is an equivalence relation for minimal actions of commutative semigroups. The development runs to roughly 20,000 lines of Lean across 17 files and formalizes every lemma, proposition, corollary and theorem of the paper; the registered statements are Theorems A, B, C and D. Proved along the way, and not available in Mathlib, is the classical fact that the characters of a compact abelian group separate its points.

records.title: Spectral bounds on the chromatic and independence numbers
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of classical eigenvalue bounds for a finite simple graph G on a nonempty vertex type, with λ_max and λ_min the largest and smallest eigenvalues of its real adjacency matrix: the average degree is at most λ_max and λ_max is at most the maximum degree (Collatz–Sinogowitz); G is (⌊λ_max⌋ + 1)-colourable (Wilf 1967); if G has an edge, every proper colouring uses at least 1 − λ_max/λ_min colours (Hoffman 1970); and if G is k-regular with k ≥ 1, every independent set has at most n(−λ_min)/(k − λ_min) vertices (Hoffman's ratio bound). Mathlib has the spectral theorem for Hermitian matrices but none of these bounds.

records.title: Normalizers of the congruence subgroups Γ_H
records.abstract: Formal statements and proofs, in Lean 4 with Mathlib, about the normalizers in SL₂(ℝ) of every congruence subgroup Γ ⊇ Γ(N), that is, of every Γ_H for H ≤ SL₂(ℤ/N): Nor(Γ)/Γ is finite, of order at most [SL₂(ℤ) : Γ]·Σ_{D ∣ N} ψ(D); the local restrictions of Dose–Lido–Mercuri on the determinants of normalizing matrices; if, at every p ∣ N, H mod p fixes no line or H mod p^{v_p(N)} lies in a split Cartan subgroup, then Nor(Γ_H)/Γ_H ≅ N(H)/H; and at prime level the order is always [N(H) : H], or 2·[N(H) : H] when H fixes exactly one line. 21 theorems, no sorry, only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

records.title: Distinct prime divisors of central binomial coefficients
records.abstract: A formal proof of the classical asymptotic omega(binomial(2n,n)) times log n divided by n tending to log 4. The proof combines prime-power estimates, central-binomial bounds, a prime-factor cutoff, and elementary logarithmic limits; it does not use the prime number theorem. This strengthens the earlier finite lower-bound package to a full asymptotic theorem. It does not solve the uniform conjecture in Erdos problem 685 and claims no new mathematical theorem.

records.title: The Arithmetic of Time: the slowest settling clock on at most three letters is the Padovan substitution, unique up to mirror image, and both minimal rules are chiral
records.abstract: Five compared theorems. Among all substitutions on at most three letters whose incidence matrix has a Pisot eigenvalue θ > 1, the least such θ is the plastic number ρ, the real root of x³ = x + 1, attained only by the Padovan rule a ↦ b, b ↦ c, c ↦ ab and its mirror c ↦ ba, up to renaming the letters; both minimal rules are chiral, in opposite directions. Precisely: (1) for a substitution σ on k ≤ 3 letters (images may be empty) and a real eigenvalue θ > 1 of its integer incidence matrix that is a Pisot number, ρ ≤ θ, and θ = ρ exactly when, after renaming the letters, σ is the Padovan rule or its mirror; no primitivity or unit hypothesis; (2) the same classification for every real eigenvalue, with no Pisot hypothesis; (3) a 3 × 3 natural matrix with characteristic polynomial x³ − x − 1 is the Padovan matrix after one simultaneous permutation of rows and columns; (4) Siegel's bound ρ ≤ θ for Pisot numbers of degree at most three (Siegel 1944, restricted; not new; proved through the minimal Mahler measures of registered entry PALOMAR-2026-08-31-000004); (5) under the Padovan rule the word ca is a factor of the fifth iterate from the seed a, and ac is a factor of no iterate from any seed; under its mirror, the reverse. The uniqueness was stated without proof by Mercat (2020) for substitutions on three letters; the contribution is a kernel-checked proof of the combined statement, for every real eigenvalue and with no primitivity, unit or non-erasing hypothesis (in the equality case these are consequences: θ = ρ forces k = 3 and characteristic polynomial x³ − x − 1), together with the chirality of both minimal rules. No first-formalization claim is made. That ρ itself is a Pisot eigenvalue of the Padovan matrix, so that the bound is attained, is proved in Supplement.lean and not compared. Companion of registered entry PALOMAR-2026-08-19-000006.

records.title: The radian nine-gon is Euclidean Ramsey iff e^(i theta) is algebraic
records.abstract: Theorem D: for real theta, the nine points (cos k theta, sin k theta), k = 0, ..., 8, of the Euclidean plane are distinct, lie on the unit circle and are not Euclidean Ramsey when tan(theta/2) is transcendental; and whenever they are distinct, they are Ramsey if and only if cos theta and sin theta are algebraic (that is, iff e^(i theta) is algebraic), if and only if tan(theta/2) is algebraic. This is an iff for a whole one-parameter family, where earlier explicit examples with a transcendental parameter (OpenAI's Proposition 7.7 and Corollary 7.5) settle single sets: the same nine-point pattern is Ramsey or not exactly as e^(i theta) is algebraic or transcendental. Nine is the exact threshold (eight consecutive multiples are Ramsey for every theta; by hand, in spherical-ramsey), and at theta = e the question becomes whether e^(i e) is algebraic, which appears to be open. Ramsey is OpenAI's definition from result 172 (for every r >= 2 there is D such that every r-colouring of R^D contains a monochromatic congruent copy). The statements are given in OpenAI's vocabulary plus the two-line definition of the nine points, and again with no definitions beyond Mathlib. The non-Ramsey direction mirrors OpenAI's nine-point proof (their Proposition 7.6): the coordinate field is Q(tan(theta/2)), its tensor square embeds in Q(T, U), and the denominator-cleared 9x9 evaluation matrix is nonsingular, certified at (T, U) = (2, 3) by an explicit integer triangular factorization checked by decide +kernel; OpenAI's linear obstruction concludes. The converse uses the theorem that finite spherical sets with algebraic coordinates are Ramsey (prior work of JD-Jones-ASES, Rogerhu12 and atimics; proved again here in Lean on OpenAI's development). The proof builds on OpenAI's complete Lean proof of the classification (openai/math fd4aeeb2), whose 35 files used here are included with header-only changes for the Lean module system. This repository is a module-system port, with no statement or proof line changed apart from a namespace rename, of Lean already public as rope AV3 of spherical-ramsey v1.1.0 (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23396387), packaged so that Theorem D can be checked on its own. All theorems depend on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound only.

records.title: Graham's bounds for list scheduling and LPT on identical machines: 2 − 1/m, 4/3 − 1/(3m) and their tight instances
records.abstract: A Lean 4 development of Graham's two bounds for scheduling independent jobs on identical machines to minimize the makespan (R. L. Graham, Bounds for certain multiprocessing anomalies, Bell System Tech. J. 45 (1966) 1563-1581; Bounds on multiprocessing timing anomalies, SIAM J. Appl. Math. 17 (1969) 416-429; both restated with their examples in his survey Bounds on multiprocessing anomalies and related packing algorithms, AFIPS Spring Joint Computer Conference (1972) 205-217). n jobs of nonnegative real lengths p : Fin n -> R are run without interruption on m >= 1 identical machines; an assignment sigma : Fin n -> Fin m loads machine i with the sum of the lengths assigned to it, its makespan is the largest load, and optMakespan m p is the least makespan over all m^n assignments. A list schedule (IsListSchedule, in the index order) gives each job a machine whose load from the earlier jobs is least, under any tie-breaking (a relation, so every theorem covers every tie-breaking); an LPT schedule (IsLPTSchedule) is a list schedule of the jobs in some nonincreasing order of length. Theorems, kernel-only: every list schedule sigma and every assignment tau satisfy m * C(sigma) <= (2m - 1) * C(tau) (Graham 1966, his Theorem for the same number of processors and no precedence constraints), so C(sigma) <= (2 - 1/m) * optMakespan; the m(m - 1) unit jobs followed by one job of length m (Graham's example for his theorem on scheduling the k largest tasks optimally first, at k = 0, as his 1972 survey restates it; Lenstra-Shmoys, Chapter 9, p. 188) have optimum m and every list schedule of them in that order has makespan 2m - 1, so 2 - 1/m is the least constant (IsLeast); every LPT schedule sigma and every assignment tau satisfy 3m * C(sigma) <= (4m - 1) * C(tau) (Graham 1969, Theorem 2, announced in the closing remarks of the 1966 paper), so C(sigma) <= (4/3 - 1/(3m)) * optMakespan; when every job is longer than a third of C(tau), every LPT schedule is at least as good as tau, so LPT is optimal when every job exceeds a third of the optimum; Graham's 2m + 1 jobs 2m - 1, 2m - 1, 2m - 2, 2m - 2, ..., m + 1, m + 1, m, m, m (his pp. 425-426) are in nonincreasing order, have optimum 3m, attained by a list schedule in the order 2m - 1, ..., m + 1, m, m, 2m - 1, ..., m + 1, m (the definition grahamOrder, a permutation of the jobs whose lengths are that list), and every LPT schedule of them has makespan 4m - 1, for every m >= 1, so 4/3 - 1/(3m) is the least constant (IsLeast); and the elementary facts (list and LPT schedules exist, the optimum is attained, every load, every job and the average load are at most the makespan, relabeling the jobs preserves the makespan); Graham's omega_0, the least finishing time over all lists, equals the optimum over all assignments (every assignment is matched or improved by a list schedule in some order), so the bounds against every assignment are his; for his instance the optimum is attained by an explicit list (grahamOrder); and the third of the optimality theorem cannot be weakened (on three machines 9, 5, 5, 4, 4, 4, each job at least a third of the optimum 12, has an LPT schedule of makespan 13, so n <= 2m jobs do not make LPT optimal; Graham's 1972 survey prints Spencer's 6, 3, 3, 2, 2, 2 for the same purpose); and the position of a job on its machine: the (c + 1)-th job k placed on a machine of a list schedule of a nonincreasing p has (c + 1) p_k <= C(tau) for every assignment tau (the property of Chen 1993, as Della Croce-Scatamacchia 2020 restate it; proved here by an invariant on pairs of machines), hence the Coffman-Sethi form q m C(sigma) <= ((q + 1) m - 1) C(tau) for a machine with q jobs attaining the makespan of an LPT schedule (Coffman-Sethi 1976 as corrected by Chen 1993, as Della Croce-Scatamacchia restate it; the literature states it for q >= 3, for m >= 2 it is weaker than the 4/3 - 1/(3m) bound at q <= 2, and neither its attainment nor Chen's 4/3 - 1/(3(m - 1)) at q = 2 is proved here; Chen's and Coffman-Sethi's papers were not read). The proof of the LPT bound is by counting, not by his exchange argument: with k the job ending a heaviest machine, the average-load bound settles 3 p_k <= C(tau), and otherwise a count of the jobs up to k (every machine of tau holds at most two of them, those at least as long as the least load sit alone, each single-job machine of sigma contributes one) shows that k's machine ends by C(tau). Further: for a job k completing at the makespan of a list schedule of a nonincreasing p, the smaller of C(sigma) and 3 p_k is at most C(tau) for every tau, and C(sigma) <= 3 p_k certifies optimality; equality 3m C(sigma) = (4m - 1) C(tau) on m >= 2 machines forces 3 p_k = C(tau), equal loads before k, every load of tau equal to C(tau) and no positive job after k; Della Croce-Scatamacchia's Proposition 4, q (m - 1) C(sigma) <= ((q + 1)(m - 1) - 1) C(tau) when another machine holds q jobs before k and q + 2 <= m, proved from Chen's property; Dósa's theorem (2004, Theorem 2: Graham's example is the only tight one): every positive multiple of Graham's 2m + 1 jobs in any order attains the bound, and for a nonempty positive instance on m >= 2 machines a list schedule in nonincreasing order, or an LPT schedule in any order, attains 3m C(sigma) = (4m - 1) optMakespan only when the instance is a positive multiple of Graham's jobs, so the inequality is strict for every number of jobs other than 2m + 1; and for every fixed n >= 2m + 1 the constant 4/3 - 1/(3m) is the supremum (IsLUB) of C(sigma)/optMakespan over the LPT schedules of the positive instances with n jobs (the proof approaches it with Graham's jobs followed by small jobs; Dósa's Remark 1 asserts a strict gap for every n != 2m + 1, which can therefore hold at most for n < 2m + 1, not formalized here). Forty-one compared statements over nine fully specified definitions; the finite facts behind every statement are replayed exactly in the standard library by scripts/check_lpt.py. As of 2026-10-11 no kernel-checked proof of the 4/3 - 1/(3m) bound, of either equality family or of the optimality statement was located in the Palomar registry, Mathlib, formal-conjectures, openai/math, anthropics/formal-math, the Isabelle AFP, the Rocq package index, GitHub code search in Lean or arXiv; the AFP's Approximation_Algorithms proves a 3/2 bound for sorted greedy and the factor 2 for greedy, and two Lean repositories prove m * C <= sum p + (m - 1) * p_max over lists of naturals. No priority is claimed.

records.title: Robbins' theorem on strongly connected orientations
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Robbins' theorem: a finite connected simple graph has a strongly connected orientation (a digraph with underlying graph G, never containing both u → v and v → u, in which every vertex reaches every other) if and only if no edge of it is a bridge. As a corollary, every finite 2-edge-connected graph on a nonempty vertex type has a strongly connected orientation. Mathlib has bridges, edge connectivity and digraphs, but not this theorem.

records.title: Normalizers of Γ_Δ(N): the group M_Δ, finiteness, and a coset count
records.abstract: Formal statements and proofs, in Lean 4 with Mathlib, about the normalizers in SL₂(ℝ) of the groups Γ_Δ(N) between Γ₁(N) and Γ₀(N), and the quotients Nor(Γ_Δ(N))/Γ_Δ(N), which are the modular automorphism groups of the curves X_Δ(N) when −1 ∈ Δ, and twice as large otherwise: the matrices allowed by the generalized Newman bound h_Δ form a group M_Δ = D⁻¹Γ₀(n_Δ)⁺D, D = diag(h_Δ, 1), which contains Nor(Γ_Δ(N)) and contains Γ₀(N) with finite index, so Nor(Γ_Δ(N))/Γ_Δ(N) is finite for every Δ; its order is [(ℤ/N)ˣ : Δ] times the number of pairs (σ, H), with σ in a fixed set of representatives of Γ₀(N)\SL₂(ℤ) and H a Hermite normal form, such that σH normalizes Γ_Δ(N); and h_Δ = h(N) except under three explicit conditions on N and Δ. 11 theorems, no sorry, only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

records.title: Lossy Distance-Shell Tomography on Paths: Recovery from Mean and Covariance
records.abstract: A substantive Lean development of two-leg identifiability under independent relay deletion and nearest-surviving-ancestor bypass. An interior path sensor observes anonymous counts at each contracted hop, superimposing both legs. For every known real survival probability strictly between zero and one, the mean and covariance identify the unordered pair of natural-valued leg populations. A sparse interface needs only the covariance diagonal and one adaptively selected column. The concrete law is a finite sum over independent Bernoulli relay masks. Ten selected statements additionally establish mean/fold equivalence, endpoint trace and degenerate-probability semantics, actual-model variance bounds, conditional integer reconstruction recurrences, and a logarithmic randomized-testing lower bound for actual paths of every length at least two. The full finite-sample probability guarantee is not claimed.

records.title: GromovMilman
records.abstract: Formalization of Theorem 1 (the Gromov–Milman conjecture on polynomials restricted to subspaces) from Dol'nikov–Karasev, "Dvoretzky type theorems for multivariate polynomials and sections of convex bodies" (arXiv:1009.0392): for any even d > 0 and any k, there exists n(d, k) such that every homogeneous polynomial of degree d on R^n (n >= n(d, k)) restricts on some k-dimensional subspace V to a scalar multiple of (x_1^2 + ... + x_n^2)^(d/2). The formalization provides an unconditional, constructive proof without sorry or external topological black boxes: Carlsson's theorem on non-abelian 2-groups is eliminated in favor of an elementary abelian Dold-type Borsuk–Ulam theorem ((Z/2)^r) proved from scratch on chain complexes and applied inductively level-by-level to iterated wreath products via block-structured join embeddings.

records.title: Pointwise a.e. convergence of ergodic averages with respect to two commuting transformations in Lean
records.abstract: This is a Lean 4 formalization of the pointwise a.e. convergence theorem for ergodic averages with respect to two commuting transformations. This theorem was proved by GPT 6 Pro when it was instructed to adapt the recent breakthrough on the triangular Hilbert transform made public by OpenAI. The formalization was generated by Claude Opus 5.5 Medium.

records.title: Paracompact expansion and collectionwise separation
records.abstract: Every locally finite indexed family of arbitrary subsets of a paracompact topological space admits a locally finite open expansion with the same index type, without separation assumptions. In a paracompact normal space, a discrete closed family admits a discrete locally finite open expansion whose closures are pairwise disjoint and lie in prescribed open neighborhoods. Consequently every paracompact Hausdorff space is collectionwise normal. Index and ambient types may be empty and have independent universes; the family has unrestricted cardinality. These are classical results; no novelty is claimed.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: Systolic growth in every genus
records.abstract: This repository introduces and formally proves the lower bound 4/3 for the limit inferior of the supremal hyperbolic systole in genus g divided by log g. At present, this formalization is the theorem's only public statement and proof. This metadata records the result as an original proof; the published papers below are cited only as background for ingredients. The proof combines arithmetic hyperbolic surfaces, uniform representations by comparable prime cubes, and surface gluing followed by a smooth conformal change to curvature minus one that preserves the systole lower bound.

records.title: Galvin's theorem, the Dinitz problem and stable matchings
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Galvin's theorem that the list chromatic index of a finite bipartite graph equals its maximum degree (if every edge has a list of at least Δ colours, a proper edge colouring can be chosen from the lists), of its corollary solving the Dinitz problem (an n × n array with lists of n symbols per cell admits a choice with distinct symbols in every row and column), and of the Gale–Shapley theorem on the existence of stable matchings with strict preferences and incomplete acceptability lists, which provides the kernels in Galvin's argument. Mathlib has line graphs and colourings but none of these results.

records.title: Persistent failure of Euclidean quartic SOS exactness
records.abstract: An explicit rational homogeneous cubic with 25 monomials in 14 real variables has maximum one on the Euclidean unit sphere and admits a positive degree-four moment functional with value 500753357629/500000000000. For every positive real regularization parameter, quadratic strength and cubic strength, the associated quartic has an explicitly attained global minimum whose shift is not a sum of squares of real polynomials. A quantitative strict separation bounds every SOS lower bound. The polynomial is stationary at zero with negative definite Hessian. A second explicit 25-term cubic, certified by the same rational functional, gives a unique global minimizer with positive-definite Hessian there and persistent SOS failure for all positive parameters. The exact sphere maximizers are classified. The proof combines an elementary quadratic-map contraction, a rational moment certificate, an ordinary SOS degree bound and an all-parameter radial factorization.

records.title: Hamiltonian s–t paths in solid grid graphs are decidable in polynomial time
records.abstract: A computable algorithm, decideHamPath, that decides whether a solid grid graph (a finite set of lattice points with no holes, with an edge between points at distance 1) has a Hamiltonian path between two given distinct points, with a Lean 4 proof that it is correct. The problem was posed by Itai, Papadimitriou and Szwarcfiter (1982). The algorithm extends Sheffield's height-function algorithm for Hamiltonian cycles: each endpoint gets a phantom edge to a missing neighbour, and an endpoint with all eight neighbours present becomes a hole whose defect (a vortex) is handled by a slit height and a search over flip classes. The registered statement is correctness. The library also proves a polynomial step bound, 5 220 000 (|V| + 3)^6, for cost functions written beside the algorithm, and formalizes the Umans–Lenhart algorithm for Hamiltonian cycles in solid grid graphs.

records.title: A Unified Kalman-Type Classification of Controllability for Linear Stochastic Systems
records.abstract: Formalization of a finite algebraic classification of approximate, approximate null, exact null, and exact controllability for finite-dimensional linear stochastic systems with constant coefficients and independent Brownian drivers. A decreasing subspace sequence gives a common obstruction for the first three properties; exact controllability additionally requires full row rank of the stacked diffusion-control matrix. The development also covers stochastic integration, forward and backward equations, duality, finite rank tests, null feedback, and polynomial small-time energy bounds. The independent Palomar statement and its solution compile with Lean v4.35.0-rc2 and canonical Mathlib. Complete sandboxed mechanical preflight and editorial review are separate requirements; no registration is claimed.

records.title: Survival and transience above the compartment-division threshold
records.abstract: Survival and transience are established throughout the strictly supercritical regime of the noncoagulating compartment model of Anderson, Howells and Rojas La Luz (https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.10223v4, Remark 4.8). Compartments produce molecules at rate b, degrade them at rate d per molecule, exit at rate e, and divide at rate f per molecule, with arbitrary conservative allocation between the daughters. For b,e,f > 0 and d >= 0 with bf > e(e+d), every finite nonempty family has positive probability of eternal survival, with an explicit product lower bound. For positive immigration intensity and any distribution of finite immigrant contents, the process is nonexplosive and the expected total physical occupation time of every compartment-count state has an explicit finite bound. This establishes the transience conjectured in Remark 4.8 without a moment assumption on immigrant contents. The quantitative bounds use a positive eigenweight of the mean system and a bounded multiplicative barrier; a distribution-dependent immigration constant sharpens the uniform occupation bound.

records.title: Omega-bounded Sigma-products and a sharp compactness criterion
records.abstract: For arbitrary T1 omega-bounded factors with an explicit product basepoint, the countable-support Sigma-product is omega-bounded and countably compact. Every countable family is trapped, together with its ambient closure, in a closed compact coordinate box using one countable support. For compact Hausdorff factors, the Sigma-product is compact if and only if only countably many factors contain a point different from the basepoint. Uncountable discrete Boolean Sigma-products are countably compact but not compact. The index and factor universes are independent; the empty index and empty countable subsets are allowed. No first-countability or separability premise is added.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: Exact db2 cascade norms and an optimal uniform constant
records.abstract: Exact supremum-operator norms for the undecimated periodic db2 cascade. For every level j and every period N at least the support, the norm is c_j^d, where c_j = 1651/1395 - (4/63)4^{-j} + (1/180)16^{-j} - (1/1736)32^{-j}. For every positive period, aliasing included, the norm is at most (1651/1395)^d, and that power is the least constant with this uniform role. The free mass is strictly increasing, converges to 1651/1395, and the gap is at most (4/63)4^{-j}. Dimension zero is exactly 1. N at least the support is sufficient, not claimed necessary, and one fixed period is not claimed to attain the limit. At dimension zero the least-constant conclusion is 1 ≤ B; it does not force B = 1. The level-one kernel is the seven-tap half-autocorrelation, with norm (9/8)^d for N >= 7. Levels 1, 2 and 3 remain the exact values (299/256)^d, (9663/8192)^d and (309991/262144)^d for N >= 19, 43 and 91. Bibliographic priority of the closed form is unresolved; see docs/RELATED_WORK.md. A conditional propagation then carries a supplied summary Lipschitz bound and a supplied seminorm comparison through the level-one operator. Bottleneck stability, persistence diagrams and landscape non-expansiveness are hypotheses, not theorems. Those conditional statements are retained in the sources as auxiliaries and are not selected. Nineteen statements are selected. They are parts of this development, not nineteen independent contributions. The exposition of the cascade argument is docs/CASCADE_THEOREM.md.

records.title: Countable cellularity of arbitrary products via finite subproducts
records.abstract: An arbitrary product of topological spaces satisfies the countable chain condition (CCC) whenever every finite subproduct does. For nonempty factors this is an equivalence. The proof includes an indexed uncountable delta-system lemma that permits repeated finite supports, and glues compatible cylinders over a finite common root. Arbitrary products of separable spaces are consequently CCC, without a cardinal bound or separation assumptions and allowing empty factors. Continuous-surjection preservation and the discrete-space countability criterion are proved companions. No unrestricted productivity of CCC factors or productively-CCC theorem is asserted.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: Erdős Problem 111: bipartizing finite subgraphs of uncountably chromatic graphs
records.abstract: A Lean proof that for every real C, a graph whose finite subgraphs on m vertices can each be made bipartite by deleting at most Cm edges has countable chromatic number. Hence h_G(n)/n → ∞ for every graph G that is not countably colorable, in particular for every graph of chromatic number ℵ₁. This answers the second question of Erdős Problem 111 in the affirmative.

records.title: Erdős Problem 173: monochromatic triangles in two-colorings of the plane
records.abstract: A Lean proof that in every two-coloring of the plane any three distinct points that are not the vertices of an equilateral triangle, collinear points included, have a monochromatic congruent copy and at most one equilateral side length is missed, so at most one triangle up to congruence, degenerate or not, has no monochromatic copy. Alternating strips show that one equilateral triangle can be missed. This answers Erdős Problem 173 as Bloom states it and settles the conjecture of Erdős, Graham, Montgomery, Rothschild, Spencer and Straus that every non-equilateral triangle has a monochromatic copy, collinear triples included; it is new to our knowledge. The step from arbitrary to measurable colorings adapts OpenAI's rigidity theorem for wild character laws, extended here from the algebraic numbers to the algebraic closure of ℚ(x) in ℂ for every real x, and its transfer from proper to weak measurable colorings.

records.title: Erdős Problem 408: distribution of iterated totient heights
records.abstract: A Lean proof that the least k with φ_k(n) = 1 has normal order α log n for a constant 1 / log 3 ≤ α ≤ 1 / log 2, with mean-square error O(x (log x)² / (log log x)⁵). This answers the first two questions of Erdős Problem 408. The proof formalizes extensions of Theorems 3.1 and 6.1 of OpenAI's The Poisson-Dirichlet law for prime predecessors, and uses vendored Lean proofs of the zero-free half-plane re s > 7/8 for Dirichlet L-functions (openai/math) and of the weighted dilation graph results (Yao Xu's totient-fibers-lean4).

records.title: Exact fault images in priority controllers
records.abstract: Exact reachable qualifier-set images for a finite priority controller with independent enable and request inputs and a specified first-stage bridge interface. The formal statements characterize detection through arbitrary Boolean qualifier observations, show that nonemptiness cannot be expressed by valid proper-coordinate relations, and classify a specified qualifier-only stuck-at fault. The selector and fault equations are explicit.

records.title: Falconer's distance problem for stretched logarithmic gauges
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of Theorem 1.1 of the supplied October 2026 manuscript: every compact subset of the Euclidean plane with positive Hausdorff measure for the gauge r exp(-(log(1/r))^theta), with 2/3 < theta < 1, has a distance set of positive Lebesgue measure. The proof constructs gauge Frostman probabilities with finite logarithmic critical and Fourier energies, obtains the required radial Orlicz densities, and decomposes the measures into finite-depth regular pieces. Measurable directional tests and smooth masks define actual filtered distance measures with summable removed mass. Quantitative stationary phase, inverse operators, orthogonality, distance linearization, and space splitting prove all four induction recurrences for the actual energies. A weighted finite-tree argument yields summable frequency-shell bounds; Fourier reconstruction gives absolute continuity of a nonzero weighted distance measure and hence the stated positive Lebesgue measure. The target theorem builds without proof holes and uses only the three standard Lean axioms. Source adaptations are recorded under fidelity.
